units.la: IN omnibus obligationibus, in quibus dies non po-nitur, præsenti die debetur.
units.tr: In all obligations in which no day is fixed, it is owed on the present day.
15. Paul, book 4 on Sabinus.

units.la: IS, qui actionem {b}habet ad rem recuperandam, ipsam rem habere videtur{c}.
units.tr: One who has an action to recover a thing is considered to have the thing itself.
16. Ulpian, book 21 on Sabinus.

units.la: Imaginaria venditio non est pretio accedente.
units.tr: An imaginary sale does not take place when a price is added.
17. The same, book 23 on Sabinus.

units.la: Cum tempus in testamento adiicitur: credendum est, pro {e}herede adiectum, nisi alia mens fuerit testatoris: sicuti in stipulationibus promissoris {f}gratia tempus adiicitur.
units.tr: When a time is added in a will, it must be believed that it was added for the heir, unless the testator intended otherwise, just as in stipulations a time is added for the benefit of the promisor.
18. Pomponius, book 6 on Sabinus.

units.la: Quæ legata mortuis nobis ad heredem nostrum transfeunt {h}, eorum commodum per nos his, quorum in potestate sumus, eodem casu adquirimus, aliter atque quod stipulati fuimus. nam & sub condicione stipulantes {i}, omnimodo {k}eis adquirimus, etiam si liberatis {l}nobis potestate domini {m}condicio exstitat.
units.tr: Legacies that pass to our heir when we die: we acquire their benefit through ourselves for those in whose power we are, in the same case, otherwise than what we stipulated. For those who stipulate under a condition, we acquire for them in every way, even if the condition is fulfilled after we have been released from our master's power.
PAUL n.

units.la: SI {o}filiusfamilias sub condicione stipulatus, emancipatus {p}fuerit: deinde exstiterit condicio: patri adquiritur, quo competit: quia in stipulationibus id tempus spectatur, quo contrahimus.
units.tr: If a son under power, having stipulated under a condition, is emancipated, and the condition is then fulfilled, it is acquired for the father, to whom it belongs, because in stipulations the time when we contract is what is considered.
19. Ulpian, book 24 on Sabinus.

units.la: unica §.7. ē.de caducis tollendis. {i} v.l.78. ē.de verb.oblig: l.144: in fine {j}eo: v.l.11.§.1. ē.qui potiores. {k} id est, etiamsi condicio exstat post emancipationem filij. in eo differt legatum à stipulatione. ex hac adquiritur patri, etiamsi condicio exstat post emancipatum filium: ex illa non item. Rationem differentiæ collige ex iis quæ scripsi ad legem 78. ē.de verborum obligat. {l} liberate nobis præstita à dominis,condicio exstat Vulgata. {m} hanc vocem domini Hotomanus expungit 5. observation. 2. in fine.
units.tr: Unica §.7, C. de caducis tollendis. {i} v.l.78, C. de verborum obligationibus; l.144, in fine; {j} v.l.11 §.1, C. qui potiores. {k} That is, even if the condition is fulfilled after the son's emancipation. In this a legacy differs from a stipulation: by the latter it is acquired for the father even if the condition is fulfilled after the son is emancipated; by the former, not. Gather the reason for the difference from what I wrote on law 78, C. de verborum obligationibus. {l} "after freedom has been granted to us by the masters," the condition is fulfilled: the Vulgate reading. {m} Hotomanus deletes the word "masters," 5 Observations 2, at the end.

units.tr: {n} This law is lacking in the Florentine and Haloander editions. {o} l.88, supra de verborum obligationibus. {p} l.15 §., de negotiis.

units.la: Qui cum alio contrahit, vel est, vel debet , sciens non ignarus condicionis eius. Sed vel esse vel autem hoc imputari non potest, cum non fuisse debeat, sponte cum legatariis contrahit. Solet exceptio doli nocere his, quibus voluntas testatoris non refragatur.
units.tr: One who contracts with another either is, or ought to be, aware of that person's condition and is not ignorant of it. But this cannot be imputed to him, since he should not have been ignorant; he contracts voluntarily with the legatees. The exception of fraud usually harms those to whom the testator's will does not object.
20. Pomponius, book 7 on Sabinus.

units.la: Quotiens dubia interpretatio libertatis est, secundum libertatem respondendum erit.
units.tr: Whenever an interpretation of liberty is doubtful, the answer must be given in favour of liberty.

units.la: 21. Vlpianus libro vicesimo septimo ad Sabinum.
units.tr: 21. Ulpian, book 27 on Sabinus.

units.la: Non debet, cui plus licet, quod minus est, non men iusta ignorantia excusat.
units.tr: One to whom the greater is permitted is not bound to do the lesser; and a just ignorance excuses.

units.la: c In iis quae scire possumus et ignorare non debemus, factum nocet l.pen. ff. de Macedoniano: l.48. de fideiussor.
units.tr: c In matters which we can know and ought not to be ignorant of, the deed harms: l. pen., ff. de Macedoniano; l.48, de fideiussoribus.

Hotom.5.obs.8. haec legis verba porrigit ad eos qui vel cotrahedi, vel diftrahedi ius non habent. superioribus, adde illud Senecae, nomina facturi, diligenter in patrimonium, et vasa debitoris inquirimus l. de beneficiis in princip.
units.tr: d That is, of status: whether one is paterfamilias or filiusfamilias, slave or master. Cuiacius 7 Obs. 36; Hotomanus 5 Obs. 8. These words of the law extend to those who have no right to contract or to alienate. To the above add that saying of Seneca: when about to make loans, we carefully inquire into the debtor's patrimony and goods, l. de beneficiis, in principio.

units.la: f haec Sabini sententia est Cuiacius 7.obs.36. Imo non est, Hotom.5.obs.8.

units.tr: i Namely, in paying; and so the word "contract" is used here improperly, for payment is a dissolution, not a contract. Therefore it does not harm the heir if he pays the money ignorant of the condition. Indeed, knowledge does not harm him even if he pays by the testator's mandate, l.14 §.2, quando dies.

Novell. 89, cap. 11.

units.tr: {i} l.5 §.2 §.commodati; l.108 §.12 §.de legatis 1; l.5 §.2 §.commodati; l.14 §.1 §.de furtis; l.1 §.10 at the end and §.ult.; l.2; l.32 §.depositi; l.3 §.1 §.nauta. {l} l.8 §.3 supra de precario. {m} l.8 §.9 §.10; l.6 at the end §.mandati. {n} said §.2, and l.18 supra commodati. {o} said §.2; l.35 §.2 supra de contrah. empt.; l.14 supra de furtis. {p} said §.2; §.ultimo Inst. quibus modis re contrahitur. {q} said §.2; l.1 §.10 §.depositi; l.25 §.7 supra locati; l.20 Cod. de locato. {r} said §.secundo. {s} see l.7 Cod. arbitrium tutelae. {t} by the third law §.9; l.11 supra de negotiis; see l.10 Cod. de negotiis. Diligence {a}, partnership {b} and communion of goods {c} admit both fraud and fault; but this only holds unless something has been agreed expressly, either more or less, in the individual contracts. For what was agreed at the beginning will be observed, since the contract itself makes the law, except for what Celsus holds, that it is not valid if it was agreed that fraud should be answerable; for that is contrary to the judgement of good faith, and so we practise it. But the chances of animals, deaths, and whatever happens without fault, the flight of slaves who are not usually kept under guard, robberies, riots, fires, floods of waters, and attacks of pirates, are answered for by no one.
24. Paul [book 5 on Sabinus.]

units.la: Quatenus cuius {r} interfit, in facto {s}, non in iure {t} consistit.
units.tr: How far a matter concerns someone depends on the fact, not on the law.
25. Pomponius [book 11 on Sabinus.]

units.tr: {g} Fraud may not be owed: this cannot be effected by a pact. l.17 §.3, §. de pactis; l.17 §. commodati; l.2 §.7, §. depositi.

units.la: {s} In facto consistunt, de quibus ex facto iudicium est, potest enim ex eodem facto pro ratione personarum, locorum, temporum l.15.§.de negotijs: l.72.§.de iudicijs: l.16.§.de pœnis. alias pluris alias minoris interesse. interdum ne interesse quidem. ideo nulla iuris definitione id comprehendi potest, Hugo Donellus in libro de eo quod interest c.2.in f. de facti quæstionibus addel. 16.in f. §.de statu: l.79.§.1.§.de iudicijs: l.52.§.2.§.ad l.Aquil: l.13.§.qui posse res: l.8.§.13.§.quibus modis pignus: l.32.§.de vsuris: l.30.in f.§.de statu.tut.
units.tr: s: These things consist in fact, and judgment about them rests on the facts; for from the same fact, according to the circumstances of persons, places and times, the interest may be greater or less, and sometimes there is no interest at all. Therefore no definition of law can comprehend it. See Hugo Donellus, in his book on what is at stake (de eo quod interest), ch. 2, at the end; on questions of fact, Addition 16, at the end; §. On Status; l. 79, §. 1, §. On Judgments; l. 52, §. 2, §. On the Lex Aquilia; l. 13, §. On Those Who Possess Things; l. 8, §. 13, §. On the Modes of Pledge; l. 32, §. On Interest; l. 30, at the end, §. On Status and Guardianship.

units.la: {t} In iure ea consistunt, in quibus cum quid inciderit, constat, quidnam id,aut quale sit. sunt hæc huiusmodi, vt hominum prudentia æstimari & diiudicari possint Donellus ib,
units.tr: t: Those things consist in law, in which, when something arises, it is settled what it is, or what kind it is. They are of such a nature that they can be estimated and judged by human prudence. See Donellus, ibid.

units.la: Plus {*}cautionis in re {b}est, quàm in prae-sona {c}.
units.tr: There is more security in a thing than in a person.
26. Ulpian, book thirty, on Sabinus.

units.la: Qvi potest inuitis {d}alienare, multo magis & ignorantibus & absentibus {e}potest {f}.
units.tr: He who can alienate a thing against the will of others can much more do so when they are ignorant or absent.
27. Pomponius, book sixteen, on Sabinus.

units.la: NEc ex praetorio {g} nec ex sollemni {h} iure priua-torum {i}conuentione quicquam immutandum est, quamuis obligationum causæ pastione {k}possint immutari & ipso {l}iure, & per pasti conuenti exceptionem, quia actionum modus vel lege, vel per praetorem introductus, priuatorum pastionibus non infirmatur {m} nisi {n}tunc, cùm inchoatur {o}actio {p}, inter eos conuenit.
units.tr: Nothing is to be changed either by the praetorian law or by the solemn law through an agreement of private persons; although the causes of obligations may be altered by pacts, and by the law itself, and by the exception of an agreed pact, because the form of actions, whether introduced by law or by the praetor, is not weakened by private pacts, unless the parties have agreed on it when the action is begun.

units.la: In reali, pro-bandum est dominium, quòd est difficile. solue, Plus cautionis est rem habere apud se, quàm contrà alium agere, v. Bellonum 1. sup-[?]tat. 8.
units.tr: In a real action, ownership must be proved, which is difficult. Answer: there is more security in holding the thing oneself than in bringing an action against another; see Bellonus, 1, sup-[?]tat. 8.

units.la: b in rem vulgata Haloand. id est, in pignore §. 4. Inst. de oblig. que ex delicto. in pastis l. 21. in fine s. de pastis, actionibus, quæ id quòd deest personalibus supplent l. 16. §. 3. s. de pignoribus: & priuilegiis realibus l. 3. in fine: l. 4. §. 3. s. de censibus.
units.tr: b: "in rem" in the Vulgate and Haloander, that is, "in pledge" (in pignore): Inst. §. 4, On Obligations arising from Delict. "In pacts": D. l. 21, at the end, On Pacts; actions which make up for what is lacking in personal actions, D. l. 16, §. 3, On Pledges; and real privileges, l. 3, at the end; l. 4, §. 3, On the Census.

units.la: c nisi lex personalium præcisè mentionem faciat l. 7. supra de stipulat. praetor.
units.tr: c: unless the law expressly mentions personal actions; l. 7, supra, On Stipulation; praetorian.

units.la: d Qui difficilius, idem facilius praestare potest l. 4. §. 3. s. de fidei-commiss. liber: adde l. 6. s. de tutor: datis. hinc colligunt neminem cogi ad eum sitandum, quo inuito actus exerceri potest, Decius.
units.tr: d: He who can perform with more difficulty can perform the same thing more easily; l. 4, §. 3, On Liberty Fideicommissa; add l. 6, On Guardians Appointed. From this they infer that no one is to be compelled to accept that by which an act may be exercised against his will, Decius.

units.la: e non debet expectari praesentia quae nihil operatur l. 13. in fine s. ad Velleianum.
units.tr: e: the presence of someone who accomplishes nothing need not be awaited; l. 13, at the end, On the Senatus Consultum Velleianum.

units.la: f nisi ratio fit diuersa, vt in arbitro l. 18. supra de arbitris: & iudicibus, quorum praesentia alios potest in suam sententiam trahere l. 39. supra de re iudicata.
units.tr: f: unless the reason is different, as with an arbiter, l. 18, supra, On Arbiters and Judges, whose presence can draw others to their opinion; l. 39, supra, On Res Judicata.

Codice de testamentis, de iure naturæ, de quo vide leg. 8. s. eo.
units.tr: g: the same holds of public matters, l. 45, at the end, ibid.; l. 38, supra, On Pacts; of the common law, l. 7, §. 16, On Pacts; of the rules of civil law, l. 28, On Pacts; of laws, l. 55, On Legacies; of the right of the commonwealth, l. 2, §. 8, supra, On the Administration of Affairs; of jurisdiction and the form of public law, l. 13, Code, On Wills; of the law of nature, on which see law 8, ibid.

units.la: h solenni vulgata Hal. i 2. Ecloga 1. cap. 27. aliud in consuetudine & statuto, quibus derogari potest iuri publico, qua de re vide quæ scripsi ad legem 9. C. de testamentis.
units.tr: h: "solenni" in the Vulgate and Haloander. i: II Ecloga, 1, ch. 27. Otherwise in custom and statute, by which public law may be set aside; on this matter see what I wrote on law 9, Code, On Wills.

units.tr: m: [ἀξεταλάσσετσι?] Ecloga, ibid.; "informatur" in Hotoman, Illustrations, 35, p. 236.

units.la: n nec si tunc. Græci ita legisse videntur, quam petiturę actioni praetoriæ, vel legali resisti non posse: iam competenti posse vel ante exordium causæ, vel in ingressu iudicij.
units.tr: n: "nec si tunc" (nor if then): the Greeks seem to have read it so, that it cannot be resisted by a praetorian or legal action being sought; yet it can be resisted by a competent exception either before the beginning of the case or at its opening in court.
©: l. 7, §. 5, supra, On Pacts[?].

units.la: ᵠ pastio vulg: past[?] Hugo à Porta.
units.tr: ᵠ: "pactio" in the Vulgate; "past[?]" in Hugo à Porta.
28. Ulpian, book 36 on Sabinus.

units.la: Diuus Pius rescripsit, eos, qui ex liberalitate{4} conueniuntur, in {b}id,quod facere possunt{c}, condemnandos{d}.
units.tr: The deified Pius rescripted that those who are assembled by liberality are to be condemned only to the extent of what they are able to pay. {b} ... {c} ... {d} ...
29. Paul, book 8 on Sabinus.

units.la: Quod initio{e} vitiosum est, non potest tractu temporis conualescere{f}.
units.tr: What is faulty from the beginning cannot be made valid by the passage of time.
30. Ulpian, book 36 on Sabinus.

units.la: Nuptias non concubitus, sed consensus{g} facit.
units.tr: It is not intercourse but consent that makes a marriage.

units.la: {c} Facere posse videntur deducto ære alieno l.19.§.1. supra de re iudicata:& omnibus ita deductis, ne ipsemet donator egeat l.173. infra eodem.
units.tr: {c} They are considered able to pay once debts have been deducted, l.19 §.1 supra de re iudicata; and when all debts are deducted in this way, the donor himself must not be in need, l.173 infra eodem.

units.la: {d} nisi tali priuilegio renunciauit donator, quia donationi (cum habet originem ex contractu) renunciari potest v.Decium hic numero 8.
units.tr: {d} Unless the donor has renounced such a privilege, since a gift (when it arises from a contract) can be renounced; see Decius here, number 8.

units.la: {e} v.l.178. l.201. l.210.§.eo: 2.Ecl.3.c.29: v.l.1.§.de regula Caton: adde l.27.§.de obligat.cap.non formatur 18.de reg.in 6: exemplum erit in sententia l.19.§.de appellationib: institutione l.210 §.eo: testamento aut codicillis v.l.201.§.eo: matrimonio c.1. de desp.imp. in 6: fideicommisso l.2.§.de legat.2: l.1.§.de reg.Caton: stipulatione l.83.§.5.§.de verborum: obligat: adquisitione, laude, liberatione, confessione, electione, Decius hic: possessione ab initio inutili, Iason in leg. Iuste possidet §.de acquir.possess.
units.tr: {e} See l.178, l.201, l.210 §.eo; 2 Ecl. 3, c.29; see l.1 §.de regula Caton; add l.27 §.de obligat.; cap. non formatur 18 de reg. in 6. An example will be in a sentence, l.19 §.de appellationibus; in an institution, l.210 §.eo; in a will or codicils, see l.201 §.eo; in marriage, c.1 de desp. imp. in 6; in a fideicommissum, l.2 §.de legat.2; l.1 §.de reg. Caton; in a stipulation, l.83 §§5 de verborum obligationibus; in obligation, acquisition, praise, liberation, confession, election, Decius here; in possession from an initially useless beginning, Jason on the law "Iuste possidet" §.de acquirenda possessione.

units.la: {f} nisi duo quae sequuntur concurrant, vitij sc. cessatio & nouissimus actus, i.principium ipsius rei vtile sequatur, idque verbis, vel aliis actibus extrinsecus declaratis, ratihabitione aliqua vt in lege 11.§.rusticor: l.vlt. supra comm.prad: l.27. supra de ritu: l.6.C.de nupt: l.24.§.1.supra de legat.1: l.1.§.1. l.7.§.de legatis 3: l.42.§.de heredibus instit: l.20.§.1.§.de condic.instit: l.vnica C.de contractib.iudic: l.1.Cod.si maior facit: quae leges alioquin contrariae essent.
units.tr: {f} Unless the two following things concur: the cessation of the defect and a final act, so that what is useful for the thing itself follows from the beginning; and this by words or by other acts declared outwardly, by some ratification, as in law 11 §.rusticorum; l.ult. supra communi praedio; l.27 supra de ritu nuptiarum; l.6 C. de nuptiis; l.24 §.1 supra de legatis 1; l.1 §.1, l.7 §.de legatis 3; l.42 §.de heredibus instituendis; l.20 §.1 §.de condictione institutione; l.unica C. de contractibus iudicum; l.1 Cod. si maior factus; which laws would otherwise be contrary.

units.la: An solus consensus? ait Iustinianus Nouell. 74.c.4. [illegible, ~14 letters] adde cap.non locum.14: ibi,solo consensu conualescit[?] extra de sponsalib. c. sufficiat[?], ibi,solus secundum leges consensus 22.quaest.2: adde l.4.ibi, nudus consensus 3.de sponsalib.
units.tr: Is consent alone sufficient? Justinian says so in Novella 74, c.4; [illegible]; add cap. non locum 14, where it is said that it is validated by consent alone; cap. sufficiat, where it is said that the consent is lawful by itself; 22 quaest. 2; add l.4, where it says "bare consent", 3 de sponsalibus.

units.la: Hotomanus vero 4. obs.26.negat. ait praeterea requiri deductionem in domum mariti l.5.in f. §.de ritu: adde l.66. in f. §.de donat. inter vir.& vxor. Hanc regulam veram esse ait in muliere domum deducta, nihil aliud hic innues, quam nuptias perfici solo consensu sine tabulis & scriptura l.11.C.de repud. sic sentio, Nuptias per verba, de praesenti contractas, ita esse efficaces, vt secundum matrimonium
units.tr: But Hotomanus, in Observation 4, number 26, denies this. He says moreover that a leading home to the husband's house is also required, l.5 in fine §.de ritu nuptiarum; add l.66 in fine §.de donationibus inter virum et uxorem. He says this rule holds true when the woman has been led into the house; here he means nothing else than that marriage is completed by consent alone, without documents or writing, l.11 C. de repudiis. Thus I think: marriages contracted by words of the present tense are so effective that a second marriage
31. The same, book 42 on Sabinus.

units.la: Verum{a} est, neque pacta{b}, neque stipulationes factum{c} posse tollere. quod enim impossibile{d} est: neque pacto, neque stipulatione potest compre-hendi, ut{e} utilem actionem, aut factum{f} efficere possit.
units.tr: It is true that neither pacts nor stipulations can undo a fact. For what is impossible cannot be comprehended by any pact or stipulation so as to produce a useful action or a fact.
32. The same, book 43 on Sabinus.

units.la: Quod attinet ad ius ciuile{g}, serui pro{h} nullis habetur{i}. non tamen & iure naturali{k}: quia, quod ad ius naturale attinet, omnes homi-nes æquales{l} sunt. net, ea negata vxore quæ per verba de præsenti semel fuerit accepta.
units.tr: As far as civil law is concerned, a slave is regarded as nothing; not, however, under natural law, because as far as natural law is concerned all men are equal. Nor is a wife denied who has once been taken by words of the present tense.

units.la: {a} l. 15. supra de condit. & demonstr: idque euidentissimè probatur lege 8.C.de incestiu, cöcubitum non requiri, video tamen seductionem in domum mariti requisitam fuisse l.6.C.de donat.ante nuptias. {a} reipsa. Fictione tamen mortuus dicitur viuere Instit.de excusat.tut: ut & aliquis bis mori l.51.§.2.s.ad legem Aquil. & duo possidere l.13.§.13.s.de hæredit petit.
units.tr: {a} l.15 supra de condit. et demonstr.; and this is most clearly proved by law 8 C. de incestis nuptiis: that intercourse is not required. I see, however, that leading into the husband's house was required, l.6 C. de donationibus ante nuptias. {a} In fact. Yet by a fiction a dead man is said to live, Instit. de excusatoribus tutorum; and someone may die twice, l.51 §.2 ad legem Aquiliam; and two may possess the same thing, l.13 §.13 de hereditatis petitione.

units.la: {b} huc refer illud Hieronymi Ad Eustoch. Audaćter dicam, cùm omnia possit Deus, sufficare virginem non potest post ruinam {c}.
units.tr: {b} Refer here to that saying of Jerome, To Eustochium: "I will say boldly that, although God can do all things, he cannot restore a virgin after her fall."

units.la: {c} [?]f Paulus 32. quæst.5: adde l.unic. ibi, Castitas corrupta restitui non potest C. de raptu. {d} v.l.12.§.2.s.de captiuis. {d} v.l.31.s.de euicti[?] l.3.s.de condit.& demonst: l.35.s.de verb.oblig.
units.tr: {c} [?] Paul, 32 quaest. 5; add l.unica, where it says "a corrupted chastity cannot be restored", C. de raptu. {d} See l.12 §.2 de captivis. {d} See l.31 de evictionibus; l.3 de conditionibus et demonstrationibus; l.35 de verborum obligationibus.

units.la: {e} Ex eo quod est impossibile vtile factum nasci non potest: si ita est, nec vtilis actio nasci poterit.
units.tr: {e} From the fact that a thing is impossible, a useful deed cannot arise; if that is so, then a useful action also cannot arise.

units.la: {f} pactum Vulgar. sic in manuscripto: & male.
units.tr: {f} "Pactum" in the Vulgate manuscript, so; and wrongly.

units.la: {g} l.41.s.de peculio: l.38.§.7.s.de verb.oblig: & prætorium l.20.§.7.s.qui testam: & extraordinarium l.7.s.de falsis.
units.tr: {g} l.41 de peculio; l.38 §.7 de verborum obligationibus; and the praetorian law, l.20 §.7 qui testamenta facere possunt; and the extraordinary law, l.7 de falsis.

units.la: {h} pro nullis l.1.s.de iure deliberandi: i.nullius iuris habentur l.3.in f.s.de capite minutis: nulla in eos cadit obligatio l.22.s.eo: l.43.in f.s.de verb. oblig: nullùmque arbitrij ius l.68.s.de verb.oblig. Ad solennia testamenti non adhibentur l.20.§.7.s.de testam: tabularii esse non possunt l.3.C.de tabulariis. his adde quæ scripsi ad l.3.in f.s.de capite minutis: & quæ dicam ad l.209.s.eo.
units.tr: {h} "pro nullis": l.1 de iure deliberandi; that is, they are held to have no right, l.3 in fine de capite minutis; no obligation falls upon them, l.22 eodem; l.43 in fine de verborum obligationibus; and no right of arbitration, l.68 de verborum obligationibus. They are not admitted to the solemnities of a will, l.20 §.7 de testamentis; they cannot be record-keepers, l.3 C. de tabulariis. To these add what I have written on l.3 in fine de capite minutis, and what I shall say on l.209 eodem.

units.la: {i} excipe l.4.§.3.s.de edendo: l.53.s.de iudiciis: l.38.§.7.s.de verb.oblig: l.7.s.de falsis.
units.tr: {i} Except: law 4, §3, D. de edendo; law 53, D. de iudiciis; law 38, §7, D. de verborum obligationibus; law 7, D. ad legem Corneliam de falsis.

units.la: {k} ideóque solutum non repetitur l.13.s.de condist.indeb: l.8.s.de solutionibus.
units.tr: {k} Therefore what has been paid is not reclaimed, l.13 de condictione indebiti; l.8 de solutionibus.

units.la: {l} natura est communis seruis l.12.in ff.s.de accusat. Iure naturali omnes sunt liberi Instit. de libertis. hinc seruitutem contra naturam esse dicimus l.4.§.1.supra de statu. Seneca 4. Epist. 31. Quid est eques Romanus aut libertinus, aut seruus? nomina ex ambitione, aut ex iniuria nata.
units.tr: {l} Nature is common to slaves, l.12 in fine de accusationibus; under natural law all are free, Instit. de libertis. Hence we say that slavery is against nature, l.4 §.1 supra de statu hominum. Seneca, Epistle 31, book 4: "What is a Roman knight, or a freedman, or a slave? Names born of ambition or of injury."
33. Pomponius, in book 22 on Sabinus.

units.la: Neo,quod vel is,qui petit,vel is, à quo petitur,lucri a facturus est,durior causa est petitoris b.
units.tr: Nor is the claimant's position harder because either the one who sues or the one against whom suit is brought is going to make a gaina; the claimant's position is harderb.
34. Ulpian, in book 45 on Sabinus.

units.la: Semper c in stipulationibus & in ceteris contrahentibus id sequimur, quod actum d est, aut, si non appareat, quid actu est, erit consequens, ut id e sequamur, quod in regione, in qua actum est, frequentatur. Quid ergo, si neque regionis mos appareat, quia varius fuit? ad id, quod minimum f est, redigenda g summa est.
units.tr: In stipulations and in other contracts we always follow what was agreedc, d, or, if it does not appear what was agreed, it follows that we follow what is customary in the region where the transaction took placee. What then if the custom of the region does not appear, because it varied? The sum must be reduced to what is leastf.
35. The same, in book 48 on Sabinus.

units.la: Nihil tam naturale h est,quàm eo i genere quid-
units.tr: Nothing is so natural as that a thing should be dissolved by the same kind of thing by which it was boundg,

units.la: è contrario melior est possessoris v. l.126. in fine, l.128. l.154. s.eo l. 41. l.48. s. de re iudic. l. 35.
units.tr: on the contrary, the better position belongs to the possessor; see l.126 at the end, l.128, l.154, eo, l.41, l.48, de re iudicata, l.35.

units.la: {c} quoties scilicet constat de voluntate, alias si nullis signis extrinsecis voluntas scripto manifesto contraria declaretur, scriptura stabitur l.19. s. de usu legato: l.112. l. 126. §.2. in fine s. de verborum obligat: l.68.§.1. s.de fideiussoribus: l.ultima C.comm.utriusque iudicij. Est enim scriptura mentis & animi testimonium ac indicium; eam tamen ex communi usu interpretamur l.7. §.2. in fine s. de supellect: aut certo iudicio prudentum l.125.s. de verborum significat. {d} v.l.52.s.de verborum obligat: 2.Ecloga 3.cap.34: quod agitur l.3. s.de rebus creditis. actum opponitur dicto l.6.§.1.s.de contrah.empt. Actum igitur est mens contrahentium ac voluntas l.219.s.de verborum significat: l.ultima C. quae res pignor: res l.41.s.de iure dotium: veritas l.1.l.3. Cod.plus valere quod agit. Quibus indiciis mens colligatur, alibi dicam.
units.tr: {c} whenever it is clear what the will was. Otherwise, if no external signs declare the will, but a manifest writing declares a contrary will, the writing will prevail: l.19 de usu legato; l.112; l.126 §2 at the end, de verborum obligatione; l.68 §1, de fideiussoribus; the last law C. communia utriusque iudicii. For writing is the testimony and indication of the mind and spirit; yet we interpret it according to common usage: l.7 §2 at the end, de supellectile; or by the certain judgment of the learned: l.125, de verborum significatione. {d} see l.52, de verborum obligatione; 2 Ecloga 3, cap. 34. What is done (quod agitur): l.3, de rebus creditis. Actum is opposed to dictum: l.6 §1, de contrahenda emptione. Actum therefore is the mind and will of the contracting parties: l.219, de verborum significatione; the last law C., quae res pignori; res: l.41, de iure dotium; truth: l.1, l.3 C. plus valere quod agitur. By what indications the mind is gathered, I shall say elsewhere.

units.la: {e} id est,consuetudinem regionis sequimur Ecloga ib. v.l.50.in fine supra de legatis 1: adde l.3. in fine s.de testib: l.21.§.1.in fine s. qui testamenta: adde l.37.s.de legibus: l.3.l.7. §.2. in fine s. Jupellect: l.14.§.2.s.de alimentis: l.17.§.1.s.de aqua pluu: & ideo conducere, concedere,contrahere,& quiduis agere,pro more regionis in dubio praesumimur: vide Decium hic. nam sicut natura non separatur à subiecto,ita nec à consueto. Quod est de consuetudine, habetur pro pacto.
units.tr: {e} that is, we follow the custom of the region: Ecloga ib.; see l.50 at the end, supra de legatis 1; add l.3 at the end, de testibus; l.21 §1 at the end, qui testamenta; add l.37, de legibus; l.3; l.7 §2 at the end, de supellectile; l.14 §2, de alimentis; l.17 §1, de aqua pluvia. And therefore, in doubt, we presume that one lets, grants, contracts, and does whatever it is in the manner of the region; see Decius here. For just as nature is not separated from its subject, so neither is it separated from what is customary. What is according to custom is held as a pact.

units.la: {f} Ecloga ib.v.l.9.s.eo. {g} ne alioquin actus pereat,cuius conseruatio quantum fieri potest attenditur l.80.s.de verborum obligat. {h} hoc fallit in matrimoniis v. leg. 8.Cod. de repud: & bonorum possessione l.ultima Cod.qui admissi. {i} id est,eadem fide, alio pacto, altero consensu,aliis verbis v.§.2.Instit.quibus modis tollit. obligat. que {a}dissoluere{b}, quo colligatum est{c}.' ideo verborum obligatio verbis tollitur: nudi consensus obligatio contrario consensu dissoluitur.
units.tr: {f} Ecloga ib.; l.9, eo. {g} lest otherwise the act perish, whose preservation is sought as far as possible: l.80, de verborum obligatione. {h} this does not hold in marriages: see l.8 C. de repudiis; and in possession of goods: last law C. qui admittantur. {i} that is, by the same good faith, by another agreement, another consent, other words: see §2 Institutes, quibus modis tollitur obligatio. What has been bound is dissolved by that by which it was bound. Therefore an obligation of words is dissolved by words; an obligation of bare consent is dissolved by contrary consent.
36. Pomponius, in book 27 on Sabinus.

units.la: Culpa{d} est{e}, immiscere se rei{f} ad se non pertinenti{g}.
units.tr: It is a fault to meddle in a matter that does not pertain to oneself.
37. Ulpian, in book 51 on Sabinus.

units.la: Nemo{h}, qui condemnare{i} potest, absoluere non potest{k}.
units.tr: One who has the power to condemn cannot acquit.
38. Pomponius, in book 29 on Sabinus.

units.la: Sicuti poena{l} ex delicto defuncti heres teneri non debeat: ita nec lucrum{m} facere, si quid ex ea re ad eum{n} peruenisset.
units.tr: Just as an heir ought not to be liable for a penalty arising from the delict of the deceased, so neither should he make a gain if anything from that matter has come to him.
39. The same, in book 32 on Sabinus.

units.la: In omnibus causis pro facto accipitur{o} id, in quo{p} per alium moræ{q} sit, quo minus fiat.
units.tr: In all cases, that is taken as done in which, through another's fault, there is a delay in its being done.

units.la: duobus testibus Decius hic numero 5. d c. non est sine culpa 19. de regulis: in sexto.
units.tr: by two witnesses. Decius here, number 5. d. c. Not without fault, 19 De regulis, in Sexto.
{d} Decius here, no. 5.

units.la: {c} non est sine culpa 19. de regulis: in sexto.
units.tr: {c} Not without fault, 19 De regulis, in Sexto.

units.la: {e} mulieri l. 8. §.1. s.ad legem Aquiliam: artifici l.9. §. 5. l. 13. §. 5. supra locati: obstetrici l.9. supra ad legem Aquiliam: l. 3. §. 2. supra de sicariis: medico l. 6. §. 7. supra de offic.praeses: §. 7. Institut.de leg. Aquil: adsessori l.2.s.quod quisque iur: iudici l.5.§.4. s. de oblig: l.6. s.de vaviis & extraordinar: Institit.de oblig. ex quasi delicto in princip.
units.tr: {e} to a woman: l.8 §1, ad legem Aquiliam; to a craftsman: l.9 §5; l.13 §5, supra locati; to a midwife: l.9, ad legem Aquiliam; l.3 §2, supra de sicariis; to a physician: l.6 §7, supra de officio praesidis; §7 Institutes, de lege Aquilia; to an assessor: l.2, quod quisque iuris; to a judge: l.5 §4, de obligationibus; l.6, de variis et extraordinariis; Institutes, de obligationibus ex quasi delicto, in principio.
{f} that is, in the business.

units.la: {g} id est,cuius est ignarus ac imperitus d.§.1.dilio §. 5: quae est aliena l.19.in fine s.de novationibus: l.4. Cod.de actuarijs: in qua nullum ius habet, aut interesse l.7 l.18. s.de verborum signif.
units.tr: {g} that is, of which one is ignorant and inexperienced: d. §1, dilio §5; which is alien: l.19 at the end, de novationibus; l.4 C. de actuariis; in which he has no right or interest: l.7; l.18, de verborum significatione.

units.la: {h} Cui condemnandi potestas non competit,is absoluere non potest l.6.in fine principij, s.de off.proconsul: & c contra l.3.s.de re iudic.
units.tr: {h} One who has no power of condemning cannot absolve: l.6 at the end of the principle, de officio proconsulis; and contrary, l.3, de re iudicata.
{i} the Vulgate reads: "cannot condemn."

units.la: {k} excipe l.3.§.2.Cod. vbi senatores l 2.Ecloga 3.cap.37: v. l.33. s.de obligat.
units.tr: {k} except l.3 §2 C. ubi senatores; 2 Ecloga 3, cap. 37; see l.33, de obligationibus.

units.la: {m} idem est in pupillo l. 3.§.1. supra de tributoria, vide l.1.l.5.s.de auctor.tutor: Ecclesia & bonae fidei possessore Decius hic.
units.tr: {m} the same holds for a ward: l.3 §1, supra de tributoria; see l.1; l.5, de auctoribus et tutoribus; for the Church, and for a possessor in good faith: Decius here.
{n} why so? see l.155, eo.

units.la: {o} in quo quis alium perhorrescit,quominus fiat vulgat.vt sit sensus, Pro facto haberi, quod fieri propter metum non potuit v.l.22.Cod.de ijs quae propter metum.
units.tr: {o} in which someone so dreads another that he does not do it; the Vulgate reads: so that the sense is: what could not be done because of fear is held as done. See l.22 C. de iis quae propter metum.

units.la: {p} mora est Hal.Si creditor aut actor est in mora,debitor fecisse videtur l.1. §.3.s.de eo per quem: l.17.§.3.s.de vsur: adde c.mora 25.de regul.in 6.
units.tr: {p} delay: Hal. If the creditor or the plaintiff is in delay, the debtor is seen to have acted: l.1 §3, de eo per quem; l.17 §3, de usuris; add c. mora 25, de regulis iuris, in 6.
40. The same, in book 34 on Sabinus.

units.la: FUriosi, vel eius,cui bonis interdictum sit, nulla voluntas est.
units.tr: A madman, or a person under interdiction for prodigality, has no capacity to form a will.
41. Ulpian, in book 26 on the Edict.

units.la: NOn debet actori licere, quod reo non permittitur.
units.tr: What is not permitted to the defendant ought not to be permitted to the plaintiff.

units.la: In re obscura melius est fauere repetitioni, quàm aduentitio lucro.
units.tr: In an unclear matter it is better to favour the one who seeks restitution than the one who seeks an accidental gain.
42. Gaius, in book 9 on the Provincial Edict.

units.la: QUi in alterius locum succedunt, iustam habent causam ignorantiæ, an id, quod petere-tur, deberetur. Fideiussores quoque non dicio, testamento, tutela, & similibus, vide Hotom. 3. observ. 29.
units.tr: Those who succeed into another's place have a just ground of ignorance as to whether what is sought was owed. Sureties too (see Hotomanus, Observ. 3, 29) ... by the same reasoning in the case of a will, guardianship and similar matters.

units.la: {b} masculi vel mulieris l.15.supra de curat.fur. l.1.s. de curat.fur.
units.tr: {b} of a male or a female: see law 15 above, De curatoribus furiosi; law 1 §, De curatoribus furiosi.
{c} that is, of a prodigal.

units.la: {d} à iudice scilicet, idque non perfunctorie, sed vel ex officio, de industria: aut prodigi adgnatis, aut amicis petentibus Decius hic.
units.tr: {d} by the judge, and that not perfunctorily but on his office, deliberately; or for a prodigal, at the request of his agnates or friends. So Decius here.

units.la: {e} in amittendo & alienando l.26.s. de contrah.empt: l.18.supra qui testam: l.12.s. de vsurpat: non in adquirendo l.5. in fine, supra de acquir.hereditat: l.6.s. de verborum obligat: l.3. supra de nouationibus: l.18.s.2.s. de castrensi peculio.
units.tr: {e} in losing and alienating: law 26 §, De contrahenda emptione; law 18 above, Qui testamenta facere possunt; law 12 §, De usurpationibus. Not in acquiring: law 5 at the end above, De acquirenda hereditate; law 6 §, De verborum obligationibus; law 3 above, De novationibus; law 18 §2 §, De castrensi peculio.

units.la: {f} hinc colligit Clarus, Prodigalitate poenam eleuari 5. sent. s. vltimo quaest. 60. numero 6.
units.tr: {f} Hence Clarus concludes that prodigality removes the penalty: Sentences 5, last §, question 60, number 6.
{g} and to the accuser.

units.la: {h} vide l.115. s. eo: cap. non licet 32. de regul. in sext. vbi vide Dinum: adde l.17. l.25. supra de procuratoribus.
units.tr: {h} see law 115 §, De regulis iuris; chapter "Non licet" 32, De regulis iuris in Sexto, where see Dinus; add laws 17 and 25 above, De procuratoribus.

units.la: {i} Nota de argumento à reo ad actorem l.9. §.6. s. de iurciurando.
units.tr: {i} Note the argument from defendant to plaintiff: law 9 §6 §, De iureiurando.

units.la: {k} Magis ei fauetur qui repetit, quàm qui de lucro captando certat. Imò magis fauendum minori qui alienum accepit & dilapidauit, quàm minori suum repetenti l.11. §.6. supra de minoribus. Ea res me mouet vt hic putem non inconcinnè legi, retentioni in l.91. §.3. in fine s. de verborum obligat. 2.Ecloga 3. cap.40: l.33. s. eo: l.14. §.1. s. de religiosis.
units.tr: {k} The one who seeks restitution is more favoured than the one who contends for gain. Indeed a minor who has received what belongs to another and squandered it is to be favoured more than a minor seeking back his own: law 11 §6 above, De minoribus. This matter leads me to think that it is not inappropriately read here "retention" in law 91 §3 at the end, De verborum obligationibus; Ecloga 2, 3, chapter 40; law 33 §, De regulis iuris; law 14 §1 §, De religiosis.

units.la: {l} Alieni facti ignorantia excusat l.11. s. ad Velleianum: l.21. §.1. s. de att.empt: l.vltim. in fine s. pro suo: non proprij ac muneris. hinc illud, Non potest esse pastoris excusatio, si lupus oues comedit & pastor nescit capit. quamuis 10. extra de regul.iuris.
units.tr: {l} Ignorance of another's act excuses: law 11 §, Ad Senatusconsultum Velleianum; law 21 §1 §, De att. emptione; last law at the end, Pro suo; but not of one's own act or office. Hence the saying: there can be no excuse for a shepherd if the wolf eats the sheep and the shepherd takes no notice; chapter 10, Extra, De regulis iuris.

units.la: {m} An venia dignam & immunem à poena? vtique. Imò, non vtique l.9. s. de nautico fanore: l.77. s. de verborum obligat. solue, Non vtique, stricto iure: aliud ex æquo dicimus, adde dicto cap.14. n l.19. s. cod: adde l.49. §.2. s. de verborum obligat: cap. cum quis 14. de regul. in sext. o ea cessat in iis quæ in testamento continentur l.12. s. de transactionibus. p aliud erit, si ipsi petant 7. eo: & l.49. §.2.3. de verb.oblig. q l.59. s. de cond.indeb: vel l.8.§.3. l.29. in princ. & §.2.s. mandati. minus, quàm heredes, iustam ignorantiam possunt allegare. Haec ita de herede dicta sunt, si cum eo agetur: non {a}etiam si agat. nam plane,qui agit,cer-tus esse debet: cùm sit {b}in potestate eius{c}, quan-do velit, experiri: & ante debet rem diligenter ex-plorare,& tunc ad agendum procedere.
units.tr: {m} Is he worthy of pardon and exempt from the penalty? Surely yes. Indeed, not surely: law 9 §, De nautico faenore; law 77 §, De verborum obligationibus, solve; "not surely" under strict law; we say otherwise in equity. Add the cited chapter 14, n; law 19 §, same title; add law 49 §2 §, De verborum obligationibus; chapter "Cum quis" 14, De regulis iuris in Sexto. {o} This ceases in those matters which are contained in a will: law 12 §, De transactionibus. {p} It will be otherwise if they themselves ask: 7, same title; and law 49 §§2–3, De verborum obligationibus. {q} Law 59 §, De condictione indebiti; or law 8 §3, law 29 beginning and §2 §, Mandati. Less than heirs can plead just ignorance. This has been said of the heir if the action is brought against him, not if he brings it. For plainly the one who sues must be certain, since it is in his power to bring suit whenever he wishes; and he ought first to examine the matter carefully, and only then proceed to act.
43. Ulpian, in book 28 on the Edict.

units.la: Nemo ex his,qui negant se debere, prohibetur{d} etiam alia{e} defensione uti,nisi lex impedit.
units.tr: No one who denies that he owes is forbidden to use another defence as well, unless the law prevents it.

units.la: ¶ Quotiens concurrunt plures actiones eiusdem{f} rei nomine,una{g} quis experiri debet{h}.
units.tr: Whenever several actions arise on account of the same thing, one must sue on one of them.
44. The same, in book 29 on the Edict.

units.la: Totiens in heredem damus de eo,quod{i} ad eum pervenit,quotiens ex dolo defuncti convenitur, non quotiens ex suo{k}.
units.tr: We grant an action against the heir for what has come to him whenever he is sued on account of the deceased's fraud, not whenever he is sued on account of his own.
45. The same, in book 30 on the Edict.

units.la: NEque pignus{l}, neque depositum{m}, neque precarium{n}, neque emptio{o}, neque locatio{p} rei{q}
units.tr: Neither a pledge, nor a deposit, nor a precarium, nor a purchase, nor a lease of a thing

units.la: {f} 2. Ecloga 3. cap. 43. nam variarum rerum nomine, varias simul actiones edi posse constat l.11. supra de iurisdict: l.35.§.1.§.locat.
units.tr: {f} Ecloga 2, 3, chapter 43: for it is agreed that several actions may be brought at once on account of various things: law 11, De iurisdictione; law 35 §1, locati.

units.la: {g} In realibus actionibus Hotomanus 27. Illustr.id admittit. arg.l.3.l.5.l.6.l.7. supra de except.rei iudic: in personalibus negat l.130. eodem: l.14.§.2. supra de except.rei iudic: l.60.supra de obligat: vide Hotoman. ib.
units.tr: {g} In real actions Hotomanus 27 Illustr. allows it: see laws 3, 5, 6, 7, De exceptione rei iudicatae; in personal actions he denies it: law 130 of the same title; law 14 §2, De exceptione rei iudicatae; law 60, De obligationibus; see Hotomanus there.

units.la: {h} & potest,non modo post unius actionis damnationem l.93.§.1.supra de legat.3: l.28.§.ultimo §.de liberat. verum etiam post unius victoriam l.10.§.de act.empti: l.18. supra de obligat: interdum eandem instaurare ac referre certis de causis, veluti ob iustum errorem l.13.supra de instit: l.1.§.ultimo §.quando de pecul: l.4.§.ultim. supra quod cum eo: vide Hotomanum ibidem.
units.tr: {h} And one may renew and bring the same action again for certain reasons, not only after the condemnation in one action (law 93 §1, De legatis 3; law 28 last §, De liberatione), but even after winning one: law 10 §, De actionibus empti; law 18, De obligationibus; for example, on account of a just error: law 13, De institutoriis; law 1 last §, De peculio; law 4 last §, Quod cum eo; see Hotomanus there.

units.la: {i} vide l.37. supra eo: l.33.supra de obligat.
units.tr: {i} see law 37, De eo; law 33, De obligationibus.

units.la: {k} l.9 in fine §. de tributoria: 2. Ecloga 3. cap.44. tunc enim in solidum tenetur.
units.tr: {k} law 9 at the end §, De tributoria; Ecloga 2, 3, chapter 44, for then he is held for the whole.

units.la: {l} l. 29. supra de pignorat. act: vide l.30. in fine supra de except. rei iud: adde 2. Ecloga 3. cap.45.
units.tr: {l} law 29, De pignoraticia actione; see law 30 at the end, De exceptione rei iudicatae; add Ecloga 2, 3, chapter 45.
{m} see law 15, De depositi.

units.la: {n} v.l.1.§.11.supra de itinere actuque: l.4.§.3.supra de precario.
units.tr: {n} see law 1 §11, De itinere actuque; law 4 §3, De precario.

units.la: {o} l.16. §.de contrah.empt: v.l.4. Codice de contrahenda emptio.
units.tr: {o} law 16 §, De contrahenda emptione; see law 4, Code, De contrahenda emptione.
{p} see law 20, Code, De locato.

units.la: {q} Proprietatem proprietarius emere non potest, sed possessionem: & e contra, l.28. §.de acquir.possess. [?]sux {a} consistere potest. 1 ¶Priuatorum {b} consuen-tio iuri publico non derogat.
units.tr: {q} An owner cannot buy ownership, but possession; and conversely [text unclear] can subsist. ¶ An agreement between private persons does not derogate from public law.

units.la: 46. Gaius libro decimo ad Edictum Prouinciale.
units.tr: 46. Gaius, in book 10 on the Provincial Edict.

units.la: QVod [?] quoquo {c} pœnæ nomine exactum est, id eidem restituere {d} nemo cogitur.
units.tr: No one is compelled to restore to the same person whatever has been exacted as a penalty [text partly unclear].
47. Ulpian, in book 30 on the Edict.

units.la: COnsilij {e} non fraudulenti {f} nulla obligatio est. cæterum si dolus & calliditas intercessit, de-lo actio competit. 1 ¶Socij mei socius {g}, meus socius non est.
units.tr: There is no obligation arising from an honest counsel that is not fraudulent. But if deceit and trickery were involved, an action of fraud lies. ¶ The associate of my associate is not my associate.
48. Paul, in book 35 on the Edict.

units.la: QVidquid {h} ‖in‖ calore iracundiæ vel fit, vel dicitur {i}: non prius ratum est, quàm si perseueran-tia {k} apparuit iudicium animi fuisse. ideoque breui {l} reuersa vxor, {m} nec diuertisse videtur.
units.tr: Whatever is done or said in the heat of anger is not valid until, by persistence, it appears to have been a settled judgment of the mind. Therefore a wife who returns shortly afterwards is not thought to have divorced.
49. Ulpian, in book 35 on the Edict.

units.la: ALterius {n} circumuentio alij non præbet actionem {o}.
units.tr: The circumventing of one person does not give an action to another.
50. Paul, in book 39 on the Edict.
in the last part, Mandati.

units.tr: {f} For one who acts fraudulently is bound: see law 8, De dolo; law 1 §5, De scriptura corrupta; law 45 §3, De furtis; law 20, Code, De furtis; law 16, De poenis; and if the other would not have acted without our counsel: law 6 §5, Mandati; and Ecloga 2, 3, chapter 47; laws 19 and 20, Pro socio. Say the same of a freedman of a freedman: law 105, De verborum significatione; and of the vassal of my vassal, and the colonus of my colonus (on account, however, of another and not the same estate which he holds from me as vassal). Not so for the friend of my enemy: law 1 §10, De officio praefecti urbi; law 3, De testibus; law 4 §3, De legationibus; see law 28, Code, De inofficioso testamento; nor for the surety of my surety: law 27 §§2–4, De fideiussoribus. {h} [τὶ κατὰ ὁ ζητῶ[?] καὶ ἑπιμὸς[?] τὸ λεγόμενον] Ecloga 2, 3, chapter 48; chapter "Si quis iratus", 2, question 2.

One is free of fault who knows but cannot prevent.
51. Gaius [from book 15 on the Provincial Edict.]

units.la: NOn videtur quisquam id capere, quod ei neces-se est alij restituere {d}.
units.tr: One does not seem to take what he must necessarily restore to another.
52. Ulpian [from book 44 on the Edict.]

units.la: NOn {e}defendere {f}videtur, non {g}tantùm qui latitat {h}, sed & is qui praesens negat {i} se defende-re, aut non vult suscipere actionem.
units.tr: A man does not seem to defend, not only he who hides, but also he who, when present, denies that he will defend, or is unwilling to take up the action.
53. Paul [from book 42 on the Edict.]

units.la: CVius per errorem dati repetitio est, eius confulto {k} dati donatio est {l}.
units.tr: What is given back because of an error is a repayment; what is given knowingly is a gift.

units.la: nitur l.5.Cod.ad legem Iul.maiest. 16. {c}alias colonus l.13.§.7. {d}locati: seruus l.1.§.18.ff.de Silaniano: dominus l.2.§.1.ff.de noxa-lib: l.6.ff.de iure patronatus: qui non prohibet cum prohibere possit, tenetur. est enim specialis ac mutua inter huiusmodi personas connexio. An idem in aliis personis? quidam aiunt voluntatis ac officij magis esse, quàm necessitatis, alteri benefacere l.17.§.3.ff.commodati. sic sentio, Hominis interesse hominem beneficio affici l.7.in fine ff.de feruis exportandis: ideóque eum iuste puniri, qui cum lacertis aut telo armatus agrefto e facile poterat propulsare,& paf-sus est inermem interfici. Seneca in Troade act.2. Non patiar, in me culpa cunctorum redit. Qui non vetat peccare, cum possit, iubet.
units.tr: This rests on Cod. 5, on the Julian law of treason, 16; otherwise a tenant (l.13 §7 locati); a slave (l.1 §18 ff. de Silaniano); a master (l.2 §1 ff. de noxalibus; l.6 ff. de iure patronatus). He who does not forbid when he can forbid is liable, for there is a special and mutual connection between persons of this kind. Is the same true among other persons? Some say that doing good to another is a matter of will and duty rather than of necessity (l.17 §3 commodati). I think this: it is in a man's interest that a man be benefited by kindness (l.7, end, ff. de feris exportandis). Therefore he is justly punished who, armed with a club or a weapon, could easily have driven off an attacker in the field and yet allowed an unarmed man to be killed. Seneca, in the Trojan Women, act 2: "I will not allow it; the fault of all returns upon me. He who does not forbid sin when he can, bids it."

units.la: {d} v.2.Ecloga 3.cap.52: l.49.ff.de donationibus inter vir: l.42.ff.de legat.2: l.16.§.15.ff.ad Trebellianum: l.3.§.4.ff.de legat.praest: l.71.ff.de verborum fignific. multo minus is cepisse videbitur, quia re pe-tenda exceptione remouetur l.13.ff.eo: Idem in eo qui tantum e-rogat, quantum accipit l.122.in fine ff.de leg.1: aut qui alij adminis-trat l.10.in fine ff.de inoffic: aliud erit si ex longo interuallo quis cogatur restituere,& medio tempore vtilitatem perceperit l.49.ff.de donat.inter vir: l.45.l.73.§.4.ff.ad legem Falcid: l.22.§.2.ff.ad Trebell.
units.tr: See 2 Ecloga 3, chap. 52; l.49 ff. de donationibus inter virum et uxorem; l.42 ff. de legatis 2; l.16 §15 ff. ad Trebellianum; l.3 §4 ff. de legatis praestandis; l.71 ff. de verborum significatione. Much less will he seem to have received, because he is kept off by an exception from the thing to be demanded (l.13 ff. eodem). The same holds for one who gives back only as much as he received (l.122, end, ff. de legatis 1), or who administers for another (l.10, end, ff. de inofficioso). It will be otherwise if someone is compelled to restore after a long interval and in the meantime has enjoyed the benefit (l.49 ff. de donat. inter vir.; l.45, l.73 §4 ff. ad legem Falcidiam; l.22 §2 ff. ad Trebellianum).

units.la: {e} Latitare, negare defensionem, nolle suscipere actionem, paria sunt. {f} defendere, quid v.l.35.§.3.ff.de procuratoribus: l.21.in fine ff.ex quibus caus.maior. {g} non tantùm qui praesens negat ff. d.a.n. v. ff. actionem,sed & is qui latitat Faber ad femest.23.& recte. Est enim a verioribus & confessis ad difficiliora progrediendum. {h} Non recte defendit, qui latitat v.l.5.§.3.ff.quib. ex caus.in possess. Quid sit latitare v.l.3.ff.de iudiciis: l.1.l.28.ff.de fideicommiss.libertat. 7.§.4.ff.quibus ex caus.in poss. {i} l.11.§.4.ff.de interrogationibus. {k} Qui dat indebitum per errorem, repetit: qui confultò, donare intelligitur: ideóque non repetit l.1.in f.ff.de condict.indeb: v.l.9.C. de condict.indeb. {l} dummodo alieno nomine non detur l.19.§.1.supra de condict.indeb.
units.tr: To hide, to deny a defence, and to be unwilling to take up an action, are equivalent. For "defend," see l.35 §3 ff. de procuratoribus; l.21, end, ff. ex quibus causis maiores. "Not only he who is present and denies, but also he who hides" (ff. de actione...), as Faber rightly says on the Semestria 23. For one must proceed from the more evident and admitted cases to the more difficult ones. He does not rightly defend who hides (l.5 §3 ff. quibus ex causis in possessionem). For what hiding is, see l.3 ff. de iudiciis; l.1, l.28 ff. de fideicommissariis libertatibus; 7 §4 ff. quibus ex causis in possessionem. l.11 §4 ff. de interrogationibus. He who gives what is not due by mistake reclaims it; he who gives knowingly is understood to make a gift, and so he cannot reclaim it (l.1, end, ff. de condictione indebiti; see l.9 C. de condictione indebiti), provided it is not given in another's name (l.19 §1 supra de condictione indebiti).
54. Ulpian [from book 46 on the Edict.]

units.la: NEmo{a} plus{b} iuris ad alium transferre potest, quàm ipse haberet.
units.tr: No one can transfer to another more right than he himself has.

units.la: NVllus videtur dolo facere, qui suo{c} iure vtitur.

units.la: 56. Idem libro tertio de legatis ad Edictum vrbicum.

units.la: SEmper in dubiis benigniora{d} praeferenda sunt.
units.tr: In doubtful matters the more lenient interpretation is always to be preferred.

units.la: BOna fides non patitur, vt bis{e} idem exigatur.

units.la: EX poenalibus{f} causis non solet{g} in patrem de peculio actio dari{h}.

units.la: {g} & merito: quia concedendo peculium filio, pater praesumitur quidem velle obligari: non tamen ex negotio illicito l.6. §.2. §.de condict. indeb: ideoque pater non tenebitur peculij ratione,bonis filij publicatis l.3. Cod.de bon.proscript. v.Dec.hic numero 3.
units.tr: (g) And rightly so: for in granting a peculium to a son a father is indeed presumed to wish to be bound, but not by an unlawful transaction (l.6 §2 de condictione indebiti). Therefore the father is not bound by reason of the peculium when the son's goods have been confiscated (l.3 Cod. de bonis proscriptorum). See Decius here, number 3.

units.la: Emper qui non prohibet pro se intervenire, mandare creditur. Sed & si quis ratum habuerit, quod gestum & est: obstringitur mandati actione.
units.tr: He who does not forbid another to intervene on his behalf is believed to have commissioned it. But also, if someone ratifies what has been done, he is bound by the action on mandate.
61. The same, from book 3 of Opinions.

Qui praesens patitur suo nomine aliquid fieri, nec id prohibet, mandare videtur l.156. in f.].co: l.1.§.5.s.de exercit: l.6. §.2.l.18.s. mandati: l.2.in f.C.de acquir.possess. e v.l.16.§.1.s.de pignorib: l.12.in f.s.de solutionibus:cap.ratihabitione 10.de regulis in 6. f adgnouerit,comprobarit l.12.§.1.s.ratam rem: verbis vel facto l.5.Cod. ratam rem: intra legitimum tempus l.24.s.ratam rem: sic qui fructus percipit, possessionem: qui censum,contractum: vt & is qui agit ex contractu,ipsum contractu adprobare intelligitur.Ite,qui rationem administrationis exigit, gestionem adprobat. & breuiter, Per ratihabitionem actus attribuitur ratum habenti,Dec.hic numero 10. §id etiam locum habet in delictis l.1.§.11.in f.s.de vi & vi: at non in actu nullo. Actus nullus ratus quidem haberi potest: sed nunquam retrotrahitur, cum tantum valeat ab ipso tempore ratihabitionis v.Dec.hic num.16. h suo nomine sc. non alieno c.ratum 9.de regulis in 6: l.6.§.6.§.9.in f.s.de negot: l.13. s.de preca-ri: ne quidem in meum praeiudicium. excipitur tamen lex 16.§.1. s.de pignorib. i nisi mandatum pro forma a lege vel statuto requiratur: quia tunc non sufficit ratihabitio Dec.hic numero 17. & negotiorum d.§.9. l Et sic aliud est reficere,& ad pristinam formam reducere,aliud de nouo facere l.3.§.15.s.de iuin.actuque pri nato: inste tamen agere possum. Nam si reficiedo officere vicino inuito non licer,multo minus & nouu opus inchoando. m dixi ad l. 55.s.eo:adde 2.Ecl.3.c.60. n Ideo officere non intelligitur,qui iure seruitutis sibi adquisito vtitur,aut citra seruitutem iusto spatio,aut altitudine legitima aedificat.i.qui soli & coeli mensuram seruat l.21.§.2.s.quod vi.
units.tr: Everyone may repair his own property, provided he does not hinder another, against whom he has no right. He who, being present, allows something to be done in his name and does not forbid it, is held to have commissioned it (l.156, end, ff. de regulis iuris; l.1 §5 ff. de exercitoria; l.6 §2, l.18 ff. mandati; l.2, end, C. de acquirenda possessione). (e) See l.16 §1 ff. de pignoribus; l.12, end, ff. de solutionibus; chap. ratihabitione 10 de regulis in 6. (f) If he acknowledges or approves it (l.12 §1 ff. ratam rem habere); by word or deed (l.5 C. ratam rem); within the legal time (l.24 ff. ratam rem habere). So one who takes the fruits is held to have taken possession, and one who collects the rent, to have taken the contract; and one who sues on a contract is understood to approve the contract itself. Likewise, one who demands an account of the administration approves the management. In short, by ratification an act is attributed to the one who ratifies it (Decius here, number 10). (§) This also holds in delicts (l.1 §11 ff. de vi et vi armata), but not for a void act. A void act can indeed be ratified, but it is never carried back, since it has effect only from the very time of ratification (see Decius here, number 16). (h) In his own name, that is, not in another's (chap. ratum 9 de regulis in 6; l.6 §§6, 9, end, ff. de negotiis gestis; l.13 ff. de precario), not even to my prejudice. The exception is l.16 §1 ff. de pignoribus. (i) Unless a mandate in a form prescribed by law or statute is required; for then ratification is not enough (Decius here, number 17; and the said §9 of the Negotia). And so it is one thing to repair and restore to its former form, and another to make anew (l.3 §15 ff. de iure iurando; and the private act). Yet I may rightly bring an action. For if one may not, by repairing, hinder a neighbour against his will, much less may one do so by beginning a new work. (m) I have said this on l.55 eodem; add 2 Ecl. 3, chap. 60. (n) He is not understood to hinder who uses a servitude acquired by right, or who builds at the lawful distance, or at the lawful height; that is, who keeps the measure of ground and sky (l.21 §2 quod vi aut clam).
62. Julian, from book 6 of the Digest.

units.la: HEreditas nihil aliud est, quàm {a}successio in v-niuersum ius quod defunctus habuerit.
units.tr: An inheritance is nothing other than the succession to the whole right which the deceased had.
63. The same, from book 17 of the Digest.

units.la: Vi sine {e}dolo malo ad iudicium prouocat, non cuique succe-di potest, & hæc definitio conflat suo genere & tribus differentiis.
units.tr: One who summons another to court by force, without evil intent, cannot be succeeded by anyone; and this definition is made up of its genus and three differences.
64. The same, from book 29 of the Digest.

units.la: EA, quæ raro {g}accidunt, non {h}temerè[?]insagendis negotiis computantur.
units.tr: Things that happen rarely are not counted when business is being transacted.
65. The same, from book 54 of the Digest.

units.la: EA est natura cauillationis {i}, quàm Græci σοφι-[?] Hal. ... appellant, vt ab euidenter veris per breuissimas mutationes modi-fputatio ad ea, quæ euidenter falsa sunt, perducatur.
units.tr: This is the nature of cavilling, which the Greeks call sophistry, by which a discussion is carried, through the smallest changes, from things that are evidently true to things that are evidently false.

units.la: quàm vniuersum ius quod defunctus habuerit, cuique succedi potest, & hæc definitio conflat suo genere & tribus differentiis. Antequam quis succedat, hæreditas est quasi domina, & vice, locum, ac
units.tr: than the whole right that the deceased had can be succeeded to, and this definition is made up of its own genus and three differentiae. Before anyone succeeds, the inheritance stands as it were in the place of a mistress, and represents the place, the role and the person of the deceased.

units.tr: It is called vacant, lying and vacating with respect to the heir (cf. l. 1 §. 1 §. fi is qui testamen; l. 13 §. 5 in sin. §. quod vi; l. 1 §. de successorio; nullius, l. 13 §. 5 §. quod vi), and once accepted it is joined to the heir (l. 10 §. 12 §. de vulg; l. 59 in fi. §. de adquir. hæreditatem), and it becomes his patrimony (d. §. 2; Socinus ad l. 1 §. 16 §. de adquir. poss.). Accordingly, if a daughter has renounced her father's inheritance, she is not excluded from her brother's inheritance (Dec. hic num. 6). To the authorities above add what Michael Grassus discusses in §. hæreditas quæst. 1 b, as in l. 2 C. ad l. Iul. de vi. From this they infer that an inheritance is not deferred except by right of succession, and that everyone succeeding to the deceased holds the place of heir (cf. l. 128 in fi. §. eo; c l. 14 §. de verb. signific.). [illegible] 2. Eclog. 3. c. 61; cf. l. 9 §. 12 §. de hæred. instit.; add l. 6 §. de except.; l. 11 §. de diuers. & tempor. And so the inheritance of a thing particular is not an inheritance (ex l. 7 §. eo; d l. 50 §. de hær. petit.), e for the inheritance of a living person is not an inheritance (l. 1 §. de hæred. vend.; l. 1 §. pro hærede). f That is, one who provokes justly (l. 21 & 24 §. de vsuris). He is also said to provoke justly who does what is commonly done (l. 16 §. de rei vind.), who is led by a just ignorance of what is not in the law (l. vlt. §. de cond. furt.). g cf. l. 114 §. eo; l. 4 §. & 6 §. de legib.; l. 3 in f. §. fi pars; Nouell. 94 c. 2. h What rarely happens is not under the law. What can happen in particular cases is not taken into account; sometimes, for a just reason, it is counted, as in the case of things that happen by nature, though rarely (l. 12 C. de legitim. hæred.; §. 21 Instit. de rer. diuis.). From this they also infer that a rash plaintiff is not heard (l. 41 §. de fideiussorib.). Likewise, that "rarely" and "never" are not equal. i cf. l. 177 §. de verborum significatione; add l. 88 supra ad l. Fale. [illegible] and subtle. Hence note that excessive subtlety is rejected by law. m Questions of this kind are permitted to judges for discovering the truth (Dec. num. 6). Rather, what he says is pleasing (num. 3): by a subtle reply a malicious question can be repelled, and so the man who in truth repaid a loan can swear with an oath that he had received nothing from the creditor.

units.tr: 68. Paulus, in a single book on the recovery of dowry: In all cases this rule is observed: where the person's condition gives occasion for a benefit, there, if the person fails, the benefit also fails; but where the nature of the action requires it, there, however far the pursuit of it reaches against anyone, the reason for help does not fail.

units.tr: k l. vlt.: defence (d. l. 156); donation (d. §. 2); partnership (l. 26 §. 4 supra de condict. indeb.); adrogation (l. 5 & 24 supra de adopt.). Thus freedom is not given to an unwilling son (otherwise in the case of a slave, l. vlt. C. de testam. manumiss.); see l. 5 C. de emancip.; for the rest see l. 62 supra de verb. oblig. Much less will a man be harmed against his will (l. 25 §. 1 in fi. supra soluto); he will not be dragged out of his house (l. 103 §. eo; l. 18 §. de in ius). So too a woman who has left, and who does not wish to return to her husband, cannot be compelled (l. 7 C. de repud.).

Cod. vbi & apud quos & iis quæ officio iudicis mercenario & iure actionis expediuntur l.1.§.14.s.de vent.in possl.vn.C.qui pro sua iurif. s l.105.s.eo: v.l.9.§.1.s.de off.proconf. g v.l vlt. s. de vsuris. units.tr: Where the guardianship returns, there the inheritance passes, unless women intervene as heirs. 1 No one can appoint a guardian for anyone except for one whom, at his death, he had or would have had among his heirs had he lived. 2 That is held to be done by force which someone does when he is forbidden; that is done in secret which someone does while having, or thinking he has, a dispute. 3 Things written in a will in such a way that they cannot be understood are as if they had not been written. 4 Neither by agreement nor by compromise, nor by a decree (see l.8 §.19 s. de transactionibus; l.1 §.18 s. de separationibus), nor in restitution (l. vlt. Cod. ubi et apud quos), nor in those matters that are dispatched by the office of a judge for a fee, or by the right of action (l.1 §.14 s. de vent. in poss. un. C. qui pro sua iurisdictione; l.105 s. eo; l.9 §.1 s. de off. proconsulis; l. vlt. s. de usuris). He who prevents me from giving my thing in pledge takes from me that benefit; hence the principle that a pact is void by which a creditor is not allowed to sell pledges (l.4 s. de pignoratitia). h "The guardianship returns to where the inheritance comes": Hotomanus so restores it (Obs. 5.26), for guardianship is a consequence of inheritance (l.3 s. de legitimis tutelis; §.1 Inst. de legitima patronorum tutela); Novel 118 c.5 confirms Hotomanus's opinion, and the Greeks (Eclog. 2.3 c.73). i Those things are said to "return" which are assigned by law (l.1 s. de testamentaria tutela; l.1 s. de legitima tutela; Inst. de legitima patronorum tutela in fine; Eclog. 2.3 c.71). Why is it so? (l.65 s. pro socio). l And minors (l. vlt. C. de legitima tutela). m l.1 s. de testamentaria tutela. n §.vlt. Inst. de tutelis. o l.1 §.5 s. quod vi aut clam. p l.3 §.7 s. quod vi aut clam. q l.62 §.1 s. de heredibus. r Eclog. 2.3 c.71; l.38 §.17 s. de verborum obligationibus. Much less can anyone harm another by making a law by his word, nor can anyone give surety for another by stipulation.

units.la: {b}Non debet alteri per alterum iniqua condicio inferri.
units.tr: An unfair condition ought not to be imposed on one person through another.

units.la: In totum omnia, quae animi destinatione agenda sunt, nō nisi vera{f} & certa scientia perfici possunt.
units.tr: All things that are to be done by a determination of the mind can be carried out only with true and certain knowledge.

units.la: & quæ ibi dicam de clausula derogatoria C. de testam. e quoties sc. ex consilio iam obligati sumus, & alteri aut nobis obligatio est quæ-sita: tunc enim totum repudiare aut agnoscere tenemur l.27. §. de procuratoribus: l.11. §. de vsuris: l.16. §. de administ. tut: l.7. in fi. §. de damno: alias, re integra, consilium vt & mentem revocare possumus l.22. §. vlt. §. mandati: vt & in re alternatiuè debita l.21. in f. §. de act. empt: l.14. §. de rer. amot: l.28. §. vlt. §. de liberat: l.8. §. de collat: & prius testamentum l.6. §. 2. §. de iure codicillorum: l.12. §. vlt. §. de leg. 1: l.22. §. de leg. 3.
units.tr: What I shall say here about a derogatory clause (C. de testamentis) is this: whenever we have, by our own decision, already bound ourselves, and an obligation has been sought either for another or for us, we are then bound to reject or accept the whole (l.27 §. de procuratoribus; l.11 §. de usuris; l.16 §. de administratione tutorum; l.7 in fine §. de damno). Otherwise, while the matter is still whole, we may revoke our plan and our intention (l.22 §. vlt. §. mandati); as also in an obligation owed in the alternative (l.21 in fine §. de actionibus empti; l.14 §. de rerum amotione; l.28 §. vlt. §. de liberatione; l.8 §. de collationibus); and a prior will (l.6 §.2 §. de iure codicillorum; l.12 §. vlt. §. de legatis 1; l.22 §. de legatis 3).

units.la: Igitur, in voluntariis consilia in melius mutare possumus. & ita variauit Papinianus l.6. in f. §. de seruis exportandis l. vlt. Cod. de furtis: variauit & Iulianus l.19. in fine, §. ad Velleian: l.1. C. de emend. C: variauit Scævola l.23. in fine, §. de adquir. rer: Mucianus: quin & ipsi Imperatores l.17. ibi, sed & cum Mutiano & aliis amicis nostris iurisperitis adhibitis pleniùs tractaverimus magis vsum est §. de iure patronatus: adde Cuiacius 4. ad Africanum sol. 39. in fine, & 2. obs. 37. Hinc illud, Sano consilio vtitur, qui malum consilium reuocat. f Demum aliquid factum a priuato vel principe ex certa scientia, an id reuocari poterit? vtique. cum huiusmodi clausula nihil operetur in iis quæ apparent ignorata vide l.57. supra de obl. & act: vide Dec. hic num. 7: aliud puto, si quis sciens se non teneri promiserit: videtur enim donasse adde l.25. supra de verborum obligatione: & quæ notaui ad l.vlt. §. pennlt. supra de condit. indeb.
units.tr: Therefore, in voluntary matters we can change our plans for the better. Papinian varied in this way (l.6 in fine §. de servis exportandis; l. vlt. Cod. de furtis); Julian varied too (l.19 in fine, §. ad Velleianum; l.1 C. de emendatione); Scaevola varied (l.23 in fine, §. de acquirendo rerum dominio); Mucianus; indeed the Emperors themselves (l.17, where "but also, with Mucianus and other friends of ours, learned in law, having been consulted, we have treated the matter more fully, it is more customary" §. de iure patronatus). Add Cujas, Afric. 4 sol. 39 in fine, and Obs. 2.37. Hence the saying: he uses sound counsel who revokes a bad counsel. f Finally, if something done by a private person or by a prince was done with certain knowledge, can it be revoked? Certainly. Since such a clause has no effect on matters that appear to have been done in ignorance (see l.57 supra de obligationibus et actionibus; see Dec. here n. 7). I think otherwise if someone promised, knowing that he was not bound; for he is then seen to have made a gift (add l.25 supra de verborum obligatione; and what I noted on l. vlt. §. penult. supra de condictione indebiti).

units.la: Actus legitimi, qui recipiunt diem, vel condicionem, veluti mancipatio{d}, acceptilatio{e}, hereditatis aditio{f}, serui optio{g}, datio{h} tutoris, in totum vitiantur per temporis, vel condicionis adiectionem, nonnumquam tamen actus suprascri-ptionem
units.tr: Legitimate acts that admit a day or a condition, such as mancipation, acceptilation, acceptance of an inheritance, a slave's option, and the appointment of a guardian, are wholly vitiated by the addition of a time or condition. Sometimes, however, it is the superscription of the act that is affected rather than the act itself.

units.la: ait 3. Illustr. sol. 210. si quidem hæ etiam magistratuum communes, omnes ex lege, & inter præsentes tantum fieri solent. In actibus legitimis secus. Cuiacius negat differre 15. obs. 16. {b}An ciuiles & solemnes vt vult Hotomanus? 32. Illust. sol. 219. 220. An a quacunque iuris parte vt Dinus? ad d.c. 50. An per legem inuenti vt Zasius? ad l. dum qui §. Si hominem, num. 3. S. de verb. obligat. An qui mero iure radicantur, vt vult idem Zasius ad l. Cum quid mutuum num. 18. S. de reb. cred. An qui iure finiuntur vt emptio, locatio, societas, mandatū, stipulatio? An qui ex vsu solemnis iuris? Cuiac. 15. obs. 16. in fine, vt sint formulæ rerum à priuatis agedarum, extra rerum contrahendarum negotia à Iurisconsultis inuentæ. Hotoman. ibid. Actum legitimum eadem significatione vsurpari in lege 11. C. de haret: ait Hotomanus 32. Illust. sol. 219: Cuiacius negat 15. observ. 16. in fine.
units.tr: Hotomanus says in 3 Illustr. sol. 210 that these are also common magisterial acts, all done by law and only between persons present. The rule is different for legitimate acts. Cuiacius denies that there is any difference (15 obs. 16). Are they civil and solemn, as Hotomanus holds (32 Illust. sol. 219, 220)? Are they from any part of the law, as Dinus says (on d.c. 50)? Are they found by statute, as Zasius says (on l. dum qui §. Si hominem, n. 3, De verb. oblig.)? Are they rooted in strict law alone, as the same Zasius says (on l. Cum quid mutuum, n. 18, De reb. cred.)? Or are they finished by law, like sale, lease, partnership, mandate and stipulation? Or do they belong to the solemn usage of the law (Cuiacius, 15 obs. 16, at the end), being formulas for carrying out private matters, outside the business of contracting, invented by the jurists (Hotomanus, ibid.)? Hotomanus says that a legitimate act is used in the same sense in law 11, C. De haered. (32 Illust. sol. 219). Cuiacius denies this (15 obs. 16, at the end).

units.la: {c}qui non recipiunt vulg. Hal. Hæc particula, inquit, Hotomanus 32. Illust. sol. 219. suum antecedens restringit, ostenditque quosdam actus legitimos esse, qui diem vel condicionem recipiunt. Acceptilatio & optio non recipiunt. vadimonium comperindinatio, obuagulatio denunciandi testimonij causa, procuratoris datio recipiunt. Cuiacius 15. obs. 16. Florentinam lectionem tuetur. ideoque hæc verba qui recipiunt, ita interpretatur, quibus aperte adiicitur dies vel condicio: alias si tacite adiicitur, non vitiatur. Cuiac. ibi.
units.tr: {c}Those that do not admit (common edition; Hal.). Hotomanus says, 32 Illust. sol. 219, that this clause restricts its antecedent and shows that some legitimate acts do admit a day or condition. Acceptilation and option do not admit one. Vadimonium, comperendinatio, obnuntiatio for the purpose of denouncing testimony, and appointment of a procurator do admit one. Cuiacius (15 obs. 16) defends the Florentine reading and therefore interprets the words "that admit" as meaning those to which a day or condition is openly added; if one is added tacitly, the act is not vitiated (Cuiacius, ibid.).

units.la: {d}emancipatio vulg. Hal. Hotomanus ibi. sol. 214. & 218. vtrúque admittit. Emancipatio actus ciuilis §. 11. Instit. de hæred. quæ ab intest: inter legis actiones numeratur. Paul. 2. sent. 25. §. 4. Cuiacius 15. obs. 16. mancipationem, mancipium dici ait.
units.tr: {d}Emancipation (common edition; Hal.). Hotomanus (ibid., sol. 214 and 218) admits both readings. Emancipation is a civil act (Inst. De hered., §11), counted among the legal actions in the matter of intestacy (Paul, Sent. 2, 25, §4). Cuiacius (15 obs. 16) says it is called mancipation, from mancipium.

units.la: {e}ea per procuratorem fieri non potest. l. 13. §. 10. 10. 3. de acceptilat: v. Hotom. 32. Illust. sol. 120: Cuiac. ibi. in princ: certis verbis fiebat. l. 18. §. de accept: sine die & condicione. l. 4. & 5. §. de accept. & merito, quia acceptilatio obligationi præsentem interitum affert.
units.tr: {e}This could not be done through a procurator (l. 13, §10, D. 10.3, De acceptilat.; see Hotomanus, 32 Illust. sol. 220; Cuiacius, ibid.). At the start it was done with fixed words (l. 18, §, De accept.). It was done without a day or condition (l. 4 and 5, §, De accept.), and rightly so, because acceptilation brings an immediate end to the obligation.

units.la: {f}ea non fiebat per procuratorem. l. 80. §. de adquir. hæred: certis verbis constabat, his puta Adeo, Cernoque, Vlpianus c. 22. §. 18. l. 51. in sin. §. de adquir. hæred. sine die & conditione fiebat. l. 54. §. de adq. hæred: non iterabatur. l. 80. in f. §. de adquir. hæreditas. Hotom. ibi.
units.tr: {f}This was not done through a procurator (l. 80, §, De acquir. haered.). It consisted of fixed words, such as "I accept" and "I take up" (Ulpian, c. 22, §18; l. 51, in fine, §, De acquir. haered.). It was done without a day or condition (l. 54, §, De acq. haered.). It was not repeated (l. 80, in fine, §, De acquir. haered.). See Hotomanus, ibid.

units.la: {g}certis verbis fiebat. l. 20. §. de opt: pure & semel. l. 5. & 8. §. de opt. l. 5. de legat. 1: An per procuratorem fiebat? Hotomanus ib. ait sol. 221, arg. l. pen. §. de opt. quod non admittit Cuiacius 15. obs. 15.
units.tr: {g}It was done with fixed words (l. 20, §, De opt.), purely and once (l. 5 and 8, §, De opt.; l. 5, De legat. 1). Was it done through a procurator? Hotomanus says yes (sol. 221, citing l. pen., §, De opt.), a view Cuiacius does not accept (15 obs. 15).

units.tr: {h}This was done before a magistrate (§1, Inst. De Attil.; l. 6, §1, De tutelis), not by a deceased person (l. 8, §§1 and 2, De testam. tut.). Are there other acts which tacitly admit what is openly included in legitimate acts? Cuiacius (15 obs. 16) adds this. For if it is said that a debt was accepted by one who promised under a condition, acceptilation is understood to have taken effect only if the condition of the obligation has been fulfilled. If the condition is expressly named in the words of the acceptilation, the act is void.
