units.tr: ...in law, and of liberty. Quaestionum. ...giving. Hotomanus on the same passage, 32, Illustr. Quaest., p. 218: ...the judge's award (addictio), ...the pledge of surety (vadimonium), ...denunciation as a witness. Cuiacius disagrees with this in the passage cited. Hotomanus in the same place, p. 218, adds conventio in manum, repudium and divortium. At p. 212 he counts among the legis actiones the appellatio, the summons to court (vocatio in ius), the oath (iusiurandum), and the authority of a guardian; Cuiacius disagrees with this too. Hotomanus also adds adoption, emancipation, manumission by the rod (vindicta), cessio in iure, the joinder of issue (litis contestatio), the transfer of a debt to the defendants, the cession and the renunciation of guardianship, arrogation, satisdation, attestation, mancipation, the nuncupation of a will, the acceptance of an inheritance, and the surrender of a noxal offender. Cuiacius, in the passage cited, also adds some things: stipulation, the appointment of a procurator, and usucapion. Put it this way: by reference to a preceding act or disposition. For a conditional debt can be released by acceptilatio pure, see below, the same title, and l. 12, above, on acceptilatio. Express terms harm; tacit terms do not, because an act of this kind contains a present fact, and so cannot be suspended by a condition or a day. A legal act that cannot be expressly qualified by a condition, if it is deferred to a preceding conditional disposition, can tacitly receive a condition. Not because it does not have something. Balduinus, in his commentary on the Lex Aquilia, (and the Greeks likewise: οὐ πολυπραγμονοῦμεν τί ἐκ[τὸ] ἔσχεν ὁ ἐνάγων [we do not inquire what the plaintiff had not], in Ecloga 3, ch. 76, and Harmenopulus 2, at the beginning) is rebuked by Robertus, 1 Animadv. 15. Cuiacius, 15 Observ. 19 at the beginning, approves both readings, and so does Antonius Mercator, 1 Notar. 15. Certainly I prefer the Greek reading, whose sense is this: what is in the plaintiff's interest is estimated not only by what he has lost, but also by what he could have acquired, so that account is taken of gain as well as of loss. The plaintiff does not properly have what he has lost, and that is a loss. What he could have had but does not have is a gain, and properly not a loss. Therefore the fruits not only already gathered but also those which could have been gathered are included, see law 62 at the end, above on the vindication of property; l. 39 §1, above on legacies; l. 33 at the end of the beginning, above on the Lex Aquilia; l. 22 §3, above on the actions of sale; l. 10 §§19-20, and l. 25 §4, above on what was done in fraud of creditors; l. 13, above...; l. 1 at the end, C. on the petition for inheritance; l. 5, C. on the vindication of property. The plaintiff may have it, but it must be considered what he could not have had through his opponent.

units.la: 79. Idem lib.32. Quæstionum. Fraudis interpretatio semper{a} in iure ciuili non ex euentu dumtaxat, sed ex consilio{b} quoque desideratur.
units.tr: 79. The same, Book 32 of the Questions. In civil law the interpretation of fraud is always required, not only from the outcome but also from the intention.{a}{b}

units.la: 80. Idem lib.33. Quæstionum. In toto iure, generi{c} per speciem{d} derogatur & illud potissimum habetur, quod ad speciem directum est.
units.tr: 80. The same, Book 33 of the Questions. In the whole law the general is derogated by the specific, and what is directed at the specific is especially held to apply.{c}{d}

units.la: 81. Idem lib.3. Responsorum. Quæ vel dubitationis tollendæ causa contradictio inseruntur, ius communi non læduntt.
units.tr: 81. The same, Book 3 of the Responsa. Contradictions introduced to remove doubt do not harm the common law.

units.la: 82. Idem libro nono Responsorum. Donari videtur, quod nullo iure cogente concedtur.
units.tr: 82. The same, Book 9 of the Responsa. That seems to be a gift which is granted without any compelling law.

units.la: 83. Idem libro 2. Definitionum. Non videtur rem amittere, quibus{g} propria non fuit.
units.tr: 83. The same, Book 2 of the Definitions. He does not seem to lose a thing that was not his own.{g}

units.tr: Whoever gives poison is guilty of crime even if it has not harmed anyone. The one whose theft was defeated by a concealed garment (the reading should be this, not "telum," which can be confirmed by law 6, at the end, §, ad l. Iul. peculatus) is no less a robber, for all crimes are complete before the result of the act, as far as the fault requires. The same in Book 4 of the Controversies (7): crimes are punished even though they have not been followed by an outcome (add l. 14, §, De sicariis; l. 18, §, De poenis; Ecloga 2, 3, c. 77; Harmenopulus 6, 2, in princip.). This holds for laws and statutes (l. 15, l. 16, §, De legib.; l. 41, §, De poenis), for legacies (l. 99, in fine, §, De legat. 3), for petitions and sentences (l. 7, §, De except. rei iud.), and for last wills (l. 41, §4, §5, §, De vulg.), for an award, and for rescripts. It does not hold for privileges or the fiscal mandate (see l. 3, C. De commun. fisci deb., lib. 10, tit. 2), and see Dec., here, n. last. Cf. c. Generi 34, De reg. in 6; l. 99, in fine, §, De legat. 3; l. 41, §, De poenis; Harmenopulus 6, 2.{e}{f}{g}{h}{i}{k}{l}{m}{n}{o}

units.la: Cum[?] ampliùs {a}solutum est,quàm debebatur, cuius pars non inuenitur, quæ repeti possit {b}: totum esse indebitum intelligitur,manente pristina obliga-tione. 1 ¶Is natura {c}debet,quem iure {d}gentium dare oportet,cuius fidem {e}secuti fumus.
units.tr: When more has been paid than was owed, and no part of the excess can be found that could be recovered, the whole payment is understood to have been not owed, the earlier obligation remaining. ¶ He owes by nature whom it is proper by the law of nations to give to, and whose good faith we have followed.
85. The same, book 6 of Questions.

units.la: IN[?] ambiguis, pro dubiis {f}respondere melius est.
units.tr: In doubtful matters it is better to answer in the way that favours the doubt.

units.la: 1 ¶Non est nouum, vt, quæ semel vtiliter constituta {g}sunt,durent: licet {h}ille casus exfiterit, a quo initium capere nõ potuerunt.
units.tr: ¶ It is nothing new that things once validly established should endure, even though the case has arisen from which they could not have begun.

units.la: 2 ¶Quotiens æqui-tas {i}desiderij, {k}naturalis ratio {l}, aut dubitatio iu-ris {m}moratur {n}:iustis decretis res temperanda {o}est, quoties res in solutum data dijudi non potest.quia fi indiuiduum est quod diuidi non potest,nec eius pars aliqua esse poterit: ideòque solutione irrita,totum condicitur,& in solidum erit agendum
units.tr: ¶ Whenever equity demands, natural reason requires, or doubt about the law stands in the way, the matter must be moderated by just decisions, whenever a thing given in payment in place of another cannot be judged apart. For if an individual thing is one that cannot be divided, no part of it can be a part of anything else. Therefore, when the payment is void, the whole is recovered by a condictio, and action must be brought for the whole.
l. 1 §. 9, §. ad l. Falcid.; l. 1 §. 21, §. fi quid in fraud. patr.

units.la: {c} Natura debetur, id quod natura æquum est solui l.11.§.2.§.de peculio: cuius obligatio solo vinculo æquitatis sustentatur l.95.§.4.§.solute: quod tamen per iudicem peti non potest l.1.§.17.§.ad l.Falcid:l.10.in f. §.de verbor.significat.
units.tr: {c} That is owed by nature which it is equitable by nature to pay: l. 11 §. 2, §. de peculio; whose obligation is upheld only by the bond of equity: l. 95 §. 4, §. solute; which nevertheless cannot be claimed before a judge: l. 1 §. 17, §. ad l. Falcid.; l. 10 in f., §. de verborum significatione.

units.la: {d} sensus est,Nemo iure gentium debet,quin & natura debeat:nihil iure gentium æquú est,quin & natura quoque fit æquú:at non continuo qui natura debent,iure gentium debet. Ius.n. gentium obligationis actione magis efficace facit,q naturalis.
units.tr: {d} The sense is: no one owes by the law of nations who does not also owe by nature; nothing is equitable by the law of nations which is not also equitable by nature; but not everyone who owes by nature owes by the law of nations. For the law of nations makes an obligation enforceable by a more effective action than natural law does.

units.la: {e} is naturali æquitate obligatur l.1.§.de pactis.
units.tr: {e} He is bound by natural equity: l. 1, §. de pactis.

units.tr: {h} c. factum legitime 73, de reg. in 6; 2 Ecloga 3, c. 84. So, because of a supervening impediment, a marriage is not undone: l. 8 §. de his qui sunt sui; a will: l. 18 §. de his qui testamento facere possunt; l. 1 §. 3, §. secundum tabulas; a hereditary order, the office of judging, a magistracy: l. 1 §. 5, verb. casum, §. de postulando. For it is enough that it was lawful in fact at the beginning; see l. 29 §. eo. So great is the authority of fact that sometimes what is forbidden to be done, once done, holds good: l. 1 §. 5, §. quando appellandum. And so a thing that is useful is not vitiated by what is useless; but what has been begun and not completed, when a useless thing arrives, vanishes: l. 16 §. ad l. Aquil. See Dec. here and Dinus on the aforesaid c. 73.

units.tr: {m} which arises from contrary laws. {n} That is, an impediment preventing the matter from being decided.

units.la: {o} Tèperare, est inter summum, & nimium indulgens ius,medium locum tenere l.17. §.de vsur:vt fit sensus,In omnibus quidem, maxime tamen in iure æquitas spectatur l.89.§.eodi:a.Eclog.3.c.87.
units.tr: {o} To temper is to hold a middle place between a law that is too severe and one that is too indulgent: l. 17 §. de usuris; so that the sense is: In all things, but especially in law, equity is looked to: l. 89 §. eodem; 2 Ecloga 3, c. 87.
86. Idem, book 7 of Questions.

units.la: NOn solet deterior condicio fieri eorum, qui li-tem contestati sunt, quàm si non sed ple-runque melior.
units.tr: The condition of those who have joined issue is not usually made worse, but for the most part better.
87. Idem, book 13 of Questions.

units.la: NEmo enim in persequendo deteriore causam, sed meliorem facit. Denique post litem contestatam heredi quoque prospiceretur, & heres te-netur ex omnibus causis.
units.tr: For no one in pursuing a case makes the cause worse, but better. Indeed, after issue has been joined, provision is made also for the heir, and the heir is bound by all the causes.
88. Scaevola, book 5 of Questions.

units.la: NVlla intelligitur mora ibi fieri, vbi nulla pe-titio est .
units.tr: No delay is understood to occur where there is no demand.
89. Paulus, book 10 of Questions.

units.la: QVamdiu possit valere testamentum, tamdiu le-gitimus non admittitur .
units.tr: As long as a will can stand valid, a legitimate heir is not admitted.
90. Idem, book 14 of Questions.

units.la: IN omnibus quidem, maxime tamen in iure (k, l) quitas spectanda sit.
units.tr: In all things, but especially in law, equity is to be regarded.
91. Idem, book 17 of Questions.

units.la: QVotiens duplici iure defertur alicui suc-cessio: repudiato nouo iure, quod ante defer-nus poena, quia non debetur poena sine mora.
units.tr: Whenever a succession is offered to someone under a double right, and the new right is renounced, the earlier right which was offered remains, because no penalty is owed without delay.
{a} See l. 58 §. de verborum obligationibus; add.
{b} Hotomanus, 3 observ. 28.
{d} l. 52 §. de rei vindicatione.

units.la: Si librarius{b} in transscribendis stipulationis{c} ver-bis errasset{d}: nihil nocere, quo minus & reus, & fideiussor teneatur.
units.tr: If a copyist, in transcribing the words of a stipulation, has made an error, it does no harm to the binding of either the debtor or the surety.

units.la: Filiusfamilias neque{e} retinere, neque recupera-re, neque apisci possessionem rei peculiaris vi-detur{f}.
units.tr: A son under his father's power does not seem to have the right to retain, to recover, or to obtain possession of property of his peculium.

units.la: Non solent, quae abundant{g}, vitiare scripturas.
units.tr: Things that are superfluous do not usually vitiate writings.
92. Scaevola, book 5 of Responsa.
93. Marcianus, book 1 of Fideicommissa.
94. Ulpian, book 2 of Fideicommissa.
95. The same, book 6 of Fideicommissa.

units.la: 1. l.77. S.de acquiren.heredit. solue. Non superest, si repudiata ipsa sit hereditas causa non adiecta, vel si repudiatur unum ex quo aliud necessario dependet, v.qua notavi ad l.77.
units.tr: 1. l. 77, §. de acquirenda hereditate. It does not remain if the inheritance itself is repudiated with no cause added, or if one thing is repudiated on which another necessarily depends. See what I have noted on l. 77.

units.la: {b} l.15.§.1.§. de usufr: l.15.§.5.§.de excusat.tut: l.7.§.5.§.de oper.libert. Horatius de arte 2. Et scriptor si peccat, idem librarius, usque. Quamuis est monitus, venia caret. Librarios Graeci καλλιγραφος[?]: notarios ταχυγραφος, ὁ ξυγραφως[?]. Hi notas, illi literas: ut tabularii rationum supputationem tractabant.
units.tr: {b} l. 15 §. 1, §. de usufructu; l. 15 §. 5, §. de excusationibus tutorum; l. 7 §. 5, §. de operis libertorum. Horace, Ars poetica: "And if a writer errs, the same copyist ... though he has been warned, deserves no pardon." The Greeks call a copyist a calligrapher [καλλιγράφος], and notaries tachygraphers [ταχυγράφος]. The latter wrote shorthand notes, the former letters, just as the clerks of accounts handled the computation.

units.la: {d} citra dolum & falsum, idque in sermone, veluti si scripserit relictum iure restitutionis pro institutionis: mulierem renunciasse Valeriano, pro Veleiano: Titium substitutum procuratorem, pro institutum. In his, notarius commissum errorem corrigere potest, cum talis emendatio neminem laesdat, addit Bartolus, Ei permissum indistionem[?] & diem omissum adiicere, nisi dies esset de substantia instrumenti, ut in hypotheca. Si diem permutauit, talem errorem corrigere non potest, nisi de errore testibus constet. Si instrumentum parti traditum est, requiritur sententia iudicis in errore mutando. Error probari potest authentico, testibus, & partium confessione v.hic Decium.
units.tr: {d} Without fraud or falsehood, and that in the wording: as, for example, if he wrote "relictum iure restitutionis" for "institutionis"; "mulierem renunciasse Valeriano" for "Veleiano"; "Titium substitutum procuratorem" for "institutum." In such cases the notary can correct the error entrusted to him, since such a correction harms no one. Bartolus adds that he is permitted to add an omitted indiction and day, unless the day belonged to the substance of the instrument, as in a mortgage. If he has changed the day, he cannot correct such an error unless the error is attested by witnesses. If the instrument has been handed to a party, a judge's sentence is required for the error to be changed. The error can be proved by an authentic document, by witnesses, and by the confession of the parties. See Decius here.

units.la: {e} i. filiofamilias interdicta ad retinendam, recuperandam, adipiscenda possessione non competit.
units.tr: {e} That is, the interdicts for retaining, recovering, and obtaining possession do not belong to a son under power.

units.la: Nemo dubitat, soluendo videri eum, qui defenditur {a}.
units.tr: No one doubts that he is seen to be solvent who is defended.

units.la: In ambiguis orationibus maximè sententia {b} spectanda ‖est ‖eius {c}, qui eas protulisset.
units.tr: In ambiguous statements, the intention of the one who made them is chiefly to be regarded.

units.la: Ea sola deportationis {d} sententia aufert, quæ ad fiscum {e} peruenient.

units.la: Quotiens utriusque causa lucri ratio vertitur: is præferendus est, cuius {f} in lucrum {g} causa tempore præcedit {h}.
units.tr: Whenever the reason for gain is contested on both sides, he is to be preferred whose cause for the gain comes first in time.
Venuleius, book 12 of Stipulations. 99.

units.la: Non potest improbus videri, qui {i} ignorat, quàtum soluere debeat.

Gaius, book 1 of Rules. 100.

units.la: Omnia, quæ iure contrahuntur, contrario {k} iure pereunt.
units.tr: All things which are contracted by law perish by the contrary law.

And thus one is solvent through another. A person is also solvent who can pay the whole: see l. 114 §. de verborum significatione. units.tr: He who acts against the praetor's prohibition is properly said to have acted against the edict. It belongs to the action to deny it to one who is able also to give.

units.la: SI in duabus actionibus alibi summa maior, alibi infamia {k}est: praeponenda est causa existimationis {m}. Vbi autem aequiparant {n}famosa iudicia, etsi summam imparem habent, pro paribus accipiendi sunt.
units.tr: If in two actions the sum is greater in one and in the other there is infamy, the cause of reputation is to be preferred. But where infamous judgments are equal, even if their sums are unequal, they are to be taken as equal.

units.la: {h} in qua habitat scilicet,non ad tepus Bartolus & Decius hic, quo nomine hortum domui iunctum intelligunt. Eadem ratione volunt molitori molendinum domus esse loco,& nautae nauem. Pelzius in libro de iure sistendi cap.6.numero 3.4.& 5. at non tabernā & apothecam & quae merciū condendarum causa, non habitationis aedificantur. Idem in porticu ab aedibus separata esse, indicat idem Pelzius ibid.
units.tr: {h} In which he lives, that is, not for a time. Bartolus and Decius here, under which name they understand a garden joined to the house. For the same reason they hold that for a miller his mill is his house, and for a sailor his ship. Pelzius, in his book De iure sistendi cap.6, nn.3, 4 and 5. But not a shop, a storehouse, or buildings erected for storing merchandise, which are not built for habitation. The same Pelzius, ibid., indicates that the same applies to a portico separated from the house.

units.la: {i} non potest etiam ibidem arrestari, Pelzius ib.d.numero 3.potest tamen sententia iudicis quis prohiberi ne domum excedat l.7 §.8. §.19.l.9.supra de interdictis & relegatis.
units.tr: {i} He cannot also be arrested in the same place: Pelzius, ib., n.3. Yet by a judge's sentence a person may be forbidden to leave the house: l.7 §.8, §.19; l.9 supra de interdictis et relegatis.

units.la: {k} potest tamen extrahi in criminalibus causis Nouell.134.cap.5. & fiscalibus Pelzius lib.de iure sistendi cap.6.numero 8: sed & quando electus est ad aliquam dignitatem l.31 C.de decurionibus. Quin huic priuilegio renunciari posse volunt,quod ei accidit,qui omni iuris auxilio renunciat, Pelzius ib. numero 9. l l.36.f.de obligationibus: v.l.7.l 97. supra de solutionis: l.10 in fine supra de poenis.

Indeed they hold that this privilege can be renounced, as happens to one who renounces all the help of the law: Pelzius, ib., n.9; l.36 f. de obligationibus; v. l.7, l.97 supra de solutionibus; l.10 in fine supra de poenis.

At is qui quid tenetur nus⁴. [?]
units.tr: In that which is greater there is always contained the lesser, whose estimate is nothing: l.3 §. fin. quadrupes; l.1 §.5; l.ult. in f. §. de his qui deiecerunt; l.2 §.2 §. de lege Rhodia; l.103 §. de verborum obligationibus. Hence Leo, Novel 59, rightly took away from a free man the power of selling himself. Infinite: l.176 in f. 1. eo. Therefore liberty is called the highest price, by the comic poet in the Andria, act 1 scene 1: nothing more pleasing can be granted to a slave. l.39 in f. §. de fideicommissariis libertatibus. Hence he who has acquired a free person has not become richer: l.126 §.1, l.1 eo. And the law favours this greatly: l.20 §. eo; l.22 l. eo. Compare l.22 §. eo; l.6, l.7 §. de iudiciis; v. tit. C. An servus ex suo facto; 2. Ecl. 3 c.105; but see Cujas 9 obs.13. 2. Ecl. 3 c.106; v. l.38 §.7 §. de adulteriis; l.16 §.3 in f. §. de poenis. l.5 §.4 §. de obligationibus; l.ult. §. de variis et extraordinariis criminibus. That the penalty may be remitted: l.8 §. de his qui notantur. Does this mean being outside the cause of the wrong, as my teacher Ramus interprets it: l.50 §. eo; l.1 §. de noxa? Or rather, that one who is willing suffers no injury? l.34 C. de transactionibus. 6 Harm. 2, "although he is able to forbid it"; Δυνάμεως 2 Eclog. 3 c.107. Hence various opinions arise. He who is compelled does not properly sin: l.15 §. de publicanis. He who suffers, although he could repel the injury, cannot complain of the injury: l.34 C. de transactionibus. He who suffers an injury to be done to another, although he could forbid it, is liable: l.45 §. ad l. Aquiliam; l.3 §. de noxalibus; l.24 §.6 §. de damno. l.21 §. eo; l.27 §.7 §. de pactis; l.27 §.7 in f. §. de arbitris; l.9 §. de in litem iurando; l.9 §.3 §. de heredibus Institutionum; l.15 §. de legatis 1; l.3 §.7 §. de adimenda; l.3 §.6 §. de statuliberis; l.1 §.4 §. de verborum obligationibus. Add l.26 §. eo; l.16; l.16; l. eo. Add l.29 §. de heredibus Institutionum. That is, it is contained, so that he who gives more also gives less. But he who is bound to something ...

units.la: ¹ ¶Nerno alienæ rei expromissor idoneus videtur, nisi sit cū satisdatione.
units.tr: No one is regarded as a suitable surety for another's debt unless he gives security (satisdatio).

units.la: ² ¶Pupillus pa- tiens posse non intelligitur.
units.tr: 2 A pupil who is able to suffer is not understood (to be capable of it).

units.la: ³ ¶Vbi verba coniunctiva non sunt: sufficit alterutrum esse factum.
units.tr: 3 Where the words are not conjunctive, it is enough that one of the alternatives has been done.

units.la: ⁴ ¶Mulieribus tunc succurrendum est, cūm defendantur non ut facilius calumnientur.
units.tr: 4 Women are to be helped when they are defended, not so that they may more easily calumniate.
III.

units.la: Gaius libro secundo ad Edictum Provinciale.
units.tr: Gaius, book two on the Provincial Edict.

units.la: PVpillum, qui proximus pubertati fit, capacem esse & furandi, & iniuriæ faciendæ. ¹ ¶In he- quoque, ut fideiussor in maiorem summam datus quam debet principalis, teneatur saltem ratione minoris l. Ostiua, §. 7. supra de fideiussoribus. ut qui decem locare existimet, Titio quinque condicere existimanti, maneat actus in quinque l. 52. §. locati.
units.tr: A pupil who is close to puberty is capable both of theft and of committing injury. Likewise, a guarantor given for a larger sum than the principal debtor owes is bound at least for the smaller sum (law Ostiua, §7, above on guarantors), just as one who thinks he is letting out ten is held to have contracted for five when he thinks he is hiring to Titius for five (law 52, §locati).

units.la: ᵇ aliud est in eo qui causam nudæ absentiæ proponit, præsertim in criminalibus v. l. 13. §.1. §. de publicis iudiciis.
units.tr: It is different for one who puts forward the cause of mere absence, especially in criminal matters (law 13, §1, on public trials).

units.la: ᶜ etiam filius, cūm is nihil possideat l. 93. §. eo. etiam procurator l. 10. §. iudicatum: l. unica C. de satisdat. etiam defensor, quantumuis possessor immobilium & dies Decius ex Bartoli sententia hic num. 2.
units.tr: So too a son, since he possesses nothing (law 93, §eo); also a procurator (law 10, §iudicatum; the single law C. on satisdation); also a defender, however much he may be a possessor of immovables; and Decius, following the opinion of Bartolus, here no. 2.

units.la: ᶠ sensus est, Pupillum in iis quibus patientia inducit consensum non obligari l. 33. §. pro socio ut in l. 4. §. locati scientiam eius non sufficere ad negotiationem l. 3. in f. §. de tributoria, & tamen pati iniuriam potest l. 3. §. 1. §. de iniuriis.
units.tr: The meaning is that a pupil is not bound in those matters in which submission to a transaction induces consent (law 33, §pro socio, as in law 4, §locati). His knowledge does not suffice for a business dealing (law 3, at the end, §de tributoria); yet he can suffer an injury (law 3, §1, de iniuriis).

units.la: ʰ In alternativis sufficit alterum impleri c. in alternativis 70. de regulis in 6: l. 10. in sin. §. de iure delium: l. 5. §. de condict. Instit. l. 13. §. 5. §. de rebus dubiis: l. 78. in f. §. de condict. & demonstrativa: l. 44. §. de obligationibus: l. 129. in sin. §. de verborum obligationibus: l. 13. §. iudicatum solui. In copulativa oratione omnes partes veras esse necesse est d. l. 129: l. 5. §. de condicionib. Instit. l. 13. §. de rebus dubiis.
units.tr: In alternatives it is enough that one of them be performed (c. in alternativis 70, de regulis in 6; law 10, at the end, §de iure deliberandi; law 5, §de condict. Instit.; law 13, §5, §de rebus dubiis; law 78, at the end, §de condict., and demonstrativa; law 44, §de obligationibus; law 129, at the end, §de verborum obligationibus; law 13, §iudicatum solvi). In a conjunctive clause all parts must be true (said law 129; law 5, §de condicionibus Instit.; law 13, §de rebus dubiis).

units.la: ⁱ & minoribus, in quibus malitia supplet ætatem l. 3. Cod. si minor se maiorem dixerit, & quibus denique decipientibus non succurritur l. 2. Cod. si res aliena pignori. mitius tamen mulier delinquens punitur. l. prima, in fine, §. de edendo: l. 2. §. 3: l. 23: l. 30. §. ad Vellejan: l. 18. Cod. ad Vellejan. l. 1. §. de iuris & facti: l. 38. §. 7. §. de adult: l. 1. §. 10. §. ad Turpill: 2. Eclog. cap. 118. §. 5.
units.tr: And to minors, in whom malice supplies age (law 3 Cod., if a minor has called himself of age), and to those who are deceived in such a way that they receive no help (law 2 Cod., if another's property is pledged). A woman who offends, however, is punished more leniently (law prima, at the end, §de edendo; law 2, §3; law 23; law 30, §ad Vellejan.; law 18 Cod. ad Vellejan.; law 1, §de iuris et facti; law 38, §7, §de adulteriis; law 1, §10, §ad Turpill.; 2 Eclog. cap. 118, §5).

units.la: ᵏ defendat vulgat. Haloan. l In delictis proximius pubertati: pro pubere habetur v. l. 23. §. de furtis: 2. Eclog. §. c. 109. : l. 14. §. de Silaniano. At non in testamenti faciendi facultate Decius hic.
units.tr: "Defendat," the Vulgate and Haloander. "In delicts, those closest to puberty": one is held to be pubescent (law 23, §de furtis; 2 Eclog. §c. 109; law 14, §de Silaniano). But not in the power to make a will, says Decius here.

units.la: ᵐ mitius tamen punitur l. 108. §. eo.
units.tr: Yet he is punished more leniently (law 108, §eo).

units.la: ⁿ v. l. 1. §. de privatis delictis: §. 1. Instit. de perpetuis v. ᵒ unicam. C. ex delictis defuncti. sedent non solent actiones transfire, quae poenales sunt ex maleficio: veluti furti , damni iniuriae, vi bonorum raptorum, iniuriarum .
units.tr: See law 1, §de privatis delictis; §1 Instit. de perpetuis; the single law C. ex delictis defuncti. But actions that are penal, arising from a wrong, are not usually transferred: for example, theft, damage, injury, the taking of goods by force, and insults.
112. Paulus, book 8 on the Edict.

units.la: NIhil interest, ipso iure quis actionem non habeat, an per exceptionem infirmetur.
units.tr: It makes no difference whether someone has no action by law or is defeated by an exception.

units.la: 113. Gaius libro tertio ad Edictum Provinciale.
units.tr: 113. Gaius, book three on the Provincial Edict.
The part is also contained in the whole.
114. Paulus, book 9 on the Edict.

units.la: TN obscuris insp ici solet , quod verisimilius est, aut quod plerumque fieri solet.
units.tr: In unclear matters one usually looks at what is more probable, or at what usually happens.

units.la: blicanus. Tenetur etiam heres, ex eo quod ad eum peruenit l. 38. f. eo: l. 5. f. de calum: l.16. f. de dolo & poena defuncto imposita, transmittitur in eius heredes l.3. §.5. f. quod quisque. b aliud in pecuniariis l.22. f. de Silaniano, & conditione furtiva: l.7. §.2. f. de cond. furtiva. c d. §.1. Inst. de perpetuis. d l.23. §.8. f. ad l. Aquil. e l.2. in f. f. vi bonorum. f d §.1. g l.13: §.1 & 66, f. eo: l.7. §.8. f. de dolo l.7. §.14. in f. f. quibus ex causis in possessionem: l.1. §.10. f. ad Turpill. h totum in loco, vt vbique: in tempore, vt semper: in modo, cuius partes sunt accidentales, vt possessio bonae, malae fidei: qualitatis, vt omnis, nullus, quilibet, centum: integrale, cuius partes essentiales integrae, vel homogeneae, vt in aqua, aut heterogeneae, vt partes totius compositi totum quiddam efficiunt, vt aedificium, fundamenta, parietes, & tectum: totum vniuersale, est vel personarum, vt ciuitas, collegium, ducatus, comitatus, regnum, & similia: vel rerum, vt hereditas, domus, grex, equitium, armentum. totum naturale vel artificiale, cui nulla pars naturalis aut artificialis deest. i l.21. f. eo: l.147. f. eo: l.7. f. de except. rei iudicat. c. plus 35: c. in toto 80. de regulis in 6. k quo gradu? voluntas prius spectatur, tum verisimilius, propria deinde verborum significatio. ab hac, id quod minus est. Id si non apparet, actus iudicatur non valere v. Dynum ad c.45. de regulis in 6 num.5. l verisimilius praesumitur c. insticimus 45. de regulis in 6: 2. Eclog.3. c.iii. in dubio, scilicet, & iudicando, & litibus decidendis: quod saepius me faciunt Iurisconsulti, vt docet Tiraquellus in repetitione legis si vnquam 8. C. de reuocand. donat. num. 37. ad 60. Non verisimile, credibile non est, nec attenditur: pro eo non praesumitur: l. 13. f. quod metus: l.19. §.4. f. de peculio: l.6. f. de pignoribus l.41. f. de manumissis testamento. imaginem habet falsitatis. Verisimile ducitur ex more, consuetudine, iis quae fieri solita sunt frequentius, communi opinione, natura, qualitatibus rei, vel personis, tempore, de quibus v. Oldendorp. In Topicis. In loco a conclusione seu praesumptione: sumitur etiam a pietate l.41. §.2. in f. f. de legat. 3: l.102. f. de conditi. & demonstr. l. 30. C. de fideicomm. rerum inter se comparatione l.1.
units.tr: ...the heir is also bound by what came to him (law 38, f. eo; law 5, f. de calumniatoribus; law 16, f. de dolo), and a penalty imposed on the deceased passes to his heirs (law 3, §5, f. quod quisque). b Otherwise in pecuniary matters (law 22, f. de Silaniano, and the condictio furtiva; law 7, §2, f. de condictione furtiva). c Said §1 Inst. de perpetuis. d Law 23, §8, f. ad l. Aquiliam. e Law 2, at the end, f. vi bonorum. f Said §1. g Law 13, §§1 and 66, f. eo; law 7, §8, f. de dolo; law 7, §14, at the end, f. quibus ex causis in possessionem; law 1, §10, f. ad Turpill. h The whole is of place, as everywhere; of time, as always; of mode, whose parts are accidental, as good or bad faith in possession; of quality, as every, none, any, a hundred; integral, whose essential parts are whole, either homogeneous, as in water, or heterogeneous, as the parts of a composite whole that together make a whole thing, as a building, with foundations, walls and roof; the universal whole is either of persons, as a state, a college, a duchy, a county, a kingdom and the like, or of things, as an inheritance, a house, a flock, a herd of horses or cattle; and natural or artificial, to which no natural or artificial part is lacking. i Law 21, f. eo; law 147, f. eo; law 7, f. de exceptione rei iudicatae; c. plus 35; c. in toto 80, de regulis in 6. k By what degree? The intention is considered first, then what is more probable, then the proper meaning of the words. After these, what is less. If this does not appear, the act is judged not to be valid (see Dynus on c. 45, de regulis in 6, no. 5). l What is more probable is presumed (c. Iustinianus 45, de regulis in 6; 2 Eclog. 3, c. 3), in doubtful matters, that is, in judging and in deciding lawsuits; which the jurists often do to us, as Tiraquellus teaches in his repetition of law "Si unquam" 8 C. de revocandis donationibus, no. 37 to 60. What is not probable, not credible, is neither attended to nor presumed in its favour (law 13, f. quod metus; law 19, §4, f. de peculio; law 6, f. de pignoribus; law 41, f. de manumissis testamento). It has the appearance of falsehood. What is probable is drawn from custom, habit, what is usually done more often, common opinion, nature, the qualities of the thing or of the persons, and time, on which see Oldendorp, In Topicis. The topic of conclusion or presumption is also taken from piety (law 41, §2, at the end, f. de legatis 3; law 102, f. de condit. et demonstr.; law 30 Cod. de fideicommissis), from the comparison of things with one another (law 1).
115. The same, {book 10 on the Edict.}

units.la: SI quis obligatione {a} liberatus sit, poterit videri {b} Scepisse. 1 ¶ Non poterit videri accepisse, qui stipulatus, poterit tamen exceptione {c} summoueri.
units.tr: If someone has been freed from an obligation, he may be thought to have received it {a}. 1 He cannot be thought to have received who stipulated, yet he can be repelled by an exception {c}.
116. Ulpian, book 11 on the Edict.

units.la: NIhil consensui tam {d} contrarium est, qui & bonae {e} fidei iudicia sustinet, quàm vis, atque metus: quem comprobare, contra bonos mores est. 1 ¶Non capitur {f}, qui ius publicum sequitur. 2 ¶ Non videntur, qui errant {g} consentire.
units.tr: Nothing is so contrary to consent, which also upholds the judgments of good faith, as force and fear; to approve of these is against good morals. 1 ¶ A person is not caught who follows public law. 2 ¶ Those who are in error are not considered to consent.
117. Paul, book 11 on the Edict.

units.la: PRætor bonorum possessorem {h}, heredis {i} loco in omni causa habet.
units.tr: The praetor treats the possessor of goods, in every case, in the place of an heir.
118. Ulpian, book 12 on the Edict.

units.la: Qui in servitute {k} est, vsucapere {l} non potest. nā, cùm {m} possideatur, possidere non videtur.
units.tr: One who is in servitude cannot acquire by usucapion, for since he is possessed, he is not seen to possess.
119. Idem {book 13 on the Edict.}

units.la: NOn {n} alienat {o}, qui dumtaxat omittit possessionem {p}.
units.tr: He does not alienate who merely lets go of possession.
120. Paul, book 12 on the Edict.

units.la: NEmo plus {q} cōmodi heredi suo relinquit, quàm ipse habuit {r}.
units.tr: No one leaves to his heir more advantage than he himself had.

units.la: nale, & ob aliam causam l.19.s.de liberali v. Decium hic. {b} vox videri, nota est fictionis. Idcòque proprie aliud est dare, aliud remittere l.46.s.de condic.&demonstr. {c} l.13. s.eo: v.l.112. s.ea: l.24.s.de donationib. {d} vis & metus consensui contraria 2. Ecl.3. c.113.6. Harmenop.2. & voluntati l.1.s.quod metus causa. {e} Bonae fidei iudicia consensu sustinentur. {f} l.11.§.4. s.de minorib: v.l. vlt C.de in integrum 2.Eclog.3.c.114. {g} l.15 s.de iurisdict:l.2.s.de iudicijs: l.57: s.de oblig. l.20.s.de aqua pluuia: l.9. C.de iure & facti ignorantia. {h} qui à Græcis hic Ἐπίτροπος appellatur id est, successor 2.Ecl.c.115.
units.tr: ...nale, and for another reason, see l. 19 s. de liberali; see Decius here. {b} The word videri is a mark of fiction. Hence, strictly speaking, to give is one thing and to remit another; see l. 46 s. de condic. et demonstr. {c} See l. 13 s. eo; see l. 112 s. ea; l. 24 s. de donationibus. {d} Force and fear are contrary to consent (2 Eclog. 3, c. 113, 6; Harmenopoulos 2), and to will (l. 1 s. quod metus causa). {e} Judgments of good faith are sustained by consent. {f} See l. 11 §4 s. de minoribus; see l. ult. C. de in integrum restitutione; 2 Eclog. 3, c. 114. {g} See l. 15 s. de iurisdictione; l. 2 s. de iudiciis; l. 57 s. de obligationibus; l. 20 s. de aqua pluvia; l. 9 C. de iuris et facti ignorantia. {h} The one called here by the Greeks Epitropos [Ἐπίτροπος], that is, successor (2 Eclog. c. 115).

units.la: {i} l.25.§.7.s.de acq.hered.v.l.29. §.2.s.de condic.&demonstr.l.2.s.de bon.possessi. {k} & in potestate l.93. s.eo. {l} l.4.§.4.s.de usufrutt:2.Ecl.3.c.116. {m} l.54.supra de acq.ver: l.1. §.6.supra de acq.possess.l.21.supra de adult. {n} 2.Ecl.3.c.117: l.4.§.1. supra de alienatione iudicij : & ideo prohibentur donationes l. 3. §. 10.supra de donat.inter virum, non prohibentur alienationes possessionis l.1.§.4.supra de acquir. possess. {o} proprie scilicet, secus improprie d.l.4.§.2.&l.21.§.2.supra quòd metus. {p} est enim alienatio proprie, dominij l.67.supra de verb.signific. {q} v.l.54.supra eo. l.59:160. in f. l.175. in f.eod.l.20.supra de acq.ver. {r} Cur ita? colige ex lege 67.supra de contrah.empt.2.Ecl.3.c.118.
units.tr: {i} See l. 25 §7 s. de acquirenda hereditate; see l. 29 §2 s. de condic. et demonstr.; l. 2 s. de bonorum possessione. {k} And in power, see l. 93 s. eo. {l} See l. 4 §4 s. de usufructu; 2 Eclog. 3, c. 116. {m} See l. 54 supra de acquirenda vel amittenda possessione; l. 1 §6 supra de acquirenda possessione; l. 21 supra de adultero. {n} 2 Eclog. 3, c. 117; l. 4 §1 supra de alienatione iudicii mutandi causa. Hence gifts are forbidden (l. 3 §10 supra de donationibus inter virum et uxorem), but alienations of possession are not forbidden (l. 1 §4 supra de acquirenda possessione). {o} Properly speaking, that is; otherwise improperly, see d. l. 4 §2 and l. 21 §2 supra quod metus causa. {p} For alienation properly concerns ownership (l. 67 supra de verborum significatione). {q} See l. 54 supra eo; l. 59, l. 160 in fine; l. 175 in fine eod.; l. 20 supra de acquirenda vel amittenda possessione. {r} Why so? Gather it from law 67 supra de contrahenda emptione; 2 Eclog. 3, c. 118.
121. Idem libro 13 on the Edict.

units.la: QVi non facit,quod facere debet: videtur facere aduersus{a} ea,quia{b} non facit.Et qui facit,quod facere non debet: non videtur facere id,quod facere iussus est.
units.tr: One who does not do what he ought to do is seen to act against that very thing, because he does not do it. And one who does what he ought not to do is not seen to do what he was ordered to do.
122. Gaius, book 5 on the Provincial Edict.
Liberty is more favoured than all things.
123. Ulpian, book 14 on the Edict.

units.la: NEmo alieno{d} nomine lege{e} agere potest.
units.tr: No one can sue by law in another's name.

units.la: I ¶Temporaria{f} permutatio ius prouinciæ non innouat.
units.tr: 1 ¶ A temporary exchange does not alter the law of the province.
124. Paul, book 16 on the Edict.

units.la: VBI{h} non voce,sed praesentia{i} opus est: mutus,si intellectum habet,potest videri respondere. Idem in surdo.hic quidem ||&|| respondere potest. 1 ¶Furiosus absentis {x}loco est l. & ita Pomponius libro primo epistolarum scribit.
units.tr: Where presence rather than voice is needed, a mute who has understanding may be seen to answer. The same applies to a deaf man, who indeed can also answer. 1 ¶ A madman is in the place of one who is absent. And so Pomponius writes in book 1 of the Letters.
125. Gaius, book 5 on the Provincial Edict.

units.la: FAuorabiliores rei{m} potius, quàm actores, habentur{n}.
units.tr: Defendants are regarded as more favoured than plaintiffs.
If the usufruct is sought. [?]

units.la: {e} lege agere, est in iure agere ex formulis a lege institutis, ex praescripto legis, impetratis solemniter actionibus, apud magistratum experiri. hinc legis actiones, formulae agendi in iure apud eum, qui iuri dicundo praeest l.4.§. de adopt.l.3.§.de off.proconf.l.1.§.de officio iudicis Paul.2.sent.25.§.4.
units.tr: {e} To sue by law is to proceed in court, under the forms established by law, according to the prescription of the law, by actions duly obtained, before the magistrate. Hence the legal actions are the forms of pleading in court before the one who presides over the administration of justice; see l. 4 §... de adoptionibus; l. 3 §... de officio proconsulis; l. 1 §... de officio iudicis; Paul, Sentences 2, 25 §4.

units.la: {f} Temporalis vulgata sensus est, Momentanea imperium non habent in ea quae iuris sunt: ideoque consuetudo duobus, aut tribus iudicijs contrariis non euertitur Decius.
units.tr: {f} The common sense of temporaria is that momentary things have no power over matters of law; therefore custom is not overturned by two or three contrary judgments. Decius.
{g} Book 17. Peter Faber, here.
{h} See l. 48 §... de obligationibus.

units.la: {i} id est, praesentis cosenfu & intelligentia l.209.§.de verb.sign.
units.tr: {i} That is, of present consent and understanding; see l. 209 §... de verborum significatione.

units.la: {k} v.l.2.§.3.§.de iure Codicill.l.17. §.11.in f. §. de iniurijs. Idem corpore praesens esse potest, mente absens l.26.§.de captiuis.
units.tr: {k} See l. 2 §3 §... de iure codicillorum; l. 17 §11 in fine §... de iniuriis. One may be present in body and absent in mind; see l. 26 §... de captivis.
{l} Indeed he is not; see l. 2 §1 §... de procuratoribus.

units.la: {m} l.41.§.en.l.38.§.de re iudic.l.47.§.de oblig.c.cum sint paria iura ii. de regulis in 6: 2.Ecl.3.c.112: adde Aristotelem Problemat.18. id est propriores fumus ad reum absoluendum d.l.47. l.5. in prin.§. de poenis: l.4. §.13.§.de doli except. fauetur possidenti v.l.128. §.e. plus etiam dilationis reo datur l.vlt.§.de feruis.l.6.inf.C de temporibus in integrum:l.2.C.de dilationib.
units.tr: {m} See l. 41 §... and l. 38 §... de re iudicata; l. 47 §... de obligationibus; c. cum sint paria iura, ii, de regulis iuris in 6; 2 Eclog. 3, c. 112. Add Aristotle, Problems 18: that is, we are more inclined to acquit the accused (d. l. 47; l. 5 in principio §... de poenis; l. 4 §13 §... de doli exceptione). The possessor is favoured (see l. 128 §... ). More delay is also granted to the defendant (l. ult. §... de servis; l. 6 in fine C. de temporibus in integrum restitutione; l. 2 C. de dilationibus).

units.la: {n} in causae decisione, non tamen in praeparatoriis iudiciorum l.8.§.qui satisdare: l.66.§.de iudi-
units.tr: {n} In deciding the case, but not in preparatory proceedings of the judgments; see l. 8 §... qui satisdare; l. 66 §... de iudiciis.
126. Ulpian, book 15 on the Edict.

units.la: Nemo prædo est est,qui pretium numeravit[?] ¶ Locupletior non est factus,qui libertum adquisierit. 2 ¶ Cùm de lucro duorum quæratur:melior est causa possidentis.
units.tr: No one is a robber who has paid the price. He who has acquired a freedman has not been made richer. 2 ¶ When the gain of two parties is in question, the cause of the possessor is the better.
127. Paul, book 20 on the Edict.

units.la: Cùm prætor in heredem dat actionem, quatenus ad eum peruenit:sufficit,si vel momento ad eum peruenit ex dolo defuncti.
units.tr: When the praetor gives an action against an heir, insofar as the property has come to him, it is enough if it has come to him even for a moment through the fraud of the deceased.
128. The same, book nineteen on the Edict.

units.la: In pari causa possessor i potior haberi debet. ¶ Hi,qui in vniuersum ius succedunt,heredis loco habentur.
units.tr: In an equal case the possessor ought to be preferred. ¶ Those who succeed to the whole right are held in the place of heir.

units.la: Malæ fidei possessor {a}[?] tamen fidei positus. {b}Ecl.ib.etiam sciens l.13.§.8.5.de haereditatis petit. 2. Harmenopul. 1. circa sin. præsertim authore iudice Harmenopul. ibi. Imo tunc videtur malæ fidei possessor: nam qui sciens contra iura mercatur (qualis is est, qui rem alienam sciens emit) bonam fidem non præsumitur habere {c}qui contra 82. de regulis iuris. {c}est tamen prædo, qui rem venditam propria auctoritate capit l.5.§.de acquiren. possess. {d}qui liberum Vulgat. Heloan: adde l.63. in sin. principii. §. ad legem Falcidiam. {e}vel qui donat l.25.§.11.§.de haered.petit. {f}v.l.128.§.eo. {g}l.16. §. quod metus causa. {h}momento aliquid fieri sufficit, ut factum fuisse dicatur & semel l.17. supra quod metus causa. 2.Eclog.3.c.129. In momento est. v.l.79. supra de acquir.haered. In articulo l. ultima, C. de offic. comitis sacri palatii. de momento dicam ad l.vlt.in sin. C. de bonis quæ liberis. {i}c.in pari 65. de regulis in 6.l.126. in fine, supra eo: l.5.§.1. supra de calumniatoribus l.9.§.4. supra de publicianâ: v.l.5. in fine, princip. supra.§.vsufructus petatur: l.8. in fine, supra de conditionibus. ob turpem: l.10. supra de pignoribus: l.36.§.3. in fine, supra de testamentis. militar: l.1.§. vti possidetis: §.4. verb. commodum insit. de interdictis: v.l.2.C. de conditione ob turpem: 2. Eclog.3.cap.125:2.Harmenop.1. circa finem. vt fiscus is enim heredis loco habetur l.3.§.solutio l.2.C. ad l. Iul.de vi: l.4.£.de bon.præscrip. ] l.60.§.1.l.194.§.eo: l.9.§.11.§.de haer.inst.2.Ecl.3.c.126.
units.tr: A possessor in bad faith is nevertheless placed in the position of good faith. {b}Ecl. ib., also knowing, l.13 §8 §5 de haereditatis petitione. 2 Harmenopulus 1, near the end; especially on the authority of the judge Harmenopulus there: "Indeed, then he seems to be a possessor in bad faith. For one who knowingly trades contrary to law (such is one who knowingly buys another's property) is not presumed to have good faith," {c}contrary to 82 de regulis iuris. {c}Yet he is a robber (praedo) who takes a thing sold on his own authority, l.5 §. de acquirenda possessione. {d}who treats it as free; Vulgate, Heloan; add l.63 at the end of the opening part, §. ad legem Falcidiam. {e}or who gives it away, l.25 §11 §. de haereditatis petitione. {f}see l.128 §. eo. {g}l.16 §. quod metus causa. {h}It is enough that something is done in a moment, so that it is said to have been done even once, l.17 supra quod metus causa; 2 Eclogae 3 c.129. "In a moment" is the phrase; see l.79 supra de acquirenda haereditate. On "in articulo", the last law, C. de officio comitis sacri palatii. On "de momento" I shall speak at l.vlt. in sin. C. de bonis quae liberis. {i}c. in pari 65 de regulis in 6; l.126 at the end, supra eo; l.5 §1 supra de calumniatoribus; l.9 §4 supra de publiciana; see l.5 at the end, princ. supra §. usufructus petatur; l.8 at the end, supra de conditionibus ob turpem causam; l.10 supra de pignoribus; l.36 §3 at the end, supra de testamentis militaris; l.1 §. vti possidetis; §4 verb. commodum insit, de interdictis; see l.2 C. de conditione ob turpem causam; 2 Eclogae 3 cap. 125; 2 Harmenopulus 1, near the end. units.tr: {a} malae fidei possessor [ὁ ἐκ τῆς κακῆς πίστεως] [?]

units.la: 139. Idem libro vicesimoprimo ad Edictum. Nihil dolo creditor facit, qui {4}suum recipit. ¶ Cùm principalis{b} causa non consistit: ne ea quidem, quæ sequuntur{c}, locum habent{d}.
units.tr: 139. The same, book twenty-one on the Edict. A creditor does nothing by fraud who recovers what is his own. ¶ When the principal cause does not stand, neither do the things which follow it have effect{b}{c}{d}.

units.la: 130. Ulpianus libro octavo decimo ad Edictum. Unquàm {e}actiones, præsertim pœnales{f}, de eadem{g} re concurrentes, alia aliam consumit{h}.
units.tr: 130. Ulpian, book eighteen on the Edict. Actions, especially penal ones, arising from the same matter, one consumes the other{e}{f}{g}{h}.

units.la: 131. Paulus libro vicesimosecundo ad Edictum. QUi dolo desierit possidere, pro possidente damnatur{i}: quia pro {k}possessione{l} dolus est{m}.
units.tr: 131. Paul, book twenty-two on the Edict. One who has ceased to possess by fraud is condemned as if still possessing, because fraud stands in place of possession{i}{k}{l}{m}.

units.la: 132. Gaius libro septimo ad Edictum Provinciale. Imperitia{n} culpæ adnumeratur{o}.
units.tr: 132. Gaius, book seven on the Provincial Edict. Lack of skill is counted as fault{n}{o}.

units.la: 133. Idem libro octavo ad Edictum Provinciale. Melior{p} condicio nostra per servos fieri potest: scilicet
units.tr: 133. The same, book eight on the Provincial Edict. Our condition can be made better through slaves, namely:

units.tr: {i} that is, he is held in the place of a possessor as far as his own loss goes, not as far as advantage; for no cession can be made, just as not for one who possesses; see Dynus on the said c.36 de regulis in 6, num. 2.

units.tr: {m} in effect, namely: to possess is as much as the useful action gives the owner against one who has ceased to possess, as much as the direct action gives against the possessor; l.47 §1 §. de negotiis gestis.

units.tr: {o} as a general rule, but not in the case of a surveyor; l.1 §1 §. si mensor.
134. Ulpian, in the twenty-first book on the Edict.

units.la: NOn{c} fraudantur creditores,cùm{d} quid non adquiritur à debitore : sed cùm quid de bonis{e} diminuitur. ı ¶ Nemo ex suo{f} delito meliore{g} suam condicionem facere potest.
units.tr: Creditors are not defrauded when the debtor fails to acquire something, but only when something is taken away from his goods. ¶ No one can improve his own condition by his own wrongdoing.
135. The same, in the twenty-third book on the Edict.

units.la: EA,quæ dari impossibilia{h} sunt , vel quæ in rerā[?] natura non sunt,pro non{i} adiectis habentur.
units.tr: Things that cannot be given, or that do not exist in the nature of things, are held as if they had not been added.
136. Paul, in the eighteenth book on the Edict.

units.la: BOna fides{k} tantundem{l} possidenti præstat, quantum veritas, quotiens lex impedimento non est{m}.
units.tr: Good faith gives the possessor as much as the truth would, whenever the law is no hindrance.
137. Ulpian, in the twenty-fifth book on the Edict.

units.la: QVi auctore{n} iudice comparauit,bonę fidei possessor est.
units.tr: One who has acquired under the authority of a judge is a possessor in good faith.
138. Paul, in the twenty-seventh book on the Edict.

units.la: OMnis hæreditas, quamuis postea adeatur, tamen cum tempore mortis continuatur{o}.
units.tr: Every inheritance, although it is entered upon later, is nevertheless reckoned as continuing from the time of death.

units.la: ı ¶ Nunquàm crescit ex postfacto{p} prætteriti de-si lifti[?] æstimatio.
units.tr: ¶ The valuation of what has been passed over never increases from a later event.
Cause: add l. 78 above, same title.

units.la: 139. Gaius libro ad Edictum prætoris vrbani.
units.tr: 139. Gaius, in his book on the Edict of the urban praetor.

units.la: OMnes actiones, quæ morte, aut tempore pereunt, semel inclusæ a iudicio, salvæ[?] permanent. ¶ Non videtur perfecte cuiusque id esse, quod ex casu auferri potest.
units.tr: All actions that perish by death or by lapse of time, once brought into litigation, remain intact. ¶ It is not held that a thing is perfectly anyone's if it can be taken away by chance.

units.la: 140. Vlpianus libro quinquagesimo sexto ad Edictum.
units.tr: 140. Ulpian, in the fifty-sixth book on the Edict.

units.la: ABsentia eius, qui reipublicæ causa abest, neque ei, neque alij damnosa esse debet.
units.tr: The absence of one who is away on public business ought to harm neither him nor another.

units.la: 141. Paulus libro quinquagesimo quarto ad Edictum.
units.tr: 141. Paul, in the fifty-fourth book on the Edict.

units.la: QVod contra rationem iuris receptum est, non est producendum ad consequentia. ¶ Vni duo pro solido heredes esse non possunt.
units.tr: What has been received contrary to the reason of law is not to be extended to consequences. ¶ Two persons cannot be heirs for the whole of one thing.

units.la: 142. Idem libro quinquagesimo sexto ad Edictum.
units.tr: 142. The same, in the fifty-sixth book on the Edict.

units.la: QVi tacet, non utique fatetur: sed tamen verum est, eum non negare.
units.tr: He who is silent does not necessarily confess; yet it is true that he does not deny.

units.la: 143. Vlpianus libro sexagesimo secundo ad Edictum.
units.tr: 143. Ulpian, in the sixty-second book on the Edict.

units.la: QVod ipsis, qui contraxerunt, obstat: & successoribus eorum obstabit.
units.tr: What stands in the way of those who contracted will also stand in the way of their successors.

units.la: 144. Paulus libro sexagesimo secundo ad Edictum.
units.tr: 144. Paul, in the sixty-second book on the Edict.

units.la: NOn omne, quod licet, honestum est.
units.tr: Not everything that is permitted is honourable.

units.la: duorum insolidum dominium esse non potest l.5.
units.tr: Ownership of one thing cannot be held wholly by two persons, l.5.

units.la: Cosentit qui non repugnat l.12.§.de sponsalib: 4. Harm.1. non tamen consentit continuo, qui exceptione vtitur l.8. supra de except. Consentimus aut expresse, aut tacite. hinc illa velle, non nolle l.4. §.eo.
units.tr: He consents who does not resist (l.12 §. de sponsalib.; 4 Harm. 1). Yet he does not consent at once who uses an exception (l.8 supra de except.). We consent either expressly or tacitly; hence the rule that to be willing is not to be unwilling (l.4 §. eo).

units.la: vel eo ipso quod tacet, nec roganti, aut loquenti contradicit. quia non palam contradicit. l.52.§.1.§. de pactis: l.37.§.de acquir.here. Hinc illa regula, Resoluto iure dantis, resolvitur ius accipientis & habentis ab eo causam v.l.2.C.de pignoribus: adde l.160.inf.§.eo. l.197.2.Ecloga 3.c.140. exemplum v. in l.14.§.2.§.de vitu. i.impunitum legibus. Cum Iulia novercæ Bassiani ei sinum nudasset: vellem, inquit, si liceret: at illa, si libet licet, An nescis Imperatore leges dare, non accipere?
units.tr: or by the very fact that he is silent and does not contradict one who asks or speaks, since he does not openly contradict (l.52 §.1 §. de pactis; l.37 §. de acquir. here.). Hence the rule: when the right of the giver is dissolved, the right of the recipient, and of one who holds from him, is dissolved (see l.2 C. de pignoribus; add l.160 inf. §. eo; l.197; 2 Ecloga 3 c.140). For an example, see l.14 §.2 §. de vitu: unpunished by the laws. When Julia, the stepmother of Bassianus, had bared her breast to him, he said, "I would like it, if it were allowed." But she replied, "If you like, it is allowed. Do you not know that emperors make laws, and do not accept them?"

units.la: exemplum v.in l.17.inf.§.de hered.petit: l.1.in f.§.de periculo, tanta est honesti ratio: hinc turpis persona v.l.17.§.de inofficioso, condicio l.xii.§.3.§.de legat.1d.63.§.7.§.ad Trebell. vita l.43.§.5.§.de rigu. est a. ¶In stipulationibusb id tempus specia-tur, quo contrahimus.
units.tr: For an example, see l.17 inf. §. de hered. petit.; l.1 in f. §. de periculo; so great is the reason of honesty. Hence a dishonourable person (see l.17 §. de inofficioso), a condition (l.12 §.3 §. de legat.; id. 63 §.7 §. ad Trebell.), a way of life (l.43 §.5 §. de rig.). ¶ In stipulations, the time is considered at which we make the contract.

units.la: 145. Ulpianus [libro sexagesimo sexto ad Edictum.] NEmo videtur fraudare eos, qui sciuntc, & consentiuntd.
units.tr: 145. Ulpian [in the sixty-sixth book on the Edict.] No one is thought to defraud those who know and consent.

units.la: 146. Paulus [libro sexagesimo secundo ad Edictum.] QUod quis, dum seruus est, egit: proficeree libero facto non potest.
units.tr: 146. Paul [in the sixty-second book on the Edict.] What a man did while he was a slave cannot bind him once he has become free.

units.la: 147. Gaius libro vicesimoquarto ad Edictum provinciale. SEmper specialiaf generalibus insunt.
units.tr: 147. Gaius in the twenty-fourth book on the Provincial Edict. Specials are always contained within generals.

units.la: 148. Paulus [libro sextodecimo breuis edicti.] CUius effectus omnibus prodest, eius & partes ad omnes pertinenth.
units.tr: 148. Paul [in the sixteenth book of the Short Edict.] Whatever has an effect for all, its parts also pertain to all.

units.la: 149. Ulpianus [libro sexagesimo septimo ad Edictum.] EX qua persona quis lucrumi capit, eius factum praestare debetk.
units.tr: 149. Ulpian [in the sixty-seventh book on the Edict.] One who takes profit from a person must answer for that person's act.
b l.18 §. eo; see.
