units.tr: Law 78, at the end of the §, "de verb. oblig."; chapters "scienti & consentienti," 27, "de regulis in 6"; 2 Ecloga, chapter 3, 41; law 1, at the end of the §, "de aed. empt."; law 24, §9, §"de aedilitio"; law 1, §3, §"depositi"; law 1, at the end, §"quod falso tutore." And I think this place holds good in the case of one who knows and at the same time consents.

units.la: d l.11.§.quid in fraudem patroni, & volunt l.11. in fine §. de in ius vocando: l.1.§.5.§.de iniuriis: l.8. §.5.§.de aqua plua: l.3.§.5.§.de hereditate libero, voluisse intelligitur, qui aduersus se aliquid scripsit l. 8.§.6.§.eo. e l.98.§.vlt.§.de solution. & nocere v.l.1.& paßim Codicis an seruus ex suo facto. f v.l.8o:l.113.§.eo: 2.Ecloga 3.cap. 141: Species inest genus, id est, comprehenditur c. generi per speciem derogatur 34.de regulis in sext. g Qui omnibus prospicit, nullos excipit. Hinc qui totum restituere tenetur vindicanti, nullam partem retinere debet: adde l.76.§.de rei vindicat: qui totum alienat, nullam partem retinet l.25.§.de vsuris, qui omnes seruos legat, nullum excipit l.52.§.de legatis. h hinc colligunt idem ius esse in parte, quod in toto arg.l.82.§.de acquir.hereditat. Cuius regulae quatuor exceptiones vide hic apud Decium. i l.10.§.eo: l.10.§.fi quis omissa causa: l.13.§.1.§.de acquiren. possessi: l.14.§. de rei vindicat. lx excipe donatarios l.15. C.de donat. & eos qui succedunt facto inuentario, nec enim factum defuncti praestant, Decius hic numero 2.
units.tr: d l.11 §. quid in fraudem patroni, and "volunt": l.11 at the end, §. de in ius vocando; l.1 §.5 de iniuriis; l.8 §.5 de aqua pluvia; l.3 §.5 de hereditate petitione: he is understood to have wished who has written something against himself. l.8 §.6 eodem. e l.98 §. ultimo de solutionibus; and "nocere", see l.1 and passim in the Code, whether a slave by his own act... f see l.80; l.113 §. eo; 2 Ecloga 3 cap. 141: the species is contained in the genus, that is, it is comprehended; the general is derogated by the special, 34 de regulis in sexto. g He who provides for all excludes none. Hence one who is bound to restore the whole to a claimant must retain no part; add l.76 §. de rei vindicatione; he who alienates the whole retains no part, l.25 §. de usuris; he who bequeaths all slaves excludes none, l.52 §. de legatis. h Hence they infer that the same law holds for a part as for the whole, arg. l.82 §. de acquir. hereditatis. For the four exceptions to this rule, see Decius here. i l.10 §. eo; l.10 §. fi quis omissa causa; l.13 §.1 de acquirenda possessione; l.14 §. de rei vindicatione. Except donees, l.15 C. de donationibus, and those who succeed by making an inventory; for they do not make good the deceased's act. Decius here, number 2.
150. The same.
150. The same, in the sixty-eighth book on the Edict.

units.la: PArem esse condicionem oportet eius, qui quid possideat, vel habeat, atque eius, cuius {a}dolo malo factum sit, quo minus possideret, vel haberet.
units.tr: The condition of one who possesses or has something ought to be the same as that of one by whose wicked deceit it came about that he did not possess or have it.
151. Paul, in the sixty-fourth book on the Edict.

units.la: NEmo damnum facit, nisi qui id fecit, quod facere {b}ius non habet.
units.tr: No one causes damage except one who does what he has no right to do.
152. Ulpian, in the sixty-ninth book on the Edict.

units.la: HOc iure vtimur: vt, quidquid omnino per vim fiat, aut {c}in vis publicæ, aut ‖in vis‖priuatæ crimen incidat. {d}Deiicit, & qui {d}mādat. {e}In maleficio ratihabitio {e}mandato comparatur. {f}In contractibus, quibus doli {f}praestatio {g}vel bona fides inest, heres in solidum tenetur.
units.tr: We follow this rule: whatever is done by force at all falls under the crime either of public violence or of private violence. He who orders a dispossession is also liable. In a wrong, ratification is equivalent to a mandate. In contracts in which liability for fraud or good faith is involved, the heir is bound for the whole.
153. Paul, in the sixty-fifth book on the Edict.

units.la: FErè {h}, quibuscunque {i}modis obligamur, iisdem in contrarium actis liberamur: cum quibus modis adquirimus, iisdem in contrarium actis amittimus. Vt igitur nulla possessio adquiri nisi animo & corpore potest: ita nulla amittitur, nisi in qua vtrumque {l}x in contrarium actum sit.
units.tr: Generally, by whatever means we are bound, by the same means, acting to the contrary, we are freed; by whatever means we acquire, by the same, acting to the contrary, we lose. So just as no possession can be acquired except by mind and body, so none is lost unless both are acted against.
154. Ulpian, in the seventieth book on the Edict.

units.la: CVm par delictum est duorum, semper oneratur petitor {k}, & melior habetur possessoris {m}causa: aut est publi-ca, aut est priuata. {f}Possessio {n}sine corpore...
units.tr: When the wrong is equal on both sides, the claimant is always burdened, and the cause of the possessor is held the better: whether it is public or private. Possession without body...

units.la: {h} cur hæc particula fere, seu σχεδὸν addita est? vt intelligas possessionem non iisdem semper modis amitti quibus adquiritur: facilius, n. amittitur, quâ adquiritur. Corpus requiritur in adquirenda, at solus animus sufficit in amittenda l.3. §.6. s. de acq. possess. vide Scholion apud Harm. 2. iii. 1. {i} l.35. l.100. s. eo. l.8. s. de acquir. possess. l.80. s. de solutio. {k} Imò solo animo possessio amitti potest? l.3. §.6. s. de acquir. possess. vtique, si animo eam amittere incipimus, secus si corpore. {l} l.33. s. eo: c. in pari delicto 65: de regul. in 6: 2. Eclog. 3. c.150. reus potior l.38. s. de re iudicata. {m} i. dolosi à quo petitur l.36. s. de dolo. l.57. in fi. s. de contrah. empt. l.4. §.13. s. de doli mali except. l.91. §.3. in fine s. de verborum oblig: v. Dynam ad c.65, de regulis in 6. sicut fit,cùm de dolo excipitur petitoris.neque enim datur talis replicatio {a} petitori, {b}Aut fi {c} rei {d} quae in ea re dolo actum fit. {1} ¶Illi debet permitti poenam petere,qui {e} in ipsam non incidit {f}.
units.tr: Why is this particle added, almost [σχεδὸν]? So that you understand that possession is not always lost by the same means by which it is acquired: it is lost more easily than it is acquired. Body is required in acquiring, but mind alone suffices in losing: l. 3 §. 6 s. de acq. possess. See the scholium in Harmenopulus 2, iii, 1. l. 35; l. 100 s. eo; l. 8 s. de acquir. possess.; l. 80 s. de solutio. Can possession be lost by mind alone? l. 3 §. 6 s. de acquir. possess. Certainly, if we begin to lose it by intention; otherwise, if by the body. l. 33 s. eo; c. in pari delicto 65 de regul. in 6; 2 Eclog. 3, c. 150: the defendant is the stronger party; l. 38 s. de re iudicata. That is, of the one who is sued, the party acting with fraud; l. 36 s. de dolo; l. 57 in fine s. de contrah. empt.; l. 4 §. 13 s. de doli mali except.; l. 91 §. 3 in fine s. de verborum oblig. See Dynamis on c. 65, de regulis in 6. This happens when an exception of fraud is raised against the plaintiff, for no such replication is granted to the plaintiff unless the thing was done with fraud in that matter. ¶It should be permitted to seek the penalty to one who has not himself fallen into it.
155. Paulus, from book sixty-five on the Edict.

units.la: Factum cuique suum {f}, nō aduersario nocere debet. {1} ¶Nō videtur vim facere,qui iure suo {g} vtitur,& ordinaria actione experitur. {2} ¶In poenalibus causis benignius {h} interpretandum est.
units.tr: Each person's own act ought to harm himself, not his adversary. He does not seem to use force who uses his own right and pursues the matter by ordinary action. In penal cases the interpretation should be more lenient.
156. Ulpian, book 70 on the Edict.
No one is compelled against his will to defend a thing.

units.la: {e}Cur ita? nemini datur actio,nisi ex honesta causa.
units.tr: Why so? No action is given to anyone except from an honest cause.

units.la: {f} l.39. l.49. l.134. s.eodem: l.9. s.qua in fraudem credit. {g} v.l.151. s.eodem: l.12. in fine s.de vi. {h} c. in pœnis 49.de regulis in 6: l.192. in fine s.eo.l.2.s.de liberis & posthumis. mitior lex sequenda l.32. in fine s.de pœnis: pœnæ molliendæ l.41. s. de pœnis: humaniorem sententiam sequi oportet l.10.§.1.s.de reb.dub. si modo negotium id pati potest, si non præsumitur delistum v.Aliatum 3.præsumpt.v: puta furtum l.51.s.pro socio, inusta infamia l.4. §.2.s.de suspectis: adde l.23.in f.s.de adult. si quidem, odia & pœnas quantum fieri potest, restringi oportet. c.odia 15.de regulis in sext. {i} adde qua de inuito dixi ad l.59.s.ro. {k} l.17.C.de procuratore, puta noxali iudicio l.19.l.33.s.de noxal. sed & executor esse, Decius hic numero 2. procuratoris munus sustinere l.8.§.1.s.de procurat.: datus tamen ad agendum, cogitur defensionem suscipere l.33.§.4.s.de procurat: l.4. s.de tutelis: & munus persequi, satisdare l.35. §.2.s.de procurat. non tamen vltra prouocationem l.17. C.de procurat. nec extra sua prouinciam l.35.§.2.s.de procur. non absimiliter cogitur nemo inuitus agere & accusare l.1.C.vt nemo inuitus: vectigal conducere l.19.§.1.s.de publicanis: aut in conductione vectigalis perseuerare lustro peracto l.3.§.6. s. de iure fisci, seu frumentum vilius, quam annona exigit, vendere l.vlt. s.de annona. potest tamen quis iusta de causa cogi inuitus negotiationem aliquam exercere l.9.§.9.s.de pœnis,& seruos suos distrahere l.2.s.de his qui sunt sui. Potest etiam cogi aduocatus ad postulandum, v.l.7. C. de postulando: doctor, ad consilium dandum v.l.6. Cod. de aduocatis diu: vsorum in distiorū, eaque quis procuratione defungi, quam nostro tempore procuratores exercere solent Decius hic: arg. l.1.§.11, s.de variis & extraord. Ita notarius instrumentum conficere cogi potest, vt & cauponi, hospes, nauta, tabernarius, commeantes, & vectores excipere lesse prima, supra nauta cauponis, quod Decius turpissimè, & contra omnem iuris & æqui artem extendit ad meretrices in lupanari stantes.
units.tr: Dig. 39, 49, 134 (same title); Dig. 9 (qua in fraudem creditorum). See Dig. 151 (same title); Dig. 12 in fine (de vi). The Papist canon 49 (de reg. iur. in 6), Dig. 192 in fine, Dig. 2 (de liberis et posthumis): the milder law is to be followed (Dig. 32 in fine, de poenis); penalties are to be softened (Dig. 41, de poenis); a more humane opinion ought to be followed (Dig. 10.1, de reb. dub.), provided the matter admits it, and if no delict is presumed (see Aliatus, praesumpt. 3); for example theft (Dig. 51, pro socio), infamy inflicted (Dig. 4.2, de suspectis). Add Dig. 23 in fine (de adult.): indeed hatreds and penalties ought to be restrained as far as possible (canon 15, de reg. in sext.). Add what I have said about the unwilling person at Dig. 59, ad ro. Dig. 17 C. de procuratore; for example in a noxal action (Dig. 19, 33, de noxal.). But Decius here, number 2, holds that the one who is also an executor bears the office of a procurator (Dig. 8.1, de procurat.); yet one given to act is compelled to take up the defence (Dig. 33.4, de procurat.; Dig. 4, de tutelis), and to pursue the office and give security (Dig. 35.2, de procurat.); not, however, beyond appeal (Dig. 17 C. de procurat.), nor outside his province (Dig. 35.2, de procur.). In a similar way no one is compelled unwillingly to act or accuse (Cod. 1, ut nemo invitus); to farm the tax (Dig. 19.1, de publicanis), or to persevere in the farming of the tax after the lustrum is completed (Dig. 3.6, de iure fisci); or to sell grain cheaper than the price fixed by the market (Dig. last, de annona). Yet for a just cause a person may be compelled, against his will, to carry on some business (Dig. 9.9, de poenis), and to sell off his own slaves (Dig. 2, de his qui sunt sui). An advocate also may be compelled to plead (Cod. 7, de postulando); a teacher to give counsel (Cod. 6, de advocatis diversorum iudicum); and one may be compelled to perform the duty of a procurator, which procurators in our time are accustomed to exercise (Decius here; argument from Dig. 1.11, de variis et extraord.). So too a notary can be compelled to draw up a document, and likewise an innkeeper, a host, a sailor, a tavern-keeper, travellers and passengers to receive; Decius extends the first case, concerning sailors and innkeepers, most shamefully and against all the art of law and equity, to prostitutes standing in brothels.

units.la: 1 ¶ Cui damus actiones{a}, eidem & exceptionem competere multo{b} magis quis dixerit{c}.
units.tr: 1 He to whom we give actions, the exception ought also to be available to him, much more so, someone has said.

units.la: 2 ¶ Cùm quis in alij{d} locum successerit: non est æquum ei{e} nocere hoc, quod aduersus eum nocuit, in cuius locum successit.
units.tr: 2 When someone has succeeded into another's place, it is not fair that what was done against the person into whose place he succeeded should harm him.

units.la: 3 ¶ Plerumque {f}em-ptoris eadem{g} causa esse debet circa petendum ac defendendum, quæ fuit auctoris.
units.tr: 3 Generally the cause of the buyer ought to be the same in seeking as in defending as that of the seller was.

units.la: 4 ¶ Quod cuique ||pro eo||præstatur, inuito{h} non tribuitur.
units.tr: 4 What is granted to someone for another is not given against his will.
157. The same, book 71 on the Edict.

units.la: AD ea{k}, quæ non habent atrocitatem facinoris vel sceleris, ignoscitur seruis, si vel dominis, vel his, qui vice{l} dominorum sunt, (veluti tutoribus, & curatoribus) obtemperauerint{m}.
units.tr: Slaves are pardoned for those acts which do not have the atrocity of a crime or wickedness, if they have obeyed either their masters or those who stand in the place of masters (such as tutors and curators).

units.la: 1 ¶ Semper, qui dolo fecit, quominus{n} haberet, pro eo habendus est, ac si haberet.
units.tr: 1 Always, one who acted by fraud so that he would not have, is to be regarded as if he had.

units.la: 2 ¶ In contractibus successores ex dolo{o} eorum, (quibus) successerunt, non tantùm in id, quod peruenit, verumetiam in solidum tenentur{p}: hoc{q} est, unusquisque pro ea parte, qua heres est.
units.tr: 2 In contracts, successors are held liable for the fraud of those whom they succeeded, not only up to the amount that came to them, but for the whole sum; that is, each one for the part of which he is heir.

units.la: recuperandæ possessionis, in quibus reo qui spoliauit non datur exceptio dominii, nisi priùs restituerit possessionem. datur ei actio, negatur exceptio l.25. C.de locato: l.1. C.si per vim l.7. C.de vi publica: l.14. s.de agricolis: adde Nouell.88. & merito, cùm actio & exceptio referantur ad res diuersas: hæc ad possessionem, illa ad proprietatem.{r}
units.tr: of recovering possession, in which the defendant who has dispossessed is not given the exception of ownership unless he first restores possession. An action is given to him, but the exception is denied (Cod. 25, de locato; Cod. 1, si per vim; Cod. 7, de vi publica; Dig. 14, de agricolis); add Novel. 88. And rightly, since the action and the exception relate to different things: the one to possession, the other to ownership.

units.la: {s}alicuius Vulgat. Hal. successori non nocet, quòd eius auctori nocere nō potuit l.3. §.2. in f. s.de itinere actuque: adde l.76. in f. s.de contrah. empt: l.37. s.de acquir. hered. & contra quòd auctori nocere potuit, successori nocere potest l.143. supra eo.{t} nam quod auctoribus bonæ fidei prodesse potuit, successori malæ fidei nocere incipit l.2. §.17. s.pro emptore.{u} 2. Ecloga 2. c.152. §.3: l.2. s.de hered. vendit: l.20. s.de acquir. rer. dom: l.2. in fine s.pro emptore: l.5. C.de hered. vendita: l.26. C.de eniti:{v} l.69. s.eo: l.19. §.2. s.de donat.{w}
units.tr: Vulgat. Hal. Harm to a successor of someone is not caused by what could not harm his author (Dig. 3.2 in fine, de itinere actuque; add Dig. 76 in fine, de contrah. empt.; Dig. 37, de acquir. hered.). And conversely, what could harm the author can harm the successor (Dig. 143, supra eo). For what could benefit the authors in good faith begins to harm the successor in bad faith (Dig. 2.17, pro emptore). 2 Ecloga 2, c. 152 §3; Dig. 2, de hered. vend.; Dig. 20, de acquir. rer. dom.; Dig. 2 in fine, pro emptore; Cod. 5, de hered. vend.; Cod. 26, de evict.; Dig. 69 (same title); Dig. 19.2, de donat.

units.la: {i} Quidam ita legunt, non eripitur, ex cap. indulsum 17. de regulis in 6. l.7. §.2. s.de noxalibus: l.21. §.1. s.rerum amotarum: l.11. §.7. s.quod vi: l.17. §.7. s.de iniuriis: l.25. §.2. s. de falsis: 2. Ecloga 3. cap.152. §.5: l.8. C.ad legem Iuliam de vi.{x} tutores sunt vice dominorum pupillarium rerum vt hic: domini loco l.27. s.de administr. tut: adde l.56. §.4. supra de furtis.{y} l.167. in fine ].eo.{z} v. l.78: l.150. s.eo.{aa} v. l.152. in f. s.eo.{bb}
units.tr: Some read it thus: "is not taken away", from the canon Indulsum 17, de reg. in 6; Dig. 7.2, de noxalibus; Dig. 21.1, rerum amotarum; Dig. 11.7, quod vi; Dig. 17.7, de iniuriis; Dig. 25.2, de falsis; 2 Ecloga 3, cap. 152 §5; Cod. 8, ad legem Iuliam de vi. Tutors are in the place of masters of the pupil's property, as here; in the place of the owner (Dig. 27, de administr. tut.); add Dig. 56 §4 supra de furtis; Dig. 167 in fine (same title); see Dig. 78; Dig. 150 (same title); see Dig. 152 in fine (same title).

units.la: {p} Imo tunc non tenentur §.1. versic. aliquando Inst.de perpet. & temp.{cc}
units.tr: Indeed, then they are not held: §1, the clause "sometimes", Inst. de perpet. et temp.

units.la: ? puto legendum, tenentur, vel unusquisque, &c. vt sit sensus, Socium heredem in solidum, teneri etiam in solidum: pro parte, ex rata partis l.9. supra de condict. furtiua. & ita intellige l.12. l.49. supra de oblig.
units.tr: I think it should be read "they are held", or "each one", etc., so that the sense is: the associate heir is held for the whole, and also for the whole, but for the part, in proportion to his share (Dig. 9, supra de condict. furtiva). And understand Dig. 12 and 49 supra de oblig. in this way.

units.la: 158. Gaius libro vicesimosexto ad Edictum Prouinciale.
units.tr: 158. Gaius, book 26 on the Provincial Edict.

units.la: CReditor, qui permittit rem venire, pignus de-{4}mittit.
units.tr: A creditor who allows the thing to be sold releases the pledge.
159. Paulus, book 70 on the Edict.

units.la: NOn{b} vt ex pluribus causis deberi nobis idem potest, ita ex pluribus causis idem possit nostrum esse{c}.
units.tr: It is not the case that, just as the same thing can be owed to us from several causes, so the same thing can be ours from several causes.
160. Ulpian, book 76 on the Edict.

units.la: ALiud{d} est{e} vendere, aliud{f} vendenti consenti-re s.{f} 1 Refertur ad vniuersos, quod publice fit per maiorem{h} partem. 2 Absurdum est, plus iuris habere ||eum, ||cui legatus{i} sit fundus, quàm heredem, aut ipsum testatorem si vixeret.
units.tr: It is one thing to sell, another to consent to the seller's sale. 1 What is done publicly by the greater part is referred to all. 2 It is absurd that he to whom a farm has been left by legacy should have more right than the heir, or the testator himself if he were alive.
161. The same, in book seventy-seven on the Edict.

units.la: IN iure ciuili receptum est, quotiens per eum, cu-
units.tr: In civil law it is accepted that, as often as a thing can be mine only once, it can be owed more than once: see Dig. 14.2 §2 de except. rei iudicatae.

units.la: semel res mea esse potest, sæpius deberi potest l.14.§.2.s.de except.vel iudicatę. Quod iam nostrum est, aut proprium, magis, aut ampliùs nostrum fieri non potest §.10. Instit.de legatis §.14. Instit. de act. {c}hinc fit vt rem nostram inutiliter stipulemur ratione domini l 31. supra de verborum obligat. vtque eadem nobis inutiliter legetur eodē respectu §.10. Inst.de legatis: adde l.45. supra eo. {d}Imo non aliud l.158. supra eo. {e}nisi sit vtrobique eadem ratio. hinc minor nec alienare, nec alienationi consentire potest l.2. C.si aduersus donationem, cui vnum eorum permittitur, alterum quoque conceditur l.163.l.165.codem.
units.tr: What is already ours, or our own, cannot become more ours or more fully ours: Inst. de legatis §10; Inst. de actionibus §14. Hence it is that we stipulate uselessly for a thing of our own, by reason of ownership (Dig. 45.1, 31, de verborum obligationibus), and in the same way a thing of our own is uselessly bequeathed to us on the same ground (Inst. de legatis §10; add Dig. 45, eodem title). Indeed, it is not otherwise (Dig. 158, eodem), unless the reason is the same on both sides. Hence a minor can neither alienate nor consent to an alienation (C. 2, si adversus donationem). Where one of two things is permitted, the other is also granted (Dig. 163 and 165, eodem).

units.la: {f} si aliud est, igitur cui vnum eorum non licebit, aliud ei permitti intelligetur l.2. Codice de manumiss. vindicta. {g} hinc aliud est contrahere, aliud contrahenti consentire. {h} v.l.3.l.4. supra quod cuiusque: l.19. supra ad municipalem, facit lex 10. supra de pactis: l.7. in fine Cod. de omni agro deserto: l.148.§.eo. & ita intelligere l.10.§.de aqua pluuia, vel per eos à quibus res municipij geri solent l.97.§.de condit.& demonstr: l.vn.§.1. supra de liber.vniuers: l.§.2.supra de acquir. possess. sic maioris partis bonorum litis ratio habetur in excusando tutore l.21.§. de excusat. iut. & maioris partis anni, vt res aliqua fundi esse dicatur, vel negetur l.18.§.12.§.de instructo, quod omnes tangit, ab omnibus debet approbari c.quod omnes 19. de regul.in sext. {i} legatarius non est potioris iuris, quàm heres aut defunctus l.120.l.143.§. eo.l.176.in f.] ee. ius interest codicionem non impleri,fiat,quo minus impleatur,perinde haberi, ac si impleta condicio fuisset. quod ad libertatem, & legata, & ad heredum institutiones perducitur. quibus exemplis stipulationes quoque committitur,cùm per promissorem factum esset,quo minus stipulator condicioni pareret.
units.tr: If the one is different, then the other, which is not allowed to one who cannot do the first, is understood to be permitted to him (C. 2, de manumissione vindicta). Hence it is one thing to contract, another to consent to a contract. See Dig. 3 and 4, supra quod cuiusque universitatis; Dig. 19, ad municipalem; the law at Dig. 10, de pactis, agrees; C. 7, in fine, de omni agro deserto; Dig. 148 §, eodem. And this is to be understood as in Dig. 10 §, de aqua pluvia, or through those by whom the affairs of a municipality are customarily managed (Dig. 97 §, de condit. et demonstr.; Dig. 1 §1, de liberis universis; Dig. 2 §, de acquirenda possessione). So too the reckoning of the greater part of the goods is taken into account in excusing a guardian (Dig. 21 §, de excusationibus), and of the greater part of the year, so that something is said to be or denied to be part of an estate (Dig. 18 §12, de instructo), since what touches all must be approved by all (c. Quod omnes 19, de regulis iuris in sexto). A legatee does not have a stronger right than the heir or the deceased (Dig. 120, Dig. 143 §, eodem, Dig. 176 in fine). It is a matter of law that when a condition is not fulfilled because of someone, it is held as if the condition had been fulfilled, if the thing is brought about by which it is not fulfilled. This extends to freedom, to legacies, and to the institution of heirs. By such examples the same applies to stipulations, when a promisor has done something by which the stipulator is prevented from meeting the condition.
162. Paulus, book seventy on the Edict.

units.la: Qvæ[?] propter necessitatem recepta sunt, nō debent in argumentum trahi.
units.tr: Those things which were admitted because of necessity ought not to be drawn into argument.

units.la: 163. Vlpianus libro quinquagesimo quinto ad Edictum.
units.tr: 163. Ulpian, book fifty-five on the Edict.

units.la: Cvius est donandi: eidem & vendendi, & cō-
units.tr: To whom it belongs to give, to the same belongs also to sell, and to consent to

units.la: 6. Harmenop.2. Plane ordo est inuersus, sic restituo. Quoties per eum,cuius interest condicionem impleri, non fiat quominus impleatur,&c. quod optimè conuenit legi 3. §. 10. in fine : l. 28. s. de statulib. cap. imputari 41: & cap. cùm non stat per eum 66. de regulis, in sexto. vt interim dicam in di&o cap.66.quominus su-mi pro,quin,vel, quod magis.
units.tr: (6 Harmenopulus 2.) The order is indeed inverted; I restore it thus: Whenever it is not through the one whose interest it is that the condition be fulfilled that it is not fulfilled, etc. This agrees very well with Dig. 3 §10 in fine; Dig. 28, de statuliberis; c. Imputari 41; and c. Cum non stat per eum 66, de regulis in sexto. Meanwhile I will say, in the said c. 66, that "quominus" is taken for "quin" or for "quod magis."

units.la: c Ecl.ib.l.20.§.3:l.28.s. de statulib. d Ecloga ibidem & l.24: l.5.§.5.s.quando dies legati. e Ecloga ib.& d. lege 24.l.3. s.de condit.instit. f Ecloga ib.& dicta lege 24. g l.85.s.de verborum obligat. h τὰ δ᾽ ἀνάγκην 2.Ecloga 3.cap.161. τὰ περὶ κατὰ νόμον λεγόμενα 6.Harmenop. 2.contra rationem iuris l.14.l.15 s.de legibus, contra tenorem rationis l.16.s.de legib. vt ea quæ à iure exorbitant cap.quæ à iure 28.de regulis in sext. quæ ob gratiam alicui conceduntur cap. quod ob gratiam 61.de regul.in sext. sic necessitas probabilem facit manumissionem l.27.s.de manum.testam. Clarus etiâ id innui putat,furem excusari à pœna furti commissi, propter extremam necessitatem 5.sententi. §.furtum versic.quandoque : necessitas etiam excusat venditionem filij l.2.C.de patr.qui filios. Quod non est licitum in lege, necessitas facit licitum cap.quod non est,extra de regulis. hinc illud, Necessitas non habet legem. Non ignoscitur tamen ei,quæ obtentu paupertatis turpissimam vitam agit l.45.§.5.s.de vita.
units.tr: (c) Eclogue, book 1, 20 §3; Dig. 28, de statuliberis. (d) Eclogue ibid., and Dig. 24; Dig. 5 §5, quando dies legati. (e) Eclogue ibid., and the said law 24; Dig. 3, de conditionibus institutionum. (f) Eclogue ibid., and the said law 24. (g) Dig. 85, de verborum obligationibus. (h) [Greek: ta d' anankēn] 2. Eclogue 3, cap. 161; [Greek: ta peri kata nomon legomena] 6 Harmenopulus 2: against the reason of law, Dig. 14 and 15, de legibus; against the tenor of reason, Dig. 16, de legibus. So things which depart from law (c. Quae ab iure 28, de regulis in sexto) and those granted to someone out of favour (c. Quod ob gratiam 61, de regulis in sexto) are such. Thus necessity makes a manumission probable (Dig. 27, de manumissis testamento). Clarus thinks this is also hinted at: that a thief is excused from the penalty of theft committed through extreme necessity (Sent. 5, §furtum, verse "quandoque"). Necessity also excuses the sale of a son (C. 2, de patribus qui filios distraxerunt). What is not permitted by law, necessity makes permitted (c. Quod non est, extra de regulis). Hence the saying, "Necessity has no law." Yet one is not pardoned who, under the pretext of poverty, lives a most shameful life (Dig. 45 §5, de vita).

units.la: t consequentias l.14.s. de oblig: ad regulas iuris l.15. s.de legibus, εἰς ὑπὸ τῶν [?] Ecloga ib.Harmenop. ib. id est exemplum. hinc sine exemplo subiuenire §.9.in fine,Inst.de iure naturali,sans tirer en consequence. k Argumentum à maiori ad minus, Qui potest donare,potest vendere,multo magis concedere 2.Ecloga 3. cap.158: adde l.21.s.eo: sic, cui testamenti factio est,donare potest mortis causa,& non causa l.7.in f.s.de donat: sic qui potest alienare, potest alienationi consentire l.165.§.eo. l & è contrà ,prohibitus vendere, donare non potest. Imò potest l.4 Codice de fideiissor. Solue.Volun-
units.tr: (i) Consequences: Dig. 14, de obligationibus; to the rules of law, Dig. 15, de legibus; [Greek: eis hypo tōn] (?) Eclogue ibid., Harmenopulus ibid.; that is, an example. Hence to help without precedent (Inst. de iure naturali §9, in fine), not drawing a consequence. (k) An argument from the greater to the less: one who can give can sell, and much more can concede (2. Eclogue 3, c. 158); add Dig. 21, eodem. So one who has testamentary capacity can give in view of death and not otherwise (Dig. 7, in fine, de donationibus). So one who can alienate can consent to alienation (Dig. 165 §, eodem). And conversely, one forbidden to sell cannot give; indeed he can (C. 4, de fideiussoribus, solve). Voluntary

units.la: taci defunctis nō repugnat, qui donat so-rori, quod ex tra familiam vendere, aut pignori dare non potest.
units.tr: (...) it does not conflict with the deceased that one who gives to a sister what he cannot sell or pledge outside the family.

units.la: α καὶ ἐγχο- ῤῆι αὐτῷ ἀ ν ταῦτ[?] Ecloga ibid. id est, etiam credere potest. concedendi vocabulo quidam intelligūt colonariū contractum.
units.tr: ([Greek: kai engcho-] ...) Eclogue ibid., that is, he can even lend. Some understand the word "concedere" to mean the colonial contract.

units.la: ƀ Imò non est. Decurio donare potest, vendere non potest l. vltima, Cod. de pradiis Decurionum, id merito sublatum Nouella 38.
units.tr: (b) Indeed it is not so: a decurion can give but cannot sell (last law, C. de praediis decurionum), a rule rightly abolished by Novella 38.
Ius is of conceding.

units.la: 164. Paulus ‖libro quinquagesimo primo ad Edictum.‖ POenalia iudicia semel o accepta, in heredes transmitti possunt.
units.tr: 164. Paulus, book fifty-one on the Edict. Penal actions, once brought, can be transmitted to heirs.

units.la: 165. Vlpianus ‖libro quinquagesimo tertio ad Edictum.‖ CVm quis possit alienare p, poterit & consentire alienationi. Cui autem donare non concedi-tur, probandum erit, nec si donationis causa consen-serit, ratam eius voluntatem habendam.
units.tr: 165. Ulpian, book fifty-three on the Edict. Since one who can alienate can also consent to an alienation. But whoever is not permitted to donate must be proved; nor, if he has consented for the sake of a donation, is his will to be held as ratified.

units.la: 166. Paulus ‖libro quadragesimooctauo ad Edictum.‖ QVi rem alienam defendit, nunquam locuples habetur q.
units.tr: 166. Paulus, book forty-eight on the Edict. One who defends another's property is never held to be wealthy.

units.la: 167. Idem ‖ libro quadragesimonono ad Edictum.‖ NOn videntur ʳ data ˢ, quæ eo tempore, quo dō[?]-tur, accipientis non fiunt. ᵗ ꝗ Qui iussu in-dicis ᵘ aliquid facit, non ᵛ videtur dolo malo face-re, qui parere necesse habet.
units.tr: 167. The same, book forty-nine on the Edict. Things are not regarded as given which, at the time they are given, do not become the property of the recipient. One who acts by the order of a judge is not regarded as acting with malicious intent, since he is bound to obey.
168. The same, book 1 on Plautius.

units.la: ᶜ 2. Ecloga 3. cap, 159. alias non contestata mininiè transmittuntur l.11. in fine ʃ.eo? l.26. l.58. ʃ.de oblig. §.1. in fine, Instit.de perpetuis: l. vnica C.ex delicto defunctii.
units.tr: (c) Eclogue 3, c. 159. Otherwise, things not litigated are not transmitted at all (Dig. 11 in fine; Dig. 26; Dig. 58, de obligationibus; Inst. de perpetuis §1 in fine; C. unica, ex delicto defuncti).

units.la: Quin, non omnia contestata in heredes transseunt. heredes rei ob delictum (paucis exceptis) non tenentur, nisi lata sententia l.20. ʃ. de accusat.
units.tr: Indeed, not all things litigated pass to heirs. Heirs of one accused of a crime are not bound (except in a few cases) unless sentence has been pronounced (Dig. 20, de accusationibus).

units.la: ᵖ Cui maius licet, eidem minus est permissum v.l.21. l.66. ʃ.eodem.
units.tr: (p) One to whom the greater is permitted, to the same the less is permitted: see Dig. 21, Dig. 66, eodem.

units.la: ᵠ Nota, argumentandi speciem à contrario sensu, id est, nunquam ita quisquam locuples habendus est, vt immunis à satisdando sit eius nomine quem defendit l.35. §.3: l.51. in fine: l.52. l.53. ʃ.de procurat. nisi defendat necessariam personam l.3. ʃ.in ius vocati: l.2. §.2. ʃ.qui satisdare: adde l.95. ʃ.eo: l.134. §.1. ʃ.de verb.signif: l.63. in fine princ. ʃ.ad leg.Falcid.
units.tr: (q) Note this kind of argument from the contrary sense: that is, no one is ever to be regarded as so wealthy as to be exempt from giving security on account of the person whom he defends (Dig. 35 §3; Dig. 51 in fine; Dig. 52; Dig. 53, de procuratoribus), unless he defends a necessary person (Dig. 3, in ius vocati; Dig. 2 §2, qui satisdare cogantur). Add Dig. 95, eodem; Dig. 134 §1, de verborum significatione; Dig. 63 in fine princ., ad legem Falcidiam.

units.la: ʳ proprie, secus improprie, ratione personæ l.55. ʃ. de condic.& demonstr. vel contractus l.4. ʃ.de vsuris.
units.tr: (r) Properly; otherwise improperly, by reason of the person (Dig. 55, de condicionibus et demonstrationibus), or of the contract (Dig. 4, de usuris).

units.la: ˢ v.l.vlt: ʃ.de condiit. causa data: l.75. in f.de verbor. oblig. §.14. Inst.de actionibus.
units.tr: (s) See the last law; Dig. de conditione causa data; Dig. 75 in fine, de verborum obligationibus; Inst. de actionibus §14.

units.la: ᵗ l.169. ʃ.eo: adde l.137. ʃ.eo. vel superioris l.157. ʃ.eo.
units.tr: (t) Dig. 169, eodem; add Dig. 137, eodem, or of the earlier one, Dig. 157, eodem.

units.la: ᵘ Iussus iudicis excusat à dolo,& delicto l.7. §.4. ʃ.de iurisdict: l.7. §.2. in fine ʃ.de minoribus: l.8. ʃ.de lege commissoria: l.4. ʃ.de aqua pluuia: l.11. §.2. ʃ.de iniuriis, non confert tamen ad lucrum, idque sentit Oldendorpius Classe 1. actit. 3. in fine.
units.tr: (u) One ordered by a judge is excused from fraud and delict (Dig. 7 §4, de iurisdictione; Dig. 7 §2 in fine, de minoribus; Dig. 8, de lege commissoria; Dig. 4, de aqua pluvia; Dig. 11 §2, de iniuriis); it does not, however, confer any gain. Oldendorp thinks this in Class 1, action 3, in fine.

units.la: [?]Capienda{a} occasio{b} est, quæ præbet benignius{c} responsum. 1 ¶Quod factum est, cùm in obscuro{d} sit, ex affectione cuiusque{e} capit interpretationem.
units.tr: An opportunity is to be seized which offers the kinder answer. 1 ¶ What has been done, since it is obscure, takes its interpretation from the disposition of each person.
169. The same, book two on Plautius.

units.la: IS damnum dat, qui iubet{f} dare. eius verò nulla culpa est, cui parere{h} necesse sit. 1 ¶Quod pe-det{i}, non est pro eo, quasi sit.
units.tr: He who orders another to give causes the loss, but he is not at fault to whom it is necessary to obey. 1 ¶ What is owed is not in place of that which seems to be.
170. The same, book 4, to Plautius.

units.la: FActum{k} à iudice, quod{l} ad officium{m} eius{n} pertinet, ratum non est{o}.
units.tr: An act of a judge, so far as it pertains to his office, is not invalid.
171. The same, book 4, to Plautius.

units.la: NEmo ideo obligatur{p}, quia præcepturus est{q} ab alio{r}, quod præstiterit.
units.tr: No one is bound merely because he is going to order another to pay what that other has performed.
172. The same, book 5[?], to Plautius.

units.la: IN contrahenda venditione ambiguum pactum contra venditorem, interpretandum est{s}. {t} ¶ Am-
units.tr: In making a contract of sale, an ambiguous agreement is to be interpreted against the seller. ¶
g Indeed, see l.1 §1 §quod vi.

units.la: h l.167. in fi.§.cod: v.l.11.§.7.§.quod vi.
units.tr: h See l.167 in fin. §cod; l.11 §7 §quod vi.

Macedoniano: l.43.§.edilitio: l.20.§.de donat. inter viuum: l.9.§.2 §.de liberis: l.59.§.6.§.de hered. units.la: k res iudicata l.116. in sin.§.de verbor. obligat.§.5.Inst. quibus modis tut patria.factum Praetoris iuri derogare non debet l.unica C.qui pro sua iurisdicti. l c.ea quae fiunt a iudice 16. de regulis in 6. 2.Ecloga 3.c.166.
units.tr: k A thing adjudged: l.116 in sin. §de verbor. obligat.; §5 Inst. quibus modis tutel. finitur. An act of the Praetor must not derogate from the law: l. unica C. qui pro sua iurisdictione. L. c. ea quae fiunt a iudice, 16 de regulis iuris in 6; 2. Ecloga, 3, c. 166.
m Also jurisdiction: see l. ult. §de iurisdictione.

units.la: n tunc etiam habetur pro priuato.
units.tr: n Then it is also held to be a private matter.

units.la: o puta ad opus sua impensa Titio restituendu.
units.tr: o For instance, that it be restored to Titius at the cost of the work.

units.la: p id est, quamuis, vt sit sensus, Non si socius impensas socij nomine factas ab eodem potest repetere, tenetur eas actori praestare. est enim iniquum innocentem, nocentis facto obligari l.11.§.2.§.de aqua pluuia.
units.tr: p That is, even though, so that the sense is: if a partner cannot recover from a co-partner the expenses made in the co-partner's name, he is bound to pay them to the plaintiff, for it is unjust that an innocent person be bound by the act of a wrongdoer: l.11 §2 §de aqua pluvia.
q Namely, in the common action for division.

units.la: r puta Mxuio, socio, qui opus Titio damnosum fecit.
units.tr: r For instance, Maevius, a partner, who made the work harmful to Titius.

units.la: s Patio obscura, vel ambigua, venditori nocet l.39.§.de pactis: l.33. in f.§.de contrahend.emptio.& stipulatori l.38.§.15.§.de verbor. obligat. quia potuit te integra apertius dicere l.21.§.de contrahend.empt.solue.vt ibidem.
units.tr: s An obscure or ambiguous agreement harms the seller, and also the stipulator, l.39 §de pactis; l.33 in fin. §de contrahenda emptione; l.38 §15 §de verbor. obligat., because he could have spoken more clearly while the matter was still open: l.21 §de contrahenda emptione, solutio, as there.

units.la: t aliud in oratione aperta,& magis verisimili l. 34.§. eodem. beneficiis principium: l.43.§.de vulgari:iudiciis §.1.l.tod: & confessione Decim hic. bigua autem intentio ita accipienda est, vt {b} interpretari debet, ut salua actori sit {c}.
units.tr: t Otherwise, in open speech and what is more probable: l.34 §eodem, beneficiis principium; l.43 §de vulgari; iudiciis §1, l. tod.; and by confession, Decimus here. An ambiguous intention, however, must be understood so as to be interpreted in a way that leaves the action safe for the plaintiff.
Otherwise the act itself would perish.
173. The same, book 6, to Plautius.

units.la: IN condemnatione personarum, quae {d} in id, quod facere possunt, damnantur, non totum quod habent, extorquendum est: sed & ipsarum ratio habenda est, ne egeant {e}. 1 ¶Cùm & verbum Restituas lege inuenitur, etsi non specialiter de fructibus additum est, tamen etiam fructus sunt restituendi. 2 ¶Vnicuique sua {g} mora nocet {h}, quod & in duobus reis {i} promittendis obseruatur. 3 ¶Dolo facit, qui {l} petit, quod redditurus est {m}.
units.tr: In the condemnation of persons who are condemned only to the extent of what they can do, not all that they have is to be extorted; their circumstances must also be taken into account, lest they be left in want. (1) Since the word "restore" is found in the law, even though fruits were not specially added, fruits too must be restored. (2) Each person's delay harms only himself, which is also observed in the case of two defendants promising. (3) He acts with deceit who demands what he is himself about to return.
174. The same, book 8, to Plautius.

units.la: QVi potest facere, vt possit condicioni parere, posse videtur. 1 ¶Quod quis, si velit, habere non potest {o}: id repudiare non {p} potest.
units.tr: He who can bring it about that he is able to comply with a condition is considered able to do so. (1) What someone cannot have even if he wishes, he cannot renounce.
175. The same, book 11, to Plautius.

units.la: IN his, quae officium per liberas fieri personas leges desiderant, seruus {q} interuenire non potest. 1 ¶Non debeo melioris condicionis esse, quam auctor {r} meus, à quo ius in me transit.
units.tr: In those matters which the laws require to be done by free persons, a slave cannot intervene. (1) I ought not to be in a better position than my author, from whom the right passes to me.

units.la: {c} si id interpretatio ferre potest, quid enim si impugnet testatoris voluntatem? l.7.§.de vulg.quid si necessariis destituatur? l.2.§.L.§.de dolo except.
units.tr: {c} If the interpretation can bear it; for what if it opposes the will of the testator? l.7 §de vulg.; what if he is left without necessary persons? l.2 §L. §de dolo except.
{d} l.20 §eod.; l.12 §soluto; l.6 §de re iudicata. 2. Ecloga, 3, c. 169.
{e} l.30 §de re iudicata.
{f} See l.38 §4 §de usuris; l.75 §de verbor. significat. 2. Ecloga, 3, c. 169.

units.la: {g} vide l.134.in fi. supra eod: c. mora sua cuilibet est nociua 25.de regulis in 6: l.5.supra de reb.cred. l.12. in sin.supra depositi: l.3.in fi.§.de actionib.empt: l.32.§.3.§.de vsuris: l.14. §.de iure dotium: l.39. §.1. verfic.ipsum: l.47.in fine,§.de legatis 1: l.78.in principio & §.2: l.84. §.de legat.2: l.18. §. ad Trebellian: l. 12. §. de aqua plunia.
units.tr: {g} See l. 134 in fin., above in the same title; c. "Mora sua cuilibet est nociva", 25, On the Rules of Law in the Sixth Book (de regulis iuris in VI); l. 5, above, On Things Lent; l. 12 in sin., above, On Deposit; l. 3 in fin. §, On Actions of Purchase and Sale (de actionibus empti); l. 32 §3, On Usury (de usuris); l. 14 §, On the Law of Dowries (de iure dotium); l. 39 §1, verse "Ipsum"; l. 47 in fine, §, On Legacies, 1; l. 78 in principio and §2; l. 84 §, On Legacies, 2; l. 18 §, on the Trebellianic (ad Trebellianum); l. 12 §, On Rain Water (de aqua pluvia).

units.la: {h} nocet tamen mora rei fideiussori l. 88. §. de verbarum obligatione.
units.tr: {h} Yet the delay of the principal debtor harms the surety: l.88 §de verborum obligatione.
{i} l.32 §4 §de usuris.

units.la: {k} vide tamen l. penultimam §. de duobus reis.
units.tr: {k} But see the last but one l. §de duobus reis.

units.la: {l} c. dolo facit 59. de regulis in 6: l. 8. supra de doli exceptione.
units.tr: {l} Whoever acts with fraud [is treated as having done it]: c. dolo facit 59. de regulis in 6; l. 8, supra de doli exceptione.

units.la: {m} eidem à quo petit, non alij l.44. in fine, §.soluto. sed nec ex interdicto recuperandæ vide l.14. Codice de agricolis & censitis.
units.tr: {m} To the same person from whom he demands, not to another: l.44 in fine §soluto. But neither by the interdict for recovering...; see l.14 Codex de agricolis et censitis.

units.la: {o} Quod non potest haberi, repudiari non potest l.18. §. de acquirend. hereditas.
units.tr: {o} What cannot be had cannot be renounced: l.18 §de acquirenda hereditate.

units.la: {p} repudiatio est quaedam priuatio, quae subiectum aliquod praesupponit l. 8. §. 2. §. de optione: l. 59. §.6. in fine, §. de haereditat. insiti: vide l.3. supra eodem.
units.tr: {p} Renunciation is a certain privation, which presupposes some subject: l.8 §2 §de optione; l.59 §6 in fine §de hereditatibus instituendis; see l.3 supra eodem.
{q} See l.22 §eodem.

units.la: {r} vide l.120; l.160. in f. §. eodem.
units.tr: {r} See l.120; l.160 in fin. §eodem.
176. The same, in book thirteen to Plautius.

units.la: Non est singulis concedendum , quod per magistratum publicè possit fieri: ne occasio sit magistratus tumultus faciendi. 1 ¶Infinita æstimatio est libertatis , & necessitudinis .
units.tr: It must not be granted to individuals what can be done publicly through the magistrate, lest there be an occasion for the magistrate to stir up tumult. 1 ¶ The value of liberty and of close kinship is beyond estimation.
177. The same, in book fourteen to Plautius.

units.la: Qvi in ius, dominium vel alterius succedit, iure eius vti debet. 1 ¶Nemo videtur dolo facere, qui ignorat causam, cur non debeat petere.
units.tr: One who succeeds another in right or ownership must use that person's right. 1 ¶ No one is thought to act by fraud who does not know the reason why he ought not to seek.
178. The same, in book fifteen to Plautius.

units.la: Cvm principalis causa non consistat: plerumque ne ea quidem, quæ sequuntur, locum habent.
units.tr: Since the principal cause does not stand, most often not even those things that follow from it have any effect.
179. The same, in book sixteen to Plautius.

units.la: IN obscura voluntate manumittentis fauendum est libertati .
units.tr: Where the will of the one manumitting is unclear, one must favour liberty.

units.la: 180. Idem ‖ libro septimo decimo ad Plautium.
units.tr: 180. The same, in book seventeen to Plautius.

units.la: Qvod iussu alterius soluitur: pro eo est, quasi ipsi solutum esset:
units.tr: What is released by another's command is treated as if it had been released by the person himself.
181. The same, in book one to Vitellius.

units.la: SI nemo subiit hereditatem, omnis vis testamenti soluitur .
units.tr: If no one has entered upon the inheritance, all force of the testament is dissolved.
182. The same, in book three to Vitellius.

units.la: Qvod nullius esse potest: id vt alicuius fieret, nulla obligatio valet efficere.
units.tr: What cannot belong to anyone, no obligation can make belong to someone.
183. Marcellus, in book three of the Digest.

units.la: ETsi nihil facilè mutandum est ex solennibus: tamen, vbi æquitas euidens poscit, subuenien-dum est.
units.tr: Although nothing should easily be changed in solemn forms, yet where evident equity demands it, help must be given.
184. Celsus, in book seven of the Digest.

units.la: ℓ & res ad intestati causam redit d.§.xl.89.§.eod:l.9. §.de testamen.tut:l.10.§.4.in fi l.38.in f.§.de vulgari nisi heredes pro adita habeant, & nisi testator pro adita esse velit,qd sæpissimè euenit propter codicillos vel similes clausulas.
units.tr: And the matter returns to the cause of intestacy (see the citations: the law of § 40 and § 89, and § eod.; law 9 § de testamentis tutelaris; law 10 § 4 in fine; law 38 in fine § de vulgari), unless the heirs have accepted the inheritance, and unless the testator wishes it to be accepted, which very often happens on account of codicils or similar clauses.
I have spoken elsewhere about equity.

units.la: Vani{a} timoris iusta excusatio non est.
units.tr: A groundless fear is not a just excuse.
There is no obligation to impossible things.

units.la: Nihil peti potest ante{e} id tempus, quo per rerum naturam persolui possit. Et cùm soluendi tempus obligationi additur: nisi{d} eo praeterito, peti non potest.
units.tr: Nothing can be demanded before the time when it can be paid according to the nature of things. And when a time of payment is added to an obligation, it cannot be demanded until that time has passed.

units.la: SI quis praegnatem{c} vxorem reliquit, non videtur sine{f} liberis decessisse.
units.tr: If anyone has left a pregnant wife, he is not considered to have died without children.

units.la: VBi pugnantia{g} inter se in testamento iuberentur, neutrum ratum est. ¶ Quae rerum na-ra prohibentur{h}, nulla lege confirmata sunt.
units.tr: Where contrary provisions are ordered among themselves in a testament, neither is valid. What is prohibited by the nature of things is not confirmed by any law.

units.la: PUpillus{i} nec velle{k}, nec nolle in ea aetate, nisi adposita tutoris auctoritate, creditur: nam quod animi iudicio fit, in eo tutoris auctoritas neces-saria est.
units.tr: A pupil is not believed to be able to will or refuse at that age unless the authority of the guardian is added; for in what is done by the judgement of the mind, the guardian's authority is necessary.

units.la: QUod euincitur{c} in bonis{m} non{n} est.
units.tr: What is evicted is not among the goods.

units.la: NEratius consultus, an quod beneficium{l} dare se quasi viuenti Caesar rescripserat, iam{o} defuncto dedisse existimaretur, respondit, non videri sibi principem, quod ei, quem viuere existimabat, concessisset, defuncto concessisse. quem tamen modum esse beneficij sui vellet, ipsius{p} aestimationem esse.
units.tr: Neratius was asked whether what Caesar had rescripted as a grant to one living would be thought to have been given to one already dead. He answered that the emperor did not seem to him to have granted to a dead man what he had granted to one whom he believed to be alive. Yet, he said, the measure of his benefit was the emperor's own estimation.
{g} See Eclogue book 2, chapter 3, on 184; law 16 § de conditionibus; Institutes; law 13 § 3; law 27 § de rebus dubiis; see also law 14 Code, de fide instrumentorum.
{h} See law 185 § same; add law 12 § 2 § de captivis; the Eclogue in the same place.
{i} Law 43 § de obligationibus; the Eclogue in the same place, chapter 185.
{k} See law 2 § 19 § ut bonorum.

units.la: {l} l.52.supra de acquiren.rer.dom: l.25.§.de verborum significatione.
units.tr: {l} Law 52 supra de acquirendo rerum dominio; law 25 § de verborum significatione.
{m} See law 49 § de verborum significatione.

units.la: {n} Imo est v.l.15.§.6. supra qui satisdare.
units.tr: {n} Indeed it is; see law 15 § 6 supra qui satisdare.

units.la: {o} Priuilegium alicui datum tanquam viuenti, ei mortuo non competit, id est, ad heredes non extenditur Ecloga ibidem c.187. facit lex 2. supra quae sententia fine appellatione.
units.tr: {o} A privilege given to someone as to one living does not pass to him once dead; that is, it is not extended to his heirs. The Eclogue in the same place, chapter 187. Compare law 2 supra quae sententia sine appellatione.

units.la: {p} Interpretatio priuilegij, vel beneficij, spectat ad principem qui concessit l.43.§.de vulgari.Ecl.ib.
units.tr: {p} The interpretation of a privilege or benefit belongs to the prince who granted it; law 43 § de vulgari. The Eclogue in the same place.
192. Marcellus ‖ in book twenty-nine of the Digest. ‖

units.la: EA,quæ in partes dividi non possunt{4}, solida {b} à singulis heredibus debentur. ¹ ¶ In rei dubia benignior {c} interpretationem sequi, non minus iustius est, quàm tutius.
units.tr: These things which cannot be divided into parts are owed in full by the individual heirs. In a doubtful matter, to follow the more favourable interpretation is no less just than it is safe.
193. Celsus ‖ in book thirty-eight of the Digest. ‖

units.la: OMnia fere iura heredum perinde habentur, ac ii continuo{d} sub tempus mortis heredes ex-stitissent.
units.tr: Almost all the rights of heirs are held as if those heirs had come into being immediately at the time of death.
194. Modestinus ‖ in book six of Differences ‖

units.la: QUi per successionem quamuis longissimam{c} defuncto heredes constituerunt, non minus heredes intelliguntur, quàm qui principaliter heredes existunt.
units.tr: Those who have appointed heirs to the deceased through a succession, however remote, are understood to be heirs no less than those who are heirs in the first place.
195. Idem ‖ in book seven of Differences. ‖

units.la: EXpressa nocent{f}, non expressa non nocent.
units.tr: Things expressed do harm; things not expressed do no harm.
196. Idem ‖ in book eight of Rules. ‖

units.la: PRivilegia quædam causæ sunt, quædam personæ: & ideo quædam ad hæredem transmittuntur{e}, quæ causæ{g} sunt, quæ personæ{h} sunt, ad heredem non transeunt.
units.tr: Some privileges belong to the cause, others to the person; so those that belong to the cause pass to the heir, while those that belong to the person do not pass to the heir.
197. Idem ‖ in the single book on the rite of marriage. ‖

units.la: SEmper in coniunctionibus{i} non solùm quid
units.tr: In conjunctions one must always consider not only what is said but also what is implied.

units.la: {f} l.77.§.ro: l.77.in f.§. de condict.[?]& demonstr: interdum vero magis probant quam tacita de quibus v.Decium hic.
units.tr: {f} See law 77 § ro; law 77 in fine § de condictione and demonstratione; sometimes indeed they prove more than tacit ones, on which see Decius here.
{g} [illegible, about twenty letters] Eclogue book 2, chapter 3, on 191.
{h} See law 68 § Code.

units.la: {i} [illegible, ~20 letters] 2.Eclog.3.cap.195. in conventionibus Haloand, contradictibus Dynus. liceat, considerandum est: sed & quid hore-ftum{a} [?]sit.
units.tr: {i} [illegible, about twenty letters] Eclogue book 2, chapter 3, on 195. In conventionibus (Haloander), contradictibus (Dynus). It must be considered whether it is permitted; but also what is hereditary.
198. Iavolenus, in book thirteen from Cassius.

units.la: NEque in interdicto{b}, neque in cæteris causis pupillo nocere oportet dolū{c} tutoris: siue{d} soluendo est, siue non est.
units.tr: Neither in an interdict nor in other causes ought the fraud of a guardian to harm the pupil, whether the guardian is solvent or not.
199. The same, in the sixth book of Epistles.

units.la: NOn potest dolo carere, qui imperio magistratus non{e} paruit.
units.tr: He cannot be free of fraud who has not obeyed the command of the magistrate.
200. The same, in the seventh book of Epistles.

units.la: QVotiens nihil sine{f} captione inuestigari{g} po-teft: eligendum est, quod minimum{h} habeat iniquitatis.
units.tr: Whenever nothing can be investigated without deception, what has the least of injustice should be chosen.
201. The same, in the tenth book of Epistles.

units.la: OMnia, quæ ex testamento proficiscuntur, ita sta-tum euentus{i} capiunt, si initium{k} quoque si-ne vitio ceperint.
units.tr: All things that proceed from a will take on the outcome of their status, if they have also begun without fault.
202. The same, in the eleventh book of Epistles.

units.la: OMnis definitio{l} in iure ciuili periculosa est, pa-rum{m} est enim, vt non subuerti possit [?].
units.tr: Every definition in the civil law is dangerous, for it is seldom that it cannot be overturned.
203. Pomponius, in the eighth book on Quintus Mucius.

units.la: QVod quis ex culpa sua damnum{n} sentit, non [illegible, ~8 letters]bus malis minus eligendum, Odia restringi{o}.
units.tr: That which someone suffers loss from his own fault, is to be chosen less than the evil ones; hatreds are restricted.
{i} i.e. the effect, [illegible Greek] 2. Ecl. 3. c. 197.

units.la: {l} l. 29: l. 178. supra eo: l. 210. §. co: v. l. 1. supra de regul. Catoniana. {m} l. 1. supra eo: adde l. 32. §. eo: [?]
units.tr: {l} l. 29; l. 178, above on that; l. 210, §. co; cf. l. 1, above on the Catonian rule. {m} l. 1, above on that; add l. 32, §. on that; [?]

units.la: {n} c. damnum 86: de regulis, in 6. ö [illegible, Greek]. Ecl. ib. c. 199: l. 46. §. 5. supra de procurat: l. 9. in f. l. 17 in f. princip. §. de noxalibus: l. 44. §. 3. supra familia: l. 15. supra qui omissa causa. Intelligitur damnum sentire{4}.
units.tr: {n} c. damnum 86: on the rules, in 6; [illegible Greek]. Ecl. ib. c. 199: l. 46, §. 5, above on the procurator; l. 9, in fine; l. 17, in fine, principium, §. on noxal actions; l. 44, §. 3, above on the household; l. 15, above on those who omit the case. It is understood to suffer loss.
204. The same, in the twenty-eighth book on Quintus Mucius.

units.la: Minus{b} est actionem habere, quam rem.
units.tr: It is less to have an action than to have a thing.
205. The same, in the thirty-ninth book on Quintus Mucius.

units.la: Plerumque fit, ut etiam ea, quae{c} nobis abire possint, proinde{d} in eo statu sint, atque si non essent eius condicionis, ut abire possent. & ideo, quod fisco obligamus, & vindicare{e} interdum, & alienare, & seruitutem [in]praedio imponere possumus.
units.tr: It often happens that even those things which can be taken from us are in the same state as if they were not of such a condition that they could be taken away. And therefore, what we pledge to the treasury, we can sometimes also vindicate, alienate, and impose a servitude on a country estate.

units.la: 206. Idem libro nono ex variis lectionibus.
units.tr: 206. The same, in the ninth book, from Various Readings.

units.la: Iure naturæ{f} æquum est, neminem cum alterius detrimento{g} & iniuria fieri locupletiorem{h}.
units.tr: By the law of nature it is fair that no one be made richer to the detriment and injury of another.

units.la: 207. Vlpianus libro 1. ad legem Iuliam & Papiam.
units.tr: 207. Ulpian, in the first book on the Julian and Papian law.
A judged matter is taken as truth.

units.la: 208. Paulus libro 3. ad legem Iuliam & Papiam.
units.tr: 208. Paul, in the third book on the Julian and Papian law.

units.la: Non potest videri defisse habere, qui{l} num-quam habuit.
units.tr: He cannot be seen to have ceased to have what he never had.

units.la: 48. de regulis in 6: l.16. §. de seruitut. rustic: l.13. §.1. supra communia prædiorum: l.17. §.4. in fine, supra de instit: l.12. §.1. supra de distract.pign: l.2. §.10. {h} ideo nequid in loco publico.
units.tr: 48. on the rules in 6: l. 16, §. on rustic servitudes; l. 13, §. 1, above on common property of estates; l. 17, §. 4, in fine, above on the Institutes; l. 12, §. 1, above on sale of pledges; l. 2, §. 10. {h} therefore nothing in a public place.

units.la: {h} ideo minor obligatur quatenus ... cessat in vsucapionibus l.1. de vsurp. & quoties vtilitas publica requirit vsum, & tamen non iniquum rei priuatæ, l.15. §.2. §. de rei vindic. l.13. §.comm.præd. l.11. §. de seruitut. {i} l.25. in §.§. de statu l.8. l.174. §. eo: defisse non videtur, quod nec incepit l.5. supra de iniust. & l.96 in princ. & §.1. §. de condic. & demonstr. l.13. §. de iuris l.16. supra de verbor. obligat: l.19. §. quemadmod. seruitutes amittuntur.
units.tr: {h} therefore the lesser is bound as far as ... it ceases in usucapions, l. 1, on usurpation; and whenever public utility requires use, and yet it is not unjust to a private thing, l. 15, §. 2, on vindication of a thing; l. 13, on common estates; l. 11, §. on servitudes. {i} l. 25, in §§. on status; l. 8; l. 174, §. on that: it is not seen to have ceased, which never began; l. 5, above on unjust things; and l. 96, in principium and §. 1, on conditions and demonstrations; l. 13, §. on law; l. 16, above on the obligation of words; l. 19, §. how servitudes are lost.
209. Ulpian, in the fourth book on the Julian and Papian law.
We liken a servitude almost to mortality.
210. Licinius Rufinus, in the second book of Rules.

units.la: Qux ab initio{c} inutilis fuit institutio, ex postfacto{d} conualescere non potest.
units.tr: An institution which was useless from the beginning cannot recover afterwards from a later event.
211. Paul, in the sixty-ninth book on the Edict.

units.la: Seruus{e} reipublicæ causa abesse non potest.
units.tr: A slave cannot be absent for the sake of the commonwealth.
THE END.

VII.

units.la: Priuilegium personale, personam sequitur, extinguitur cum persona.
units.tr: A personal privilege follows the person and is extinguished with the person.
VIII.

units.la: Semel malus, semper præsumitur esse malus.
units.tr: Once bad, one is always presumed to be bad.
IX.

units.la: Ratum quis habere non potest, quod ipsius nomine non est gestum.
units.tr: One cannot ratify what has not been done in one's name.

units.la: Canones intelligi per excellentiam, Canones sacra scriptura comprehensos. Est enim scriptura omnium Canonum, κανὼν. Paul. ad Galat. vlt. vers. 16. ad Philipp. 3. vers. 16. ad Corinth. 10. vers. 15.
units.tr: The canons are understood by excellence as the canons contained in Holy Scripture, for Scripture is the rule [κανών] of all canons. See Gal., last chapter, v. 16; Phil. 3, v. 16; 1 Cor. 10, v. 15.

Cod. de præscript. 3 .annor. §. v. l. 3. ff. de usurpat. {h} Imò, vt fiat restitutio, non dimittitur v. l. 34. §. 3 v. l. 65. ff. de furtis. l. 5 ff. vi bonorum. {i} Imò, ne correcto quidem d. §. 3 d. l. 55: d. l. 5: l. 7. §. 25 ff. de pœnis l. 17. §. 1 ff. de ædilitio: l. 3. Cod. de praescript. 30 years; l. 3 ff. de usurpat. {h} Indeed, for restitution to take place, it is not forgiven: see l. 34 §. 3 and l. 65 ff. de furtis; l. 5 ff. vi bonorum. {i} Indeed, not even to one who has amended: see d. §. 3, d. l. 55; d. l. 5; l. 7 §. 25 ff. de poenis; l. 17 §. 1 ff. de aedilitio; l. 3 Cod. de apostatis. {k} See l. 185 ff. eod.; l. 35 ff. de verb. oblig.; §. 11 Inst. de inutilibus stipulationibus; add l. 4 ff. de condictione indebiti. {l} See l. 35 ff. soluto matrimonio; see l. 24 and d. l. 25 ff. de re iudicata. {m} I have said at l. 7 §. 1 ff. de accusationibus; add l. 5 §. 5 at the end, ff. de re militari. {n} I have said on l. 64 below, ff. eod.

units.la: X. Ratihabitationem {a}retrorahi {b}& mandato non est dubium comparari {c}.
units.tr: X. Ratification is held to reach back in time, and is undoubtedly equivalent to a mandate.

units.la: XI. Cum sunt partium iura obscura, reo favendum est potius quam actori.
units.tr: XI. When the rights of the parties are unclear, the defendant is to be favoured rather than the plaintiff.

units.la: XII. In iudiciis non est acceptio {f}personarum habenda.
units.tr: XII. In judgments, the acceptance of persons is not to be taken into account.
XIII. Ignorance of fact, not ignorance of law, excuses.

units.la: XIIII. Cum quis in ius succedit {g}alterius, iustam ignorantiam causam censetur habere.
units.tr: XIIII. When someone succeeds to another's right, he is considered to have a just cause of ignorance.
XV. Penalties are to be restricted, and favours are fitting to be extended.

units.la: XVI. Decet concessum a principe beneficium esse man-surum {k}[?].
units.tr: XVI. A benefice granted by the prince ought to be lasting [?].

units.la: XVII. Indultum a iure beneficium non est alicui ause-rendum {l}.
units.tr: XVII. A benefice granted by law is not to be taken away from anyone.

units.la: XVIII. Non firmatur {m}tractu temporis, quod de iure ab initio non subsistit.
units.tr: XVIII. What did not subsist by law from the beginning is not confirmed by the passage of time.

units.la: XIX. Non est siue culpa qui rei quae ad eum non {n}per-tinet se immiscet.
units.tr: XIX. He who meddles in a matter that does not pertain to him is not without fault.
XX. No one is forbidden to use several defences.

units.la: XXI. Quod semel {p}placuit, amplius displicere non potest.
units.tr: XXI. What has once pleased cannot afterwards displease.

units.la: XXII. Non debet aliquis alterius {q}odio praegrauari.
units.tr: XXII. No one ought to be burdened by another's hatred.

units.la: XXIII. Sine {r}culpa (nisi subsit causa) non est aliquis puniendus.
units.tr: XXIII. Without fault (unless some cause lies behind it), no one is to be punished.

Where there is harm, there is a penalty, l. 22 Cod. de poenis; where there is no offence, no penalty is to be imposed.
XXIIII.

units.la: Quod quis mandato{a} iudicis, facit dolo facere non{b} videtur, cum habeat parere necesse.
units.tr: One who does something by the command of a judge is not seen to act with fraud, since he must of necessity obey.
XXV.
One's own delay is harmful to anyone.
XXVI.

units.la: Ea quæ fiunt à iudice, si ad eius non spectant officium{d}, viribus non subsistunt.
units.tr: Things done by a judge, if they do not fall within his office, do not stand by their own force.
XXVII.

units.la: Scienti{e} & consentienti non fit iniuria neque dolus.
units.tr: No injury or fraud is done to one who knows and consents.
XXVIII.

units.la: Quæ à iure communi{f} exorbitant, nequaquam ad consequentiam sunt trahenda.
units.tr: Things that depart from common law must by no means be drawn into precedent.
XXIX.

units.la: Quod omnes tangit, debet{g} ab omnibus approbari.
units.tr: What touches all ought to be approved by all.
XXX.
In obscure matters the least is to be followed.
XXXI.

units.la: Eum qui certus est certiorari{i} ulterius non oportet.
units.tr: One who is certain need not be informed any further.
XXXII.

units.la: Non{k} licet actori quod reo licitum non exsistit.
units.tr: What is not allowed to the defendant is not allowed to the plaintiff either.
XXXIII.

units.la: Mutare{l} consilium quis non potest in alterius detrimentum.
units.tr: One cannot change his decision to another's detriment.
XXXIIII.
The general is derogated by the specific.
XXXV.

units.la: Plus{n} semper in se continet, quod est minus.
units.tr: The greater always contains the less.
XXXVI.

units.la: Pro possessore habetur qui dolo{o} desiit possidere.
units.tr: He is held to be a possessor who has ceased to possess through fraud.
XXXVII.

units.la: Utile non debet per inutile{p} vitiari.
units.tr: What is useful must not be vitiated by what is useless.
{e} See l. 145 ff. eod.
{f} See l. 141 ff. eod.; l. 14, l. 15, l. 16 ff. de legibus.
{g} l. 11 ff. de servitutibus rusticorum; l. ult. ff. communia praediorum.

units.tr: {k} See l. 41 ff. eod. Even less is it permitted to the plaintiff than to the defendant: l. ult. ff. de feriis.
{l} See l. 21 §. 3 eod.; l. 75 ff. eod.
{m} See l. 8 [?] ff. eo.
{n} See l. 110 ff. eo.

units.tr: {p} l. 20 ff. de usuris. Compare l. 9, l. 29 ff. of the same title; l. 61 ff. de iure dotium; l. 1 §. 3 ff. quod falso; l. 4 §. 5 at the end, l. 65 ff. de verborum obligationibus; l. 34 §. 2 Cod. de donationibus.

units.la: XXXVIII. Ex eo non debet quis fructus consequi quod ni-sus extitit impugnare {a}.
units.tr: XXXVIII. One ought not to obtain the fruits of that which he has laboured to impugn.

units.la: XXXIX. Cum quid prohibetur, prohibentur omnia quae sequuntur {b} ex illo.
units.tr: XXXIX. When something is prohibited, all the things that follow from it are prohibited.

units.la: XL. Pluralis locutio, duorum {c} numero est contenta.
units.tr: XL. Plural speech is confined to the number two.

units.la: XLI. Imputari non debet eiper {d} quem non stat, si non faciat quod per eum fuerat faciendum.
units.tr: XLI. That should not be imputed to one whom it does not concern, if he does not do what was to be done through him.

units.la: XLII. Accestorium {e} naturam sequi congruit principalis.
units.tr: XLII. It is fitting that an accessory follow the nature of its principal.
XLIII. He who keeps silent seems to consent.

units.la: XLIIII. Is qui tacet non fatetur, sed nec utique negare videtur {g}.
units.tr: XLIIII. He who keeps silent does not confess, but neither is he seen to deny.

units.la: XLV. Inspicimus in obscuris, quod est verisimilius {h}, vel quod plerumque fieri consueuit {i}.
units.tr: XLV. In obscure matters we look to what is more probable, or to what usually happens.

units.la: XLVI. Is qui in ius succedit {k} alterius, eo iure quo ille vti debebit.
units.tr: XLVI. He who succeeds to another's right is bound by the law under which that other would have been bound to act.

units.la: XLVII. Præsumitur ignorantia {l}, ubi scientia non probatur.
units.tr: XLVII. Ignorance is presumed where knowledge is not proved.

units.la: {d} l.8.§.7. ff.de condicionib.instit: v. l.38. ff.locati: l.1.l.2.l.3.l.4. ff.de peculio legat: facit l.61.l.173.§.2.l.174.ff.de regul.iur.

units.la: {g} Taciturnitas & patientia medium quoddam est inter consensum & dissensum obligandi. obligatur qui literas acceptat, nec contradicit l.26.§.1.ff.de pignorib: qui non prohibet cum possit prohibere l. 60. ff.de regul. iur: qui sibi credi patitur l.18.ff.mandati: adde l.28. ff.communi divid: l.38.in f.ff.de donat.inter virum. dixi ad l.3. ff.de regulis.
units.tr: {g} Silence and patience are a kind of middle ground between consent and dissent for the purposes of obligation. One who accepts a letter and does not contradict is bound: l. 26 §. 1 ff. de pignoribus; one who does not forbid when he could forbid: l. 60 ff. de regulis iuris; one who allows himself to be trusted: l. 18 ff. mandati. Add l. 28 ff. communi dividundo; l. 38 at the end ff. de donationibus inter virum et uxorem. I have said on l. 3 ff. de regulis.

units.la: {h} verisimilitudo colligitur ex consuetis.eod: colligitur etiam ex adiuncti comparatione l.1.in f.l.7.§.2.ff.de reb.dub.& aliis coniecturis l. 50 in f.ff. de leg.: adde l.34.l.67.l.46.ff.de regul.iur l. 219.ff.de verb.signif.
units.tr: {h} Probability is gathered from what is customary, eod.; it is also gathered from comparison with the attendant circumstances, l. 1 at the end, l. 7 §. 2 ff. de rebus dubiis, and from other conjectures, l. 50 at the end ff. de legatis. Add l. 34, l. 67, l. 46 ff. de regulis iuris; l. 219 ff. de verborum significatione.
{i} See l. 34 ff. eo. See altogether l. 50 at the end ff. de legatis 1.
{k} l. 143; see l. 15 §. 3, l. 175 at the end, l. 177 ff. eo.

units.la: {l} facti sc. alieni praesertim, non iuris. nam quilibet praesumitur scire iura l.2.ff.confessis.l.9 Co.de legibus. Propterea iuris error non praesumitur nisi probetur l. 68. in f.ff.ad Treb. {z} Alciatum 3.praesumpt. 31.
units.tr: {l} Of fact, namely of another's fact especially, not of law: for everyone is presumed to know the law, l. 2 ff. confessis; l. 9 Cod. de legibus. Therefore an error of law is not presumed unless it is proved, l. 68 at the end ff. ad Trebellianum. {z} Alciatus, 3 praesumpt. 31.
XLVIII.

units.la: Locupletari {a}non debet, aliquis cum {b}alterius iniuria vel iactura.
units.tr: One ought not to be enriched at another's injury or loss.
XLIX.
In penal matters the more lenient interpretation is to be made.
L.

units.la: Actus legitimi {d}conditione non recipiunt neque diem.
units.tr: Legal acts admit neither a condition nor a day.
LI.

units.la: Semel Deo dicatum,non {e}est ad vsus humanos vl terius transferendum.
units.tr: What has once been dedicated to God must not be transferred to human uses, or to anything else.
LII.

units.la: Non praestat impedimentum,quod de iure non fit, vt effectum {f}.
units.tr: An impediment which is not created by law does not prevent the effect.
LIII.

units.la: Cui licet,quod est plus, licet {g}vtique quod est minus.
units.tr: One to whom what is greater is permitted is certainly permitted what is less.
LIIII.
He who is first in time is stronger in law.
LV.

units.la: Qui sentit onus {i}, sentire debet commodum, & contra.
units.tr: He who feels the burden ought to feel the benefit, and conversely.
LVI.

units.la: In re communi, potior est conditio prohibetis {k}.
units.tr: In a common thing, the condition of the one forbidding is the stronger.
LVII.

units.la: Contra eum {l}qui legem dicere potuit apertius est interpretatio facienda {m}.
units.tr: Where a man could have stated the law more plainly, the interpretation is to be made against him.
LVIII.

units.la: Non est obligatorium contra {n}bonos mores prę stitum iuramentum {o}.
units.tr: An oath sworn against good morals is not binding.
LIX.

units.la: Dolo {p}facit qui petit,quod restituere oportet eudem.
units.tr: He acts by fraud who demands what he ought to restore to the same person.
LX.

units.la: Non est in mora {q}qui potest exceptione legitima se tueri.
units.tr: He is not in default who can protect himself by a lawful exception.

units.la: LXI. Quod ob gratiam alicuius conceditur, non est in eius dispendium retorquendum.
units.tr: LXI. What is conceded for the sake of someone's favour must not be turned to that person's loss.

units.la: LXII. Nullus ex consilio (dummodo fraudulentū non fuerit) obligatur.
units.tr: LXII. No one is bound by advice (provided it was not fraudulent).

units.la: LXIII. Exceptionem obiiciens non videtur de intentione aduersarij confiteri.
units.tr: LXIII. One who raises an exception does not seem to admit the opposing party's claim.

units.la: LXIIII. Quæ contra ius fiunt domini, vbique pro infesis haberi.
units.tr: LXIV. Whatever is done contrary to the law of the lord is everywhere held to be void.

units.la: LXV. In parif, delicto vel causa, potior est condicio possidentis .
units.tr: LXV. Where the fault or the cause is equal on both sides, the condition of the possessor is the stronger.

units.la: LXVI. Cum non stat per eum ad quem pertinet quominus conditio impleatur, haberi debet perinde ac si impleta fuisset.
units.tr: LXVI. When the condition is not fulfilled through the fault of the person to whom it pertains, it must be held as if it had been fulfilled.

units.la: LXVII. Quod alicui suo non licet nomine, nec alieno licebit.
units.tr: LXVII. What is not lawful for someone in his own name will not be lawful in another's name either.

units.la: LXVIII. Potest quis per alium, quod potest facere per seipsum.
units.tr: LXVIII. One may do through another what he can do himself.

units.la: LXIX. In malis promissis, fidem non expedit obseruari.
units.tr: LXIX. In bad promises, it is not expedient that good faith be kept.

units.la: LXX. In alternatiuis debitoris vbi est electio, sufficit alterum adimpleri.
units.tr: LXX. In alternative obligations of a debtor, where the choice lies with him, it is enough that one of the alternatives be performed.

units.la: LXXI. Qui ad agendum admittitur, est ad exceipiendū multo magis admittendus.
units.tr: LXXI. One who is admitted to bring an action is much more to be admitted to plead an exception.

units.la: LXXII. Qui facit per alium, est perinde ac si faciat per seipsum.
units.tr: LXXII. He who acts through another is just as if he acted in his own person.

units.la: LXXIII. Factum legitimè reuocari non debet, licèt {a}casus postea euenerit à quo potuit inchoari.
units.tr: LXXIII. A deed lawfully done must not be revoked, even if a chance event has occurred afterwards from which it could have begun.

units.la: LXXIIII. Quod alicui gratiosè concederitur, trahi non debet {b}ab aliis in exemplum.
units.tr: LXXIV. What is granted to someone as a favour must not be drawn by others as a precedent.

units.la: LXXV. Frustra sibi fidem {c}quis postulat ab eo seruari cui fidem à se praestitam seruare recusat.
units.tr: LXXV. A man asks in vain that good faith be kept toward him by one to whom he refuses to keep the good faith he has pledged.

units.la: LXXVI. Delictum personae {d}non {e}debet in detrimentum ecclesiae redundare.
units.tr: LXXVI. The fault of a person must not redound to the detriment of the Church.

units.la: LXXVII. Rationi congruit vt succedat in onere {f}quae sub-stituitur in honore.
units.tr: LXXVII. It accords with reason that one who is substituted in honour should succeed also in the burden.

units.la: LXXVIII. In argumentum {g}trahi nequeunt quę propter ne ceßitatem {h}aliquando sunt concessa.
units.tr: LXXVIII. Things conceded at some time on account of necessity cannot be drawn into argument.

units.la: LXXIX. Nemo potest plus {i}iuris transferre in alium quin sibi competere dinoscatur.
units.tr: LXXIX. No one can transfer more right to another than is recognised as belonging to himself.

units.la: LXXX. In toto {k}partem non est dubium contineri.
units.tr: LXXX. There is no doubt that a part is contained in the whole.

units.la: LXXXI. In generali concessione non veniunt ea quae quis non esset verisimiliter {l}in specie concessurus.
units.tr: LXXXI. In a general grant, those things are not included which the grantor would probably not have granted in particular.

units.la: LXXXII. Qui contra iura mercatur bonam {m}fidem præsumitur non habere.
units.tr: LXXXII. One who buys contrary to law is presumed not to have good faith.

units.la: LXXXIII. Bona fides non patitur vt semel exactum iterum {n}exigat.
units.tr: LXXXIII. Good faith does not allow that what has once been exacted be demanded again.

units.la: LXXXIIII. Cum quid vna via prohibet alicui,ad id alia {o}non debent admitti.
units.tr: LXXXIV. When something is forbidden to someone by one way, other ways must not be admitted to the same end.

units.la: LXXXV. Contractus {p}ex conuentione legem accipere dignoscuntur.
units.tr: LXXXV. Contracts are recognised as receiving their law from the agreement.

units.la: {n} Bona fides hic non exigit v.l.57.ff.eod. {o} v.c.39.§.eodem. {p} v.l.1.§.6.ff.depositi.l.58 ff.de verbor.obligat. Nequel.136.c.2.
units.tr: {n} Good faith does not require this here: v. l. 57 ff. eod. {o} v. c. 39 §. eodem. {p} v. l. 1 §. 6 ff. depositi; l. 58 ff. de verbor. obligat. Nor l. 136; c. 2.
LXXXVI.

units.la: Damnum quod quis sua {a}culpa sentit, sibi {b}debet non aliis imputare.
units.tr: Loss which a man suffers through his own fault must be imputed to himself and not to others.
LXXXVII.
Infamous persons do not have access to dignities.
LXXXVIII.

units.la: Certum est quod is committit in legē, qui {d}legis verba complectens contra legis nitítur voluntatem.
units.tr: It is certain that he commits an offence against the law who, while keeping to the words of the law, strives against the intention of the law.
{d} see l.5 Cod. de legib.

units.tr: Who may lawfully contract marriage, and in what manner, in pr. de nuptiis; and whether the consent of parents is required, in pr. Permitted: with the daughter of an adoptive sister, §.3, verse "eius vero"; between paternal and maternal cousins (patrueles, amitinos and amitinas), §.4; between stepchildren (compriuignos and compriuignas), §.8. On the contrary, forbidden between parents and children without limit, §.1. de nuptiis, including adoptive ones; d.§.1. Between brothers and sisters, including adoptive ones while the adoption lasts, §.2. A brother's or sister's daughter, granddaughter, great-granddaughter, etc.; with an adoptive aunt or great-aunt, §.5. On account of affinity: such as with a stepdaughter, daughter-in-law, §.6; mother-in-law and stepmother, §.7; a daughter by a wife, with another husband after divorce, §.8; with a father's betrothed or a son's betrothed, §.6. On account of servile kinships, §.10; and finally for other causes, §.11.

units.tr: Paternal power is dissolved: by the father's death, in pr., quibus modis ius patriae potestatis; by deportation to an island, §.1; by servitude as a penalty, §.3. On the other hand, it is not dissolved by the grandfather's death, in pr., quibus modis ius patriae potestatis. It is dissolved by relegation, §.2; by consular dignity, §.4; by Mitia, d. §.4; by captivity, if the man afterwards returns, §.5; by coerced emancipation, §.10; by condemnation to the mines, §.3; by exposure to wild beasts, d. §.3; by the highest dignity of patrician rank, §.4; by emancipation, §.6, of a grandson as well as of a son, §.7; by giving someone in adoption, §.8.
