Theophil. ditio loco l.io ff. de probat: l.64.ff. de adquir.rerum. {g} Dominus seruum testamento potest manumittere ff. de manumiss. testam: Codice de testam. manumiss. {h} Verba huius legis vide in titulo 11.§.14. infrà eodem: & in lege prima, ff. ad legem Falcidiam: lege 53. lege 120. ff. de verborum significationibus: in Nouell. 22. c. 2. v. etiam quædam, quæ ibidem dixi.
units.tr: Today, however, those manumitted are free by the law itself, through the tutor, and with the solemn words, even if they are not spoken, since they are taken as spoken (Digest, law 23, same title). Moreover, Theophilus thinks that this kind of manumission was named from this, that by it the slave is claimed into natural liberty (wrongly; for if it were so, those manumitted by census or will would also be said to be manumitted by the rod). Or it is named from a certain Vindex, who, though a slave, revealed by his information the conspiracy against the Romans, and was publicly manumitted by the Romans; and in his honour, whoever was manumitted before a magistrate was said to be manumitted by the rod. Theophilus, on Institutes, on freedmen, καὶ τῆς μὲν [and of the...]. Livy, book 2, does indeed mention the conspiracy detected by Vindex. It is also probable that manumission is called by the rod because the lictor placed a little rod on the slave being freed. Persius: "After I withdrew from the praetor, my rod..." and later: "not the rod which the lictor carries in an empty festuca." I mean the little rod which is called the vindicta; Boethius on the Topics; Plutarch, in On the Delay of Divine Justice, calls it the rod of liberty. Hence the phrase to impose the rod (vindictam imponere), in the Digest laws on manumissions, on the liberal and castrense peculium, and in the Code. [Here follows a long list of citations of the Digest and Code on the praetor, consul, proconsul, and the rod, with the observation that the municipal magistrates of cities that have this right also manumit by the rod, as do the prefect of Egypt, the legate of the proconsul, and even the emperor himself.]

units.la: Iunia {4},qua lege Latini {b} sunt nominati, inter amicos {c} manumissi.
units.tr: The Junian law, by which Latins were so named, provides for those manumitted among friends.

units.la: II Deditiorum {d} numero sunt, qui poenae {e} causa vincti sunt a domino {f}: quibus vestigia {g} scripta fuerunt: qui propter noxam torti nocentes tesque {h} inuenti sunt: quiue traditi sunt, vt ferro, aut cum bestiis depugnarent: vel in custodia {i} coniecti {k} fuerunt: deinde quoquo modo manumissi sunt: idque lex Aelia {l} Sentia facit.
units.tr: Among the dediticii are those who were bound by their master as punishment, on whom marks had been written; those who, tortured on account of a crime, were found guilty; or those who were handed over to fight with the sword or with beasts, or were thrown into custody; and then were manumitted in any way at all. The Aelian Sentian law provides this.

units.la: 12 Eadem lege {m} cautum est, vt {m} nor triginta annorum seruus {n} vindicta manumissus, ciuis Romanus non fiat, nisi apud consilium causa probata fuerit: ideo sine consilio manumissum seruum manere putat. Testamento vero manumissum perinde habere iubet, atque si domini voluntate in libertate esset, ideoque Latinus fit.
units.tr: 12 By the same law it is provided that a slave not younger than thirty years, manumitted by vindicta, does not become a Roman citizen unless the cause has been approved before the council. Hence he thinks a slave manumitted without the council remains a slave. But one manumitted by will he orders to be treated just as if he were free by the master's wish, and so he becomes a Latin.

units.la: 13 Eadem lex eum {o} dominum qui minor viginti annorum est, prohibet seruum manumittere, terquam si causam apud consilium probauerit. In consilium {p} autem adhibentur {q} Romae qui nunc adhibitione manumittebantur, vide Caium r. §.2. Hosce manumittendi modos Theophilus dicto § [illegible, ~12 letters] appellat [?] quibus opponit dicto loco [illegible, ~10 letters] {d} v. Cod. de dedititia libert. {e} nam fugitiuos solebant plerunque poenae causa notis compungere. {f} l.43.ff.de fideicommiss. liber. vel alio, eius iussu aut ratihabitione Paulus 4.sent.12.§.8. Aliud si ab hac rede Paulus 4.sent.12.§.4. Quid si a communi domino {v}. Paul. ibidem §.5. quid si a creditore? sunt quoque Paul. ibidem §.6. Quid si domini furiosi aut pupilli iussu? Non fient dedititij Paulus ibidem §.7. {g} [illegible, ~10 letters] Theophilus §. Inst. de libertis: vide Caium 1.§.1. {h} aliud si innocentes Paulus 4.sent.12.§.3. {i} publicam scilicet, Theophilus ibidem, aliás, priuatus carcer non impediret, nisi vincula fuissent iniecta l. 216.ff.de verb.signif. {k} non idem fuit, si dominus seruum ab honore ministrandi vel administrandi remouisset l.51. in f.ff.de manumiss.testam. {l} §.3. Inst. de libert. {m} Sentia §.11. in f. s. codem. {n} Ita etiam manumittitur, Cum ad statutam aetatem peruenerit l.vlt.ff.de rebus dubijs, i. Cum seruus erit 30. annorum, liber esto, l.39.§.2.ff.familiae l.46.ff.de manumiss.testament. l.13.§.5.ff.de statul. {o} §.4. Inst. quibus ex cauf. manumitt. {p} Theophilus Inst. quib. ex cauf. manumiss. Consilium definiuit [illegible, ~8 letters] seu consessum spectabilium virorum statis diebus coeuntium. Consilium autem hic intellige, Praetoris, Romae: Praesidum, & proconsulis in prouinciis Theophil. d. loco. {q} a Praetore sc.
units.tr: 13 The same law forbids a master who is under twenty years of age to manumit a slave, unless he has proved the cause before the council. Those who are brought in to the council at Rome are the ones who were then manumitted by the hand of the praetor. See Gaius r. §2. Theophilus, in the said §, calls these modes of manumission [illegible], and opposes them in the said place [illegible]. See Cod. de dedititia libert. For fugitives were usually branded with marks as a punishment. l.43 ff. de fideicommiss. libert. Or by another, at his command or with his ratification, Paulus, Sent. 4.12 §8. It is otherwise if it is done by this heir, Paulus Sent. 4.12 §4. What if by a common owner? Paulus, ibid. §5. What if by a creditor? There are also Paulus, ibid. §6. What if at the command of an insane master or a guardian's ward? They do not become dediticii, Paulus, ibid. §7. [illegible] Theophilus, Inst. de libertis; see Gaius 1 §1. Otherwise if they are innocent, Paulus Sent. 4.12 §3. Namely a public prison, Theophilus ibid.; otherwise a private prison would not hinder, unless chains had been put on, l.216 ff. de verb. signif. It was not the same if the master had removed the slave from the office of serving or administering, l.51 in f. ff. de manumiss. testam. Inst. de libert. §3. Sentia §11 in f., s. codem. So he is also manumitted when he has reached the set age: "When the slave shall be thirty years old, let him be free," l.vlt. ff. de rebus dubiis; i.e. "When the slave shall be thirty years old, let him be free," l.39 §2 ff. familiae; l.46 ff. de manumiss. testament.; l.13 §5 ff. de statul. §4 Inst. quibus ex causis manumitt. Theophilus, Inst. quib. ex causis manumiss.: he defined the council as an assembly, or gathering of distinguished men, meeting on fixed days. But understand the council here as that of the praetor at Rome, and of the governors and proconsuls in the provinces, Theophilus, in the said place. By the praetor, namely.
See Cod. de dedititia libert.

units.la: {f} l.43.ff.de fideicommiss. libert. vel alio, eius iussu aut ratihabitione Paulus 4.sent.12.§.8. Senatores {a},& quinque Equites Romani,in prouin- cia {b} viginti Recuperatores {c},ciues Romani.
units.tr: l.43 ff. de fideicommiss. libert. Or by another, at his command or with his ratification, Paulus, Sent. 4.12 §8. Senators, and five Roman knights; in a province, twenty recuperators, who are Roman citizens.

units.la: 14 Ab eo domino, qui {d} soluendo non est, seruus testamento liber esse iussus, & heres instituturus, minor sit triginta annis,vel in ea causa sit, ut dedititius fieri debeat,ciuis Romanus &hæres sit:si {f} ta-men alius ex eo testamento nemo heres sit. Quod si duo pluresve liberi heredesque esse iussi sunt, primo {g} loco scriptus liber & heres sit. Quod & ipsum lex Aelia Sentia facit.
units.tr: 14 If a slave is ordered by will to be free and to be made heir by a master who is not solvent, he becomes a Roman citizen and heir if he is under thirty years of age, or is in a case where he ought to become a dediticius, provided no other person is named heir under that will. But if two or more are ordered to be free and heirs, the one written first in order becomes free and heir. The Lex Aelia Sentia itself provides this.

units.la: 15 Eadem lex in {h} fraudem creditoris & patroni manumittere prohibet.
units.tr: 15 The same law forbids manumission to the defrauding of a creditor or patron.

units.la: 16 Qui tantum in bonis {i}, non etiam ex iure Quiritium seruum habet,manumittendo Latinum facit.In bonis {k} tantum alicuius seruus est, velut hoc modo, si ciuis Rom. à ciue Romano seruum emerit, isque tradi tus ei sit, neque tamen mancipatus {m} ei, neque in iure cessus {n} neque ab ipso anno {o} postessus sit. Nam quandiu {p} horum quid fiat, is seruus in bonis quidem emptoris est, ex iure Quiritium autem venditoris est.
units.tr: 16 A person who has a slave only in bonis, and not also ex iure Quiritium, makes him a Latin by manumitting him. A slave is in someone's bonis only in such a case as this: a Roman citizen has bought a slave from a Roman citizen, and the slave has been handed over to him, but has not yet been mancipated to him, nor transferred in court, nor possessed for a year by him. For as long as none of these things has happened, the slave is indeed in the buyer's bonis, but by the civil law (ex iure Quiritium) he still belongs to the seller.

units.la: 17 Mulier {q} quæ in tutela est, item pupillus & pupilla manumittere non possunt.
units.tr: 17 A woman who is under guardianship cannot manumit, nor can a ward, male or female.

units.la: 18 Communem seruum vnus ex dominis manumittendo, partem suam amittit: eáque adcrescit {r} tur ex §. 12. socio, maximè si eo modo manumiserit, quo, si pro- §. eod.
units.tr: 18 When one of several masters manumits a jointly owned slave, he loses his own share, and it accrues to the partner, especially if he has manumitted in the manner by which, had he first made him his own, he would have made him a Roman citizen. For if he has manumitted him among friends, most hold that he has done nothing.

units.la: {q} quib. ex cauf. manumit: id autem species est ignominiæ l.26. ff. de fideicommiss. libert. {g} Ordo scripturæ attenditur l.24. §.17. ff. de fideicommiss. libert. {h} Caius i. Inst. §.6 : Inst. quib. ex cauf. manumitt. in pr. & §.3 adde tit. ff. qui & a quib. manumiss. liberi non fiant, & ad l. Aeliam. {i} Qui seruum ita habet Bonitarius à Theophilo dicitur Inst. de libertin. {k} Quod ciuis à ciue comparat, nec manicipatu, aut cessione in iure accipit, aut necdum vsucepit, id in bonis non habet. Ied iure Quiritium tantum. {l} duplex dominium. Naturale, quod in bonis, eius dominus Bonitarius §. eod. Legitimum, seu iure Quiritium, cuius dominus, iure Quiritario. {m} Qui vtrumque habet dominiū, pleno iure dominus. {n} Manci patio vt fieret vide tit.19.§.3.§. {o} Cessio in iure vt fiat, v.tit. 19. §.9. §.10. {p} Quemadmodū quis dominus fieret vsucapione v.tit.19 §.8. {q} p. Theoph. d. loco de libert. nisi tutoris auctoritate, quim, sine tutoris auctoritate si ius habebat liberorum v.fra gineatum iuris veteris eunlgatū à Pitheo. de fœminarū tutela dixi ad legem X II. Tabularum libro 2. {r} hodie non adcrescit & ita hic locus, vt & alius Pauli 4. fent. 12. §.1. abrogatur §. pen. Inst. de donationib. & lege x & 2. C. de communi seruo. prium haberet, civem Romanum facturus effet. Nam si inter amicos eum manumiserit, plerisque placet eum nihil egisse.
units.tr: Notes: "quib. ex cauf. manumit." (on the causes for manumission); this is a mark of disgrace, see l. 26, ff. de fideicommissariis libertatibus. The order of the writing is regarded, see l. 24 §17, ff. de fideicommissariis libertatibus. Gaius, Inst. i. §6; Inst. quib. ex causis manumittuntur, in pr. and §3; add the title ff. qui et a quibus manumissi liberi non fiant, and on the lex Aelia. A man who has a slave in this way is called Bonitarius by Theophilus, Inst. de libertinis. Whoever buys a slave from a citizen, and has not received him by mancipation or by cession in court, or has not yet acquired him by usucapion, does not have him in bonis; but only ex iure Quiritium. Double ownership: natural ownership, which is in bonis, whose owner is the Bonitarian (§ eod.); and legal ownership, or ex iure Quiritium, whose owner is the owner by Quiritary law. One who has both kinds of ownership is full owner. On how mancipation is effected, see tit. 19 §3. On how cession in court is effected, see tit. 19 §9, §10. On how one becomes owner by usucapion, see tit. 19 §8. Theophilus, loc. cit. on liberty; unless with the authority of the guardian, for without the guardian's authority, if she had the right of free children (ius liberorum), see below on the ancient law of gentilicium, as explained by Pithou on the guardianship of women, in my commentary on the Twelve Tables, book 2. Today it does not accrue, and so this passage, like that of Paulus, Sent. 4.12 §1, is abrogated (§ penult. Inst. de donationibus; and lex 10 and 2 C. de communi servo). He would have made him a Roman citizen. For if he manumits him among friends, most hold that he has done nothing.

units.la: 19 Servus, in quo alterius est usufructus alterius proprietas, a proprietatis domino manumissus, liber non {a}fit, sed servus sine domino est.
units.tr: 19 A slave in whom one person has the usufruct and another the ownership, if manumitted by the owner of the ownership, does not become free, but remains a slave without a master.

units.la: 20 Post mortem heredis {b}aut ante {c}institutionem heredis, testamento libertas dari non † potest, excepto pto[?] testamento militis.
units.tr: 20 After the death of the heir, or before the heir is appointed, liberty cannot be given by will, except in the will of a soldier.

units.la: 21 Inter medias heredum institutiones libertas data, verisque adeuntibus non † valet: solo autem priore adeunte, iure antiquo valet. Sed post legem Papiam Poppeam, quæ partem non adeuntis caducam facit, si quidem primus hæres vel ius antiquum habeat, valere eam posse placuit: quod si non habeat, non valere constat, quòd loco non adeuntis legatarij {d}partis hæredes fiunt. Sunt tamen qui & hoc casu valere eam posse dicunt.
units.tr: 21 Liberty given between the appointments of several heirs is not valid if the true heirs accept the inheritance. But if only the first heir accepts, it is valid under the ancient law. However, after the lex Papia Poppaea, which makes the share of a non-accepting heir caducous, it has been held that it can be valid if the first heir has the ancient right; but if he does not have it, it is clearly not valid, because in place of the non-accepting heir the share of the legatee becomes heirs. Yet some say that in this case too it can be valid.

units.la: 22 Qui testamento liber esse iussus est, mox {e}quàm unus ex hæredibus adierit hereditatem, liber fit.
units.tr: 22 A person who has been ordered to be free by will becomes free as soon as one of the heirs has entered upon the inheritance.

units.la: 23 Insta libertas testamento potest dari his seruis, qui testamenti {f}faciendi, & mortis {g}tempore, ex iure Quiritium testatoris fuerunt.
units.tr: 23 Immediate liberty can be given by will to those slaves who, at the time of making the will and at the time of the testator's death, belonged to the testator ex iure Quiritium.

units.la: 24 Lex Furia {h}Caninia iubet testamento ex {i}tribus seruis non plures quàm duos manumittere: & vsque ad decem, dimidiam partem manumittere concedit: à decimo vsque ad triginta, tertiam par-
units.tr: 24 The lex Furia Caninia orders that by will no more than two of three slaves may be manumitted; and it allows half to be manumitted for up to ten; from ten up to thirty, a third part

units.la: {b} quia nihil ab hærede hæredis relinqui poterit Paul.3.sent.§.2. & hæc prima ratio dubitandi fuit veteribus. {c} quia testamenta accipiunt vim ab institutione hæredis §.34. Insiit.de legat. & hæc fuit secunda ratio dubitandi veteribus. {d} hodie hoc abrogatum est §.34.Insiit.de legat. Cur ita? Inciuile est scripturæ ordinem sequi, testatoris autem voluntatem sperni d.§.34. † hodie valet d.§.34.in sin.
units.tr: {b} because nothing can be left by the heir of an heir (Paulus, Sent. 3.§2); and this was the first reason for doubt among the ancients. {c} because wills receive their force from the appointment of the heir (§34, Inst. de legatis); and this was the second reason for doubt among the ancients. {d} Today this has been abrogated (§34, Inst. de legatis). Why so? It is unjust to follow the order of the writing and to scorn the will of the testator (d. §34). Today it is valid (d. §34, in fin.).

units.la: {e} Præfecti ærarij hæredes sunt. Cuiacius ita hunc locum refituit. Monetur, quòd præfectorum ærario fuerit, bona quæ fisco deferebantur sperne:e,vel agnoscere l.4.§.20.ff.de fideicom.liber.l.13.ff.de inofficiosis. e l.23.l.25.l.58 ff.de manumiss.testam. f v.d.l.58.tit. 22:§.1. ¶.cod. g vel intra tempus additionis, hi enim defuncti videntur fuisse. h Furia v.Paul.4.sent.§.14.ad L.Fuf.Can. i de numero seruorum testamento manumittendorum Caium 2:adde §.7. Insiit.quib. ex canf.manumiss. tem , vt tamen adhuc quinque manumittere liceat, aeque vt ex priori numero : a triginta vsque ad cen-tum quartam partem, aeque vt decem ex priori numero liberari possint : a centum vsque ad quingen-tos, partem quintam, similiter vt ex antecedenti numero viginti quinque possint fieri liberi. Eadem que praecipit, ne{a} plures omnino quam centum, ex cuiusquam testamento liberi fiant.
units.tr: {e} The prefects of the treasury are heirs. Cujacius restored this passage thus: it is warned that, since they were prefects of the treasury, they should spurn or acknowledge the goods that were brought to the fisc; see l. 4 §20 ff. de fideicommissariis libertatibus; l. 13 ff. de inofficiosis; l. 23, l. 25, l. 58 ff. de manumissis testamento. f see the same l. 58, tit. 22 §1, ¶ cod. g or within the time for accepting, for these are regarded as having died. h Furia: see Paulus, Sent. 4 §14, on the lex Furia Caninia. i Gaius 2 on the number of slaves manumitted by will; add §7, Inst. quib. ex causis manumittuntur, so that nonetheless five may still be manumitted, just as from the former number; from thirty up to a hundred a fourth part, just as ten from the former number may be freed; from a hundred up to five hundred a fifth part, similarly, just as twenty-five may become free from the preceding number. The same law provides that not more than a hundred in all may be made free by anyone's will.

units.la: 25 Eadem lex cauet, vt libertates seruis testamento nominatim{b} dentur.
units.tr: 25 The same law provides that liberties be given to slaves by will by name.
ON STATULIBERS. TITLE II.

units.la: 1 VI sub conditione testamento liber esse iussus est, statu liber appellatur{d}.
units.tr: 1 A slave who is ordered to be free in a will under a condition is called a statuliber (statu liber).

units.la: 2 Statu liber, quandiu pendet conditio{e}, seruus heredis est.
units.tr: 2 While the condition is pending, the statuliber is the slave of the heir.

units.la: 3 Statu liber seu alienetur ab herede, siue suscipiatur ab aliquo, libertatis conditionem secum trahit{f}.
units.tr: 3 Whether the statuliber is sold by the heir or taken over by someone else, he brings the condition of freedom along with him.

units.la: 4 Sub hac conditione liber esse iussus, si decem millia heredi dederit, & si ab herede ab alienatus fit, emptori{g} dando pecuniam, ad libertatem perueniet: idque lex duodecim tabularum iubet.
units.tr: 4 A slave ordered to be free under the condition that he give ten thousand to the heir, and if he is sold by the heir, that he pay the money to the buyer, attains liberty; the Law of the Twelve Tables orders this.

units.la: 5 Si per heredem{h} factum{i} fit, quo minus statu liber conditioni pareat, perinde fit liber, atque si conditio expleta fuisset.
units.tr: 5 If the heir's act is what prevents the statuliber from fulfilling the condition, he becomes free just as if the condition had been fulfilled.

units.la: 6 Extraneo{k} pecuniam dare iussus & liber esse, quibusda[?] libertates dare[?]ius codicilli, testamentario cedebat Paul. 4.sent.14.§.2.
units.tr: 6 Being ordered to give money to a stranger and to be free: the will of the codicils, which gives liberties... yields to the testamentary disposition, as Paul, Sentences 4.14.2.

units.la: {b} Nominatim videtur liber esse iussus, qui vel ex artificio, vel officio, vel quolibet alio modo cuiderer[?] denominatus est v.l.24.ff.de manum.testa: Paul.4.sent.vlt.§.1: §.25.in f.Inst.de leg.
units.tr: {b} "Expressly" (nominatim) seems to mean that he is ordered to be free who has been named from a craft, an office, or any other mode whatever: Digest 40.? law 24, on manumission by will; Paul, Sentences 4, last title, §1; Institutes, on legacies, §25 at the end.
{c} I have spoken on this at Digest 4.? (note 4) and 7.
{d} I have spoken on this at the law 1 of the same title.
{e} Digest, law 9, same title.

units.la: {f} Statuliber vendi potest l.30.ff.eod.non tamen duris conditionib. in vendi-tione onerandus est l. 25. ff. eod. ne pacto haeredis eius condicio fiat durior l.33.ff.eo.ideoq.nec alienatio,nec vsucapio ei nocebit,quomi-nus existente conditione libertatem cofequatur l.13.C.de testa.manu. Quid si legatus fuit? cu sua causa alienabitur l.45. in f. ff.de fidei.lib.
units.tr: {f} A statuliber may be sold (Digest, law 30, same title), yet he is not to be burdened with harsh conditions in the sale (law 25, same title), so that by the heir's agreement his condition is not made harsher (law 33, same title). Therefore neither alienation nor usucaption will harm him, so that when the condition is fulfilled he obtains his freedom (Code, law 13, on wills and manumission). What if he was left as a legacy? He is then alienated with his cause (Digest, law 45 at the end, on trusts).

units.la: {g} aut similibus successor ib.l.27.in f ff.eod.
units.tr: {g} Or by a similar successor (ibid., law 27 at the end, same title).
{h} Digest, law 3, §1, same title.

units.la: {i} aut haeredis tutore & curatore l.3.§.10. ff.eo.
units.tr: {i} Or by the heir's tutor or curator (Digest, law 3, §10, same title).

units.la: {k} cuiuis deniq.d.§.10, si paratus sit dare, & is qui iussus est dare, aut nollet accipere, aut antequàm acceperit moriatur, perinde sit liber, ac si pecuniam dedisset.
units.tr: {k} Finally, to anyone at all (d. §10): if he who is ready to give is ordered to give, and the one who is ordered to give either refuses to accept, or dies before he has accepted, he becomes free just as if he had given the money.

units.la: 7 Libertas & directo{a} potest dari hoc modo, Liber esto, Liber sit, Libertum esse iubeo{b}: & per{c} fideicommissum{d} [?] ...
units.tr: 7 Liberty can be given directly in this way: "Let him be free," "Let him be free," "I order him to be a freedman," and through a trust [?] ...

units.la: 8 Is qui directo liber esse iussus est, horcinus{e} fit libertus. Is autem, cui per fideicommissum data est libertas, non testatoris sed manumissoris fit libertus.
units.tr: 8 One who is ordered to be free directly becomes a freedman of the testator, the one who has him freed; but one to whom liberty is given through a trust becomes a freedman not of the testator but of the manumittor.

units.la: 9 Cuius fidei committi potest ad rem aliquam{f} praestandam, eiusdem etiam{g} libertas fidei committi potest.
units.tr: 9 Whoever can be entrusted with the performance of something may also be entrusted with the granting of freedom.

units.la: 10 Per fideicommissum libertas dari potest tam proprio servo testatoris, quam heredis, aut legatarii, vel cuiusvis extranei{h} servo.
units.tr: 10 Liberty may be given through a trust to a slave of the testator himself, or of the heir, or of a legatee, or of any stranger whatever.

units.la: 11 Alieno servo per fideicommissum data libertate, si dominus eum iusto pretio non vendat, extinguitur{i} fideicommissum{j} nec pretij computatio{k} poli erit hier potest.
units.tr: 11 If liberty is given through a trust for another's slave, and the owner does not sell him for a fair price, the trust lapses, and no calculation of the price can be made.

units.la: 12 Libertas sic dari, ita & adimi{l} tam testamento, quam codicillis testamento confirmatis potest: vt tamen eodem{m} modo adimatur, quo & data est.
units.tr: 12 Liberty so given can be taken away both by will and by codicils confirmed by will, but only in the same way in which it was given.
TIT. III. CONCERNING THE LATINS.

units.la: {a} l. 43. ff. de manumiss. testam. ... Ea forma dici Cuiacius putat qua à Plutarcho in M. Antonio Charonitæ. Idem existimat, dici non male Horcinum. nam & Horcum quidam dixere, [illegible, ~5 letters].
units.tr: Cuiacius thinks the form of words is the one that Plutarch gives in the life of Marcus Antonius, the Charonite. He likewise holds that it may fairly be called Horcinus, for some have also called it Horcus, [illegible].

units.la: {h} §. 2. Instit. de fingul. reb. per fideicom. {g} putà pecuniam. {h} Ex hoc loco, puto initium legis 24. ff. de fideicommiss. libert. passim legendum esse, quod & sequentes d. legi paragraphi satis ostendunt.
units.tr: Institutes 2, §2, on singular things through trust bequests. From this passage I think the beginning of law 24 of the Digest, on trust bequests of freedom, should be read throughout, as the following paragraphs of that law sufficiently show.

units.la: {i} l. 16. ff. de fideicommiss. libertatib. Paul. 4. sent. 3. §. 7. † hoc abrogatum est l. 6. Cod. de fideicommiss. libert. {k} libertas aestimari non potest. {l} l. 50. ff. de fideicommiss. libertatib. & ff. de adimpletione libertatis. {m} v. l. 35. ff. de regul. iur. † Latini fiebant ex lege Iunia Norbana. 78. Latinorum condicio hodie abrogata l. vn. C. de Lat. libert. tollend.
units.tr: Digest, law 16, on trust bequests of freedom; Paulus, Sentences 4, 3, §7. † This has been abrogated by Code, law 6, on the removal of trust bequests of freedom. Freedom cannot be valued in money. Digest, law 50, on trust bequests of freedom, and the Digest, on the fulfilment of freedom. See Digest, law 35, on the rules of law. † Latins were made under the Lex Junia Norbana. 78. The condition of the Latins is abrogated today: Code, the single law, on the removal of Latin freedom.

units.la: LATINI ius Quiritium {a}consequuntur his modis, beneficio {b}principali, liberis {c}, iteratione {d}, mili-tia {e}, naue {f}, aedificio, pistrino: praterea ex Senatusconsulto, veluti quae fit ter enixa.
units.tr: A Latin attains Roman citizenship (ius Quiritium) by these means: by imperial favour, by children, by repetition, by military service, by a ship, by a building, by a mill; besides these, by senatorial decree, as in the case of a woman who has borne three children.

units.la: Beneficio principali Latinus civitatem Romanam accipit, si ab imperatore ius Quiritium impetraverit.
units.tr: By imperial favour a Latin receives Roman citizenship if he has obtained the right of the Quirites from the emperor.

units.la: Liberis ius Quiritium consequitur Latinus, qui minor triginta annorum manumissionis tempore fuit. Nam lege Iunia cautum est, ut si civem Romanam vel Latinam uxorem duxerit testatione interposita, quod liberorum quaerendorum causa uxorem duxerit, postea filio filiave nat[?] natav[?], & anniculo facto, possit apud Praetorem vel Praesidem provinciae causam probare, & fieri civem Romanum tam ipse, quam filius filiave eius & uxor, scilicet si & ipsa Latina sit. Nam sub uxor civi Romana sit partus quoque civis Romanus est, ex senatusconsulto, quod auctore Divo Adriano factum est.
units.tr: A Latin attains the right of the Quirites by children if he was under thirty years of age at the time of his manumission. For the Lex Junia provides that if he marries a Roman or Latin woman, with a declaration made that he marries her for the purpose of having children, and afterwards a son or daughter is born to him, and the child has reached the age of one year, he may prove the case before the Praetor or the governor of the province, and he, his son or daughter, and his wife, become Roman citizens, provided that she too is a Latin. For if the wife is a Roman citizen, the offspring too is a Roman citizen, by the senatorial decree which was passed on the advice of the deified Hadrian.

units.la: Iteratione fit civis Romanus, qui post Latinitatem, quam acceperat, maior triginta annorum, iterum iuste manumissus est ab eo, cuius ex iure Quiritium servus fuit. Sed huic concessum est ex senatusconsulto, etiam liberis ius Quiritium consequi.
units.tr: By repetition a man becomes a Roman citizen who, after the Latin status he had received, being over thirty years of age, is manumitted again, lawfully, by the one whose slave he was under Roman law. But by senatorial decree it has been granted to him that his children too attain the right of the Quirites.

units.la: Militia ius Quiritium accepit Latinus, si inter vigiles Romae sex annis militaverit, ex lege Visellia. Praeterea ex senatusconsulto concessum est, ut si triennio inter vigiles militaverit, ius Quiritium consequatur.
units.tr: A Latin receives the right of the Quirites by military service if he has served for six years among the night watchmen at Rome, under the Lex Visellia. Besides, by senatorial decree it was granted that if he has served for three years among the watchmen, he attains the right of the Quirites.

units.la: Tres ob causas ducitur uxor. Prima est causa prolis. Graeci quoque definiunt Matrimonium, coniunctione viri & mulieris secundum leges [illegible, ~30 letters]. Et Menander apud Clemetem [illegible, ~40 letters]. Valerium 7.c.7: Tacitum 7. Annali. h Ex matre, cive Romana, patre Latino, qui nascitur, civis Romanus est. Antea fiebat Latinus argument. §.8. in sin. I. titul. 5. i §.1.5. eodem. Novella 78. ubi de iteratione Plin. 7. epist. k Latinus, si iterato manumissus fuisset, fiebat civis Romanus §.1. §.eodem 1. Gaius 1. §.5. in sin. l §.3. §.eodem. m Nocturni vigiles, militare censentur. dixi ad l.8. §.4. §.6. ff. de excusat. tut. n lata anno 763, rogante Visellio Varrone v. Cod.ad L.Visellium. o id est postea.
units.tr: A wife is taken for three reasons. The first is the purpose of offspring. The Greeks too define marriage as the union of man and woman according to the laws [illegible]. And Menander, in Clement [illegible]. Valerius Maximus 7, c. 7; Tacitus, Annals 7. h A child born of a Roman citizen mother and a Latin father is a Roman citizen. Formerly such a child became a Latin. Argument, §8, at the end, Institutes, title 5. i §§1, 5, same title. Novel 78, where concerning repetition; Pliny, Letters 7. k A Latin, if he had been manumitted a second time, became a Roman citizen: §1 and §1 of the same title; Gaius 1, §5 at the end. l §3 of the same title. m Night watchmen are counted as serving in the army. I have said so on the law 8, §§4 and 6, Digest, on excuses from guardianship. n Passed in the year 763, on the proposal of Visellius Varro; see the Code, on Lucius Visellius. o That is, afterwards.

units.la: 6 Naue a Latinus ciuitatem Romanam accipit, si non b minorem quam decem millia modiorum nauem fabricauerit, & Romani sex annis frumentarium portauerit, ex edicto Diui c Claudii.
units.tr: 6 By a ship a Latin attains Roman citizenship if he has built a ship of not less than ten thousand modii and for six years has carried the corn supply, under the edict of the deified Claudius.

units.la: DE, HIS QVI SVI IVRIS SVNT. TITVL. IIII.
units.tr: DE, HIS QVI SVI IVRIS SVNT. TITVL. IIII.

units.la: VI iuris sunt familiarum suarum principes, id est, paterfamiliae, itemque materfamiliae.
units.tr: Those who are their own masters (sui iuris) are the heads of their own families, that is, the father of a family and likewise the mother of a family.

units.la: 2 Qui matre quidem certa, patre autem incerto nati sunt, h spurii appellantur.
units.tr: Those born of a certain mother but an uncertain father are called h spurii.

units.la: b Magna capacitas nauis fuit. Senatoribus olim non licuit lege lata a Q. Claudio Tribuno plebis, nauem maritimam maiorem 3co. amphorarum habere Liuius lib.21. qua de re dixi ad l.3.ff.de vacatione mun. nec.
units.tr: b This was a ship of great capacity. Senators were once forbidden, by a law passed by Quintus Claudius, tribune of the plebs, to own a sea-going ship larger than 300 amphorae, as Livy relates in book 21. I have discussed this matter on l. 3 ff. de vacatione munerum.

units.la: c Suetonius in Claudio 18. in f. Naues, mercaturae causa, fabricatibus magna comoda constituit. & c.19. foeminis (quae naues mer caturae causa fabricarent,) us tribuit quatuor liberorum. d desunt in hoc fragmento haec capita, De aedificio, de pistrino & de ea quae ter.tenixa arg.§.1.S.eo. e v.1.Inst.8.1.ff.6: Cai.3. f quali dicere Non sunt in alterius familia, sui iuris sunt, l.4.ff.hoc tit: putà morte parentum. tunc n. singuli liberi, singulas familias inchoant, iure saltem, etiamsi sint pupilli l.95. §2.ff.de verbor. signif: ac sine matrimonio & liberis. Tertullianus in libro de veland. virginib. Mater familias est, licet virgo: pater familias, licet inuesfis. nouarùmque familiarum principes atque duces esse possunt. Festus in voce Familia. Quod patresfamilias, quàm domini familiae potius appellantur ratione non caret. Gratius est n. nomen patris, quàm domini Tertull. in Apologet: Seneca 6. epist: Macrob. 1. Saturnal.11. Martial. 1.Epigram. g Ea familiae suae & caput & finis est l.195. in f.ff.de verb. signif. h ita dicuntur πατρὸς τῆν σπερμάτων idest à satione l.25.ff.de statu; quasi σπορὰς s'ν seu sparsim concepti: vel à liberis latinis S.P. quasi sine patre. Theophil. §. εἰ δὲ τὶς ἐπιτεκνῶν, quam postremam originem probat Caius 4. §.8.in f. & Martianus l.25.in f.ff.de captiuis. Vtramque originem assumit Tribonianus §.12.Inst.de nupt. dum vult spurios dici ἀπάτορας & σπορὰς τὴν σπορὰν. Festus nothum appellat spurio patre natum. Σπυρὶς vios à Plutarcho ioculari dicto appellatur, quasi matr s filius. Muliebrem.n. naturam veteres spurium vocarunt 9.Isidor. 5. σπορίας Plutarch. in problemat.
units.tr: c Suetonius, in Claudius 18, near the end: Claudius granted great advantages to those who built ships for trade. In chapter 19 he granted the privilege of four children to women who built ships for trade. d The following chapters are missing from this fragment: De aedificio, de pistrino, and de ea quae ter.tenixa arg. §1 S. eo. e See 1 Inst. 8.1, ff. 6; Cai. 3. f That is to say, those who are not in another's family are sui iuris, for example through the death of their parents: then each child begins a family of his own, at least in law, even if he is a ward (l. 95 §2 ff. de verborum significatione), and even without marriage and children. Tertullian, in his book on the veiling of virgins: a mother of a family she is, even if a virgin; a father of a family he is, even if unmarried; and they can be the leaders and heads of new families. Festus, under the word Familia: that they are called fathers of the family rather than masters of the family is not without reason, for the name of father is more gracious than that of master. See Tertullian, Apologeticus; Seneca, Epistle 6; Macrobius, Saturnalia 1.11; Martial, Epigrams 1. g She is both the head and the end of her family (l. 195 in fine ff. de verborum significatione). h They are so called from πατρὸς τὴν σπορὰν [patros ten sporan], that is, from sowing (l. 25 ff. de statu), as if conceived σπορὰς ἐν [sporas en], that is, scattered or at random; or from the Latin liberi S.P., as if without a father. Theophilus on the words εἰ δὲ τὶς ἐπιτεκνῶν; Gaius 4 §8 in fine adopts this last origin, and so does Martianus (l. 25 in fine ff. de captivis). Tribonian adopts both origins (§12 Inst. de nuptiis), when he wishes spurii to be called ἀπάτορες [apatores] and σπορὰς τὴν σπορὰν [sporas ten sporan]. Festus calls a nothus one born of a spurious father. Plutarch, in a joking saying, calls a σπυρὶς [spyris] a son of the mother, as if μητρὸς υἱός [metros huios]. For the ancients called the female nature spurium. Isidore 9.5. σπορίας [sporias]: Plutarch, in Problems.
D

units.la: DE HIS QUI IN POTE-STATE SUNT. TITUL. V.
units.tr: ON THOSE WHO ARE UNDER POWER. TITLE 5.

units.la: IN potestate sunt liberi parentum ex {a}iusto matrimonio nati.
units.tr: Children born of a lawful marriage are under the power of their parents.

units.la: 2 Iustum {b}matrimonium est, si inter eos {c}, qui nuptias contrahunt, connubium {d}sit, & tam masculus pubes quàm fœmina potens {e}sit, & utrique consentiant {f}si sui iuris sunt, aut etiam parentes eorum, si in potestate sunt.
units.tr: A marriage is lawful if there is connubium between the parties who contract it, if the man is of marriageable age and the woman is able to bear children, and if both consent, provided they are sui iuris, or their parents consent if they are under power.
Connubium is the legal capacity to take a wife.

units.la: 4 Connubium habent {h}ciues Romani cum ciu-bus Romanis: cum Latinis autem & peregrinis, ita {i}i concessum sit.
units.tr: Roman citizens have connubium with Roman citizens. With Latins and foreigners it exists only if it has been granted to them.
There is no connubium with slaves.

units.la: {e} i. pubes. Masculus pubes esse debet, virgo viripotens Instit. de nupt. l. 13 ff. de verb. signif. l. 101 ff. de condit. & demonst. l. 30 ff. quando dies legati: l. 5 §. 2 ff. quib. ex caus. in poss: nubilis aetatis l. 10 ff. de condit. & demonst: maior annis duodecim l. 4 ff. de vit. ἐφηβος ἀρρὴν[?] 2.Eclog.2.15.
units.tr: That is, pubescent. A male must be pubescent, and a virgin must be ripe for a husband, of marriageable age, and older than twelve years: Instit. de nupt.; l. 13 ff. de verb. signif.; l. 101 ff. de condit. & demonst.; l. 30 ff. quando dies legati; l. 5 §. 2 ff. quib. ex caus. in poss.; l. 10 ff. de condit. & demonst.; l. 4 ff. de vit.; a male youth [ἔφηβος ἄρρην]; 2 Eclog. 2.15.

units.la: {f} Tria requiruntur in iusto matrimonio Primum, ut qui contrahunt sint ciues Romani ʒ[?]. cod. ibi, connubium: ut sint pubères ʒ. cod. ibi, potens: Tertio ut consentiant si sint sui iuris: vel parentes eorum, si in potestate ut hic: & l. 2. ff. de ritu: Instit. de nupt: Quartum Caius addidit, nuptias d.§.1: quo vocabulo, ut opinor, ritum solennem intelligit [?] v. l. 24. Cod. de nuptiis.
units.tr: {f} Three things are required for a lawful marriage. First, that the parties be Roman citizens (law cited in the Code, "connubium"). Second, that they be of marriageable age (cod. ibi, "potens"). Third, that they consent, if they are sui iuris, or their parents consent, if they are under power, as here; and l. 2 ff. de ritu; Inst. de nupt. Caius added a fourth, nuptias (§1), by which word, I think, he means the solemn rite; see l. 24 Cod. de nuptiis.

units.la: {g} Quidam scribunt, Conubium per unicum n.
units.tr: {g} Some write Conubium with a single n.

units.la: {h} Isidorus 10. Etym. vlt. addit æquales. eo sensu, Connubium esse, cum æquales nuptiis coeunt ut puta ciues Romani, pari utique dignitate. Idem receptum aliquando fuit ab Atheniensibus apud quos lege Periclis pro notho habebatur qui natus non fuisset ex duobus Atheniensibus v. Demosthenes in oratione κατὰ Νεαίρ.
units.tr: {h} Isidore, Etym. 10, last chapter, adds "equals": in this sense connubium exists when equals marry, for example Roman citizens, who are of equal dignity. This was at one time also the rule among the Athenians, among whom by the law of Pericles one who was not born of two Athenian parents was regarded as a bastard; see Demosthenes in the speech Against Neaera.

units.la: {i} Boetius in Topicis. Non omnibus erat connubium cum Romanis, nec erant nuptiæ iure contractæ, quæ non aut inter ciuem Romanum, ciuemque Romanam initabantur, aut cui princeps, populusve ciuitatem vel connubium permisisset. eo sc. modo in potestatem parentum liberi rediguntur. Hæc ille. sic Hernicis permissum, Anagnignis ademptum connubium Livius lib. 9.
units.tr: {i} Boethius in the Topics: Not everyone had connubium with the Romans, and those marriages were not lawfully contracted which were not entered into between a Roman citizen man and a Roman citizen woman, or with those to whom the prince or the people had granted citizenship or connubium. In that way children were brought under the power of their parents. So far Boethius. Thus connubium was granted to the Hernici and taken away from the Anagnini, Livy, book 9.

units.la: {l} cum ancillis l. 3. Cod. de incestu: inter seruos & liberos Paul. 2. sent. 19. §. 3. quid ergo? contubernium fuit. l. 14. §. 3. ff. de ritu. l est tamen inter seruos cognatio Inst. de seruili cognat. l. 10 §. 5 ff. de gradib. & quidè talis, ut inter ascendentes & descendentes impediantur nuptiæ. Seruilis n. cognatio impedimento nuptiis est §. 10. Inst. de nupt.
units.tr: {l} With concubines, law 3 Cod. de incestu; between slaves and free persons, Paul, Sent. 2.19 §3. What then? There was contubernium. Law 14 §3 ff. de ritu. There is, however, kinship among slaves, Inst. de seruili cognat.; law 10 §5 ff. de gradib., and of such a kind that marriages are forbidden between ascendants and descendants. For kinship among slaves is an impediment to marriage, Inst. de nupt. §10.

units.la: 6 Inter parentes & liberos infinitè cuiusfeum-que gradus connubium non est. Inter cognatos au-igitur connu-tem ex transuerso gradu, olim quidem vsque ad bium inter quartum gradum matrimonia contrahi non pote-seruos? Non rant: nunc autem etiam ex tertio gradu licet vxo-est. rem ducere. Si tamen fratris filia, non etiam fo-roris filia, aut amita, vel matertera, quanuis eo-dem gradu fit: eademque vxore: nouerca, vel pri-uigna, vel nurus, vel socrus nostra fuit, ducere non possumus.
units.tr: Between parents and children there is no connubium of any degree whatever. Between collateral kin, marriages were formerly not permitted up to the fourth degree; now it is lawful to marry even in the third degree. [Therefore is there no connubium between slaves? No, there is not.] If, however, it is a brother's daughter, but not a sister's daughter, or a paternal aunt, or a maternal aunt, although she is of the same degree; and likewise a wife who was our stepmother, stepdaughter, daughter-in-law or mother-in-law, we may not marry.

units.la: 7 Si quis eam, quam non licet, vxorem duxerit, incestum matrimonium contrahit: ideoque liberi in potestate eius non fiunt, sed quasi vulgò concepti, spurij sunt.
units.tr: If anyone marries a woman whom it is not lawful for him to marry, he contracts an incestuous marriage; therefore the children do not come under his power, but, like those conceived out of wedlock, they are spurious.

units.la: 8 Connubio interueniente, liberi semper patrem sequuntur: non interueniente connubio, matris conditioni accedunt, excepto eo, qui ex peregrino & ciue Romana: peregrinus nascitur: quoniam lex Menfia ex alterutro peregrino natum deteriorem patrem sequi iubet.
units.tr: When connubium exists, children always follow the father. When it does not, they take the condition of the mother, except in the case of one born of a foreigner and a Roman citizen woman, who is born a foreigner, since the Minician law orders that a child born of a foreigner on either side follows the worse parent.
C. de incestis:

units.la: & tamen quibus in negotiis summus pudor, summaque honestas esse debet, vt in nuptiis d.§.2. non parcimus his nominibus: vt ita, fit cognatio etiam inter seruos d.§.5.l.14.§.3.ff.de vitu. [?] Sic conuentibus oculis seruos dicimus habere bona propria l.4. §.1. ff. de manumiffionib. & quasi testamenta facere. Plinius 8. epiftol. 16. Permitto seruos quoque testamenta facere, eaque vt legitima custodio mandant, rogantque quod vium est, pareo ocyus, res suas diuidunt, donant, relinquunt, duntaxat in ra domum. Nam feruis respublica quedam & quasi ciuitas, domus est. a l.17.C. de nuptiis.
units.tr: And yet in matters where the greatest modesty and honour ought to prevail, as in marriage, we do not spare these names; thus kinship arises even among slaves, d. §2, d. §5, l. 14 §3 ff. de ritu. So, with our eyes closed, we say that slaves have their own goods, l. 4 §1 ff. de manumissionibus, and that they make wills as it were. Pliny, Epistles 8.16: I allow slaves to make wills too, and I observe them as lawful; they give instructions and ask what is customary, and I obey at once. They divide, give and leave their own things, but only within the household, for to slaves the household is a kind of commonwealth and, as it were, a city. a l. 17 C. de nuptiis.
a l. 17 C. de nuptiis.
b Cujas reads "quarto" (fourth).

units.la: c Locus est corruptus, quem ita Cuiacius restituit, sed tamen fratris aut sororis filiam, neptemque eoruni, quamuis eodem gradu fit: amitam vel matertera m, & amque vxorem quae nouerca vel priuigna, vel nurus vel socrus nostra fuit ducere non possumus. Hæc ille. Fratris vel sororis neptem (& hc deinceps) duci non potest constat, etiamsi quarto gradu §.3. Inftit. de nupt. Multò minus filiam fratris, quæ est tertio gradu. Caius 4.§. Q. id amitini, vel consobrini inter fe? iure veteri, hæc personæ iungi inter fe non potuerunt Caius 4.§.6. Puffunt hodie, nouiss constitutionibus §.4. Infl.de nuptiis. l.19.C.de nupt.
units.tr: c The passage is corrupt, and Cujas restores it thus: "but a niece of a brother or sister, although she is of the same degree; a paternal aunt or maternal aunt, and a wife who was our stepmother, stepdaughter, daughter-in-law or mother-in-law, we cannot marry." So far Cujas. It is established that the granddaughter of a brother or sister cannot be married, even in the fourth degree, §3 Inst. de nupt. Much less a brother's daughter, who is in the third degree. Caius 4 §9: whether cousins can marry one another; under the old law these persons could not be joined in marriage, Caius 4 §6. They may now, by recent constitutions, §4 Inst. de nupt.; l. 19 C. de nupt.

units.la: d Incesti appellatio hic latissime extenditur. v.C.de incestis.
units.tr: d The term incest is extended here very broadly; see C. de incestis.

units.la: e Vt vulgo concepti ipsi ri dicuntur sit. 4.§ 2.5. ita ex incestis nuptiis nati.
units.tr: e Just as those conceived out of wedlock are called spurious, so those born of incestuous marriages are such. See §§2, 5 above.

units.la: f quod quid est, dicitur ff §.3.§.4.5.eod.
units.tr: f What this is, is said in ff. §3, §4, §5 of the same title.
g i.e. the condition of the father.

units.la: h Natus, patre & matre ciuibus Romanis, ciuis est vt hic: peregrino & ciue Romana, vel ex ciue Romano & peregrina, peregrinus est, i. non ciuis vt hic, nisi per errorē nuptiæ contractæ docentur ii.7.§.4.
units.tr: h A child born to parents who are both Roman citizens is a citizen, as here; a child of a foreigner and a Roman citizen woman, or of a Roman citizen man and a foreign woman, is a foreigner, i.e. not a citizen, as here, unless the marriage was contracted by mistake, as taught in ii. 7 §4.

units.la: 9 Ex a ciue Romano & Latina Latinus nascitur: & ex libero & ancilla, seruus: quoniam cùm his casi-bus connubia non sint, partus sequitur matrem.
units.tr: 9 A child of a Roman citizen and a Latin woman is born a Latin, and a child of a free man and a slave woman is a slave. Since in these cases there is no connubium, the offspring follows the mother.

units.la: 10 In his qui iure cōtracto matrimonio nascuntur, conceptionis {b}tempus spectatur, in his autem
units.tr: 10 In the case of those born of a lawfully contracted marriage, the time of conception is taken into account; but in the case of those

units.la: ciuis titul.3. §.3.in sin. 5. cod: ex libero & ancilla, seruus est d.§.9. natus vulgo, matrem sequitur l.1. in f ff. ad municipalem: vt & is qui illegitimo matrimonio, nisi lex specialis aliud inducat l.24, ff.de statu. Est hoc obseruandum, quod interpretes notant, Baltardos patrum suorum nobilitate, eorumque priuilegiis frui, sed & nomine & insignibus gentis & familiae. Guido Papae quaest. 580: Papon.3. Notar.6.c.de legitimatione de bastardis: eosque adipiscendarum quoque dignitatum capaces l.3. §.2 ff.de decurionib.
units.tr: citizen, title 3 §3 in fin., 5 cod.; a child of a free man and a slave woman is a slave, d. §9; a child born out of wedlock follows the mother, l. 1 in fin. ff. ad municipalem; and likewise one born of an illegitimate marriage, unless a special law provides otherwise, l. 24 ff. de statu. It should be observed, as the commentators note, that bastards enjoy the nobility of their fathers and their privileges, and also the name and insignia of the clan and family. Guido Papae, quaest. 580; Papon 3, Notar. 6, c. de legitimatione de bastardis. They are also capable of obtaining dignities, l. 3 §2 ff. de decurionibus.

units.la: Ex duobus ingenuis natus patrem sequitur, quod ad honores l.19. ff. de statu. Ideoque natus ex patre Campano municeps erit Campanus, quae regula vera est, nisi priuilegio aliquo materna origine censeantur liberi. Tunc enim liberi maternae originis municipes erunt, exempli gratia: Iliensibus concessum est, vt qui matre Iliensi esset, Iliensium municipium sortiretur l.1. §.2. ff ad municip. Idem Delphensibus & Ponticis mulieribus tributum d. §. 2: & Antiochenis l.22. Cod. de decurionib.
units.tr: A child born of two freeborn parents follows the father as regards honours, l. 19 ff. de statu. Therefore a child born of a Campanian father will be a Campanian citizen; this rule is true unless by some privilege children are judged by their maternal origin. For then the children will be citizens of their mother's origin; for example, it was granted to the people of Ilium that one who was born of an Ilian mother would obtain the municipal rights of the Ilians, l. 1 §2 ff. ad municip. The same was granted to the Delphians, and to women of Pontus, d. §2; and to the Antiochenes, l. 22 Cod. de decurionibus.

units.la: In Campania Gallix, natus ex non illi muliere & ignobili patre fit nobilis, eo scilicet priuilegio, Ex Campania le uenire exnoblit. dixi ad l.1. in f. ff. ad municip. Ex duobus diuersorum dominorum adscriptitiis natus impar, matris: par vero, patris conditionem sequitur Nouell. 156. Ex libera & feruo vel adscriptitio, olim fiebat seruus vel adscriptitius l.27. ff. depositi: quod merito sublatum l. vn. Cod. de Senatusconsult. Claud. Ex ingenua & murilegulo condicionem paternam sequitur l.3. Cod. de murilegulis. Adde & hoc in gratiam nostrae gentis hominum, Natum in Gallia ex peregrino & Gallae muliere, Gallici iuris censeri, patri succedere & ab intestato & testato, sicque nullum albinagij competere, haereditatem paternam ad liberos eius in infinitum & cognatos in eadem Gallia commorantes, deferri: quod est contra ius ciuile, quo peregrini sine beneficio principali testari non poterant l.11. ff. qui testam: l.31.32. ff. de iure fisci: v. Papon.7. Notar.6. cap. des lettres de Naturalite. Idem ius etiam puto: si Galli apud peregrinas gentes morentur, ibique liberos suscipiant, fruentur n. eius liberi iure Gallico, si tamen apud foederatos Galliae populos eos suscepserint l.32. ff. de iure fisci: l.7. ff. de captiuis: ideoque nedum haereditatis paternae dominium retinebunt d.l.7. sed & haeredes poterunt institui d.l.32.in f. a dixi §.8.5.eo.
units.tr: In Campania, a child born of a non-noble mother and an ignoble father becomes noble, by that privilege; as I said on l. 1 in fin. ff. ad municipalem. A child born of two adscripticii of different masters follows the mother's condition if they are unequal, but the father's if they are equal, Nov. 156. In the past, a child born of a free woman and a slave or adscripticius became a slave or adscripticius, l. 27 ff. depositi; which was rightly abolished, l. unica Cod. de senatusconsultis Claudiano. A child born of a freewoman and a murilegulus follows the father's condition, l. 3 Cod. de murilegulis. Add also, for the sake of our countrymen, that a child born in Gaul of a foreigner and a Gallic woman is deemed subject to Gallic law: he succeeds his father both by intestacy and by will, and so no albinagium can apply, and the paternal inheritance passes to his children without limit and to kinsmen living in Gaul. This is contrary to the civil law, under which foreigners could not make a will without the prince's special grant, l. 11 ff. qui testam.; l. 31, 32 ff. de iure fisci; see Papon 7, Notar. 6, cap. des lettres de naturalité. I think the same law holds if Gauls stay among foreign peoples and there have children; for those children will enjoy Gallic law, provided they were born among the allied peoples of Gaul, l. 32 ff. de iure fisci; l. 7 ff. de captivis. Therefore they will not only retain ownership of the paternal inheritance, d. l. 7, but may also be instituted heirs, d. l. 32 in fin.; I said this at §§8 and 5 of the same title.

units.la: {b} Mulier quae libera vel concepit, vel vtero libera partum gestauit, vel libera peperit, liberum parit. vel ita, Cuius mater libera fuerit vel conceptionis vel partus vel intermedio tempore, liber nascitur l.5. §.2.ff.de statu: Paul. 2. sent. 24. §.1.2.3. Censa[?] tur autem li-bera quæ ma-numitti de-buit, nec est manumissa l. qui non legitimè concipiuntur, editionis: veluti si ancilla conceperit, deinde manumissa pariat, libe-rum parit. Nam quamuis non legitimè concepit, cùm editionis tempore libera sit, partus quoque li-ber est.
units.tr: {b} A woman who was free either when she conceived, or carried the child in her womb while free, or gave birth while free, bears a free child. Or in this form: whose mother was free at the time of conception, or of the birth, or in the interval, is born free (Dig. 1.5.2.2 de statu; Paul, Sent. 2.24.1-3). A woman is considered free who ought to have been manumitted and has not been manumitted; as the edict says, those who are not lawfully conceived... For example, if a female slave conceives, and is afterwards manumitted and then gives birth, she bears a free child. For although she was not lawfully conceived, since she is free at the time of the edict, the offspring is also free.
On Dowries
TITLE VI.

units.la: Os aut datur aut dicitur b,aut promittitur c.
units.tr: A dowry is either given, or declared, or promised.

units.la: 1 Dote dicere d potest mulier e,quæ nuptura est:& debitor mulieris,si iussu eius dicat institutus f: parens mulieris virilis sexus per virilem sexum cognatione iuctus, velut pater,auus paternus. Dare promittere dotem omnes g possunt.
units.tr: (1) A dowry may be declared by the woman who is about to marry, or by her debtor if he declares it at her command, or by a parent of the woman related through the male line, such as her father or paternal grandfather. Anyone may give or promise a dowry.

units.la: 3 Dos aut profectitia dicitur,i.quàb pater mulieris dedit i: aut aduetitia,i.ea q à quouis alio[?] data est.
units.tr: (3) A dowry is called profectitia (from the father) when the woman's father gave it, or adventitia when it was given by anyone else.

units.la: 4 Mortua in matrimonio muliere, dos à patre profecta, ad patrem reuertitur, quin-ea peregrino nascatur. & nobilem,qui tempore conceptionis, patrem nobilem habuerit,quantumuis postea pater nobilitatem amiserit.a 2.
units.tr: (4) If the woman dies during the marriage, a dowry that came from her father returns to her father, unless she left children, in which case it is kept by the husband for each child, and the father is still entitled to the dowry. If the father is not living, the husband keeps it. A woman who is a foreigner ... and a noblewoman, if her father was a nobleman at the time of conception, remains noble, even if her father later lost his nobility.

units.la: a 2. Paul.21. 3.Codic. Theodof.13; & 5. Codic. 11. de dotis promissione.
units.tr: Note a 2. See Paulus, Sentences 2.21.3; the Theodosian Code 13; and Code 5.11 on the promise of a dowry.

units.la: b vide §.2.in principi ] eodem.2.Caius 9.§.4. c vide dict.§.2.in sin.aut datur l.2.Codice Theodof.de incestis d Dotis dictio,(l.3.Codice Theodosi, eodem. solenniter fiebat dicta l. 2. id est , solennibus verbis. Hodie qualiacunque verba sufficiunt lege 6. Codice de dotis promiss. Doti dicere veteres dicebant, cuius forte loco Tribonianus hanc formulam vsurpauit. Doti promittere, vide l.79.ff.de iure dot. e Tres personæ tantum poterant doti dicere 2.Caius 9.§.4.mulier nuptura ut hic: procurator specialis f. eodem: parens nupturæ f. eodem. Dotem verò promittere poterant omnes, cuiuscumque sexus & conditionis lege 41.ff. de iure dot. f id est, constitutus. g dicta lege 41. h l.5.ff.de iure dot. i Per se vel per alium dicta lege quinta §.primo, & breuiter non ius potestatis, sed parentum nomen dotem profectitiam facit dicta lege quinta §.primo. k dicta lege quinta §.nono, etiam matre, dicto §.nono. l Nobilis est quæstio, & à multis agitata, Ad quem dos profectitia (de aduenititia dicam §.quinto f.) mortua muliere reuertatur. Paucis ita definio: dotem profectitiam morte mulieris ad eius patrem reuerti ut hic: & lege 17.ff.de Sc. Macedon: lege quarta §.decimatertio ff.de iure dotium, siue filiafamilias fuit l.4. Codice soluto: siue materfamilias vt Theodorus Græcus interpres adnotauit ad dict. leg.4. Hic difficiles occurrunt quæstiones. tis † in singulos liberos in infinitum relictis penes virum. Quod si pater non sit, apud maritum remanet.
units.tr: Note b: see §2 at the beginning of the same title, and Gaius 2.9.4. Note c: see the same §2 at the end, "aut datur", and Theodosian Code on incest. Note d: the declaration of a dowry (Theodosian Code 3, same title) was made solemnly, that is, with solemn words, as Law 2 says. Today any words at all suffice, by Code 6, on promises of dowries. The ancients said "to declare a dowry", and Tribonian used this formula in place of that one. On "to promise a dowry", see Digest 23.3.79. Note e: only three persons could declare a dowry, Gaius 2.9.4: the woman about to marry, as here; a special agent (procurator); and the parent of the bride-to-be. But anyone of either sex or condition could promise a dowry, Digest 23.3.41. Note f: that is, the one appointed. Note g: by the same Law 41. Note h: Digest 23.3.5. Note i: whether by himself or through another, by the said fifth law, §1. In short, it is not the power of authority but the name of parent that makes a dowry profectitia. Note k: by the said fifth law, §9, even if it comes from the mother, §9 above. Note l: This is a difficult question, much debated: to whom a profectitia dowry returns when the woman dies (I will discuss the adventitia at §5 below). I define it briefly thus: on the woman's death the profectitia dowry reverts to her father, as here, and Digest 17 on the Senatus consultum Macedonianum, and Digest 23.3 law 4, §13, whether she was a daughter under her father's power (Code 4 on the dissolved marriage), or a mother of a family, as the Greek interpreter Theodorus noted on the said Law 4. Here difficult questions arise.

units.la: § Aduentitia autem dos semper penes maritum remanet, nisi quum is qui dedit, vt sibi reddere[?] stipulatus fuit: quæ dos specialiter recepta est dicitur.
units.tr: §. An adventitia dowry, however, always remains with the husband, unless the giver stipulated for its return to himself. A dowry so specially stipulated for is called receptitia.

units.la: 6 Diuortio facto, si quidem sui iuris sit mulier, ipsa habet actionem, id est, dotis repetitionem: quod si in potestate patris sit, pater adiuvat filiæ personæ habet actionem reuera[?]. Nec f interest aduentitia sit dos, an profectitia.
units.tr: (6) If a divorce takes place, and the woman is her own master (sui iuris), she herself has the action, that is, the recovery of the dowry. If she is under her father's power, the father brings the action on behalf of his daughter. And it makes no difference whether the dowry is adventitia or profectitia.

units.la: 7 Post diuortium defuncta muliere, heredi eius actio non aliter datur, quam si moram in dote lutionib: l.2.l.7.inf Cod.hac tit. Si emancipata, vno casu ad patrem reuertitur l.7.ff.de cuiet.: puta si ideo filia diuertit vt maritū lucro dotis afficeret, patrem defraudaret l.5.ff. de diuort.
units.tr: (7) After a divorce, if the woman dies, her heir is granted the action only if the husband has been in delay in paying the dowry; see Code 2 and 7 below, this title. If she has been emancipated, the dowry returns to her father in one case, Digest 7 on Cuiacius: that is, if the daughter divorced in order to enrich her husband with the dowry, defrauding her father, Digest 5 on divorce.

units.la: Quid si capta ab hostibus? perinde dicendum est ac si nupta decessisset. Ideoque dos ad patrem reuertitur l.10.ff.soluto. Quid si mortua liberos reliquit? Bulgarus dotem ad patrem filiæ reuerti existimat. Martianus contrà: cuius opinio communi interpretum sententia defensa est Accurf.ad l.4.Cod.soluto.
units.tr: What if she was taken captive by enemies? It must be said just as if she had died married. And so the dowry returns to the father, Digest 10 on the dissolved marriage. What if she died and left children? Bulgarus thinks the dowry returns to the daughter's father. Martinus holds the contrary, and his opinion has been defended by the common view of the interpreters, Accursius on Code 4 on the dissolved marriage.

units.la: Num ex iure Romano? iure veteri non puto. hic enim dos profectitia ad patrem filiæ reuertitur, quintis in singulos liberos reliētis penes virum: si pater non sit, apud maritum remanet adde l.6.ff.de iure dot.: 9.Ecl. i.e.3. Scio tamen subtiliter quædam dici in contrariam sententiam posse. quale est, illud, Dotis repetitionem patri competere, mortua in matrimonio puella l.17.ff. de Sc. Macedon. ergo, à contrario, si non puella, id est nō virgo mortua, sed mater reliētis liberis, dos ad eius patrem nō reuertetur. Ad hæc, Iunni potest ex lege vlt.§.1. ff.vt legator: vel vnius filij superstitis nomine dotem apud maritū remanere, non ad patrem reuerti. Colligunt etiam nonnulli ex lege 26.§.2.ff.de pactis dotalibus: dotem pertinuisse prius ad liberos defuncti: ab his, ad maritum: nisi maritus suo iuri in fauorem patris de functæ expresse renunciasset. Sed præstat Martini opinionem defendere liberorū fauore: eoque magis quod vsu fit recepta, Accurf.ad l.4.C.folut: Bald.ad l.post dotem 40.ff.soluto: Ferrariensis in forma libelli quo vxor agit ad dotem 33. in verbo diētæ domina num: 1.adde Antonium Fabrum 1.conictiar.16.
units.tr: Is this from Roman law? I do not think so under the old law. For there the profectitia dowry returns to the daughter's father, as I have said, and is kept by the husband for each child, and if there is no father, it remains with the husband; add Digest 6 on the dowry law, and Ecloga 9, title 3. I know, however, that some subtle arguments can be made for the contrary view, such as this: the right to recover the dowry belongs to the father when the girl dies in marriage, Digest 17 on the Senatus consultum Macedonianum. Therefore, conversely, if she was not a girl, that is, not a virgin, but a mother who left children, the dowry will not return to her father. Moreover, it is said from the last law, §1, Digest on the legacy, that the dowry remains with the husband on behalf of the one surviving child, and does not return to the father. Some also gather from Digest 26, §2, on dotal pacts, that the dowry first belonged to the children of the deceased, and from them passed to the husband, unless the husband had expressly renounced it in favour of the deceased's father. But it is better to defend Martin's opinion in favour of the children, and all the more because it has been received by custom, Accursius on Code 4 on the dissolved marriage; Baldus on Digest 40, "post dotem", on the dissolved marriage; Ferrariensis in the form of the petition by which a wife sues for her dowry, 33, under "dicta domina", num. 1. Add Antonius Faber, Conjectures 1.16.

units.la: † nota de quintæ retentione. Sextæ retentionis hic merito in §.10.1. vtraque abrogata l.vn. §.5.verf. liceat ob liberos retentio C.de rei vxor.act. a Aduentitia dos ea est quæ ab alio q parēte cōstituitur l.7.§.13.verf.extraneum C.de rei vxor.act. b i.siue sint liberi,siue nō sint. c dixi l 31.§.2. ff.de mort.caus. d l.2.§.1.ff.sol. e actione rei vxorie. ita emendat Cuiacius. f Imo interest d.§.1. g l.57.ff.soluto,
units.tr: Note on the retention of a fifth. The retention of a sixth is rightly treated here at §10, 1; both were abrogated by the single law §5, "liceat ob liberos retentio", Code on the action on the wife's property. Note a: an adventitia dowry is that which is constituted by someone other than a parent, Code 7 §13, "extraneum", on the action on the wife's property. Note b: that is, whether or not there are children. Note c: I have said so on Digest 31 §2 on death-causes. Note d: Digest 2 §1 on the dissolved marriage. Note e: the action on the wife's property; so Cuiacius corrects it. Note f: indeed it makes a difference, see the said §1. Note g: Digest 57 on the dissolved marriage,

units.la: [Full-width footnote text continues in the scan; see the notes above for the readings I could not settle.] mulieri reddenda maritus fecerit.
units.tr: [The note in the scan continues here; see the notes above for the readings I could not settle.] which the husband has made to be returned to the wife.

units.la: 8 Dos si pondere, numero, mensura continetur, annua, bima, trima die reddetur †: nisi fi, vt præ- fens reddatur, conuenerit. Reliquæ dotes statim red- duntur.
units.tr: (8) If the dowry consists of weight, number, or measure, it shall be returned in annual, biannual, or triennial instalments, unless the parties agreed that it be returned at once. Other dowries are returned immediately.

units.la: 9 Retentiones ex dote fiunt † aut propter libe- ros a, aut propter mores b, aut propter impensas c, aut propter res donatas d, aut propter res amotas e.
units.tr: (9) Retentions from the dowry are made either on account of children, or on account of conduct, or on account of expenses, or on account of gifts, or on account of goods removed.

units.la: 10 Propter liberos retentio fit †, si culpa mulie- ris aut patris cuius in potestate est, d:uortium fa- ctum fit. Tunc enim singulorum liberorum nomi- ne sextæ † retinentur ex dote: non plures quàm tres sextæ f in retentione g sunt, non in petitione.
units.tr: (10) A retention on account of children is made when the divorce results from the fault of the wife, or of the father under whose power she is. For then a sixth is retained from the dowry for each child by name. Not more than three sixths are retained from the dowry, Digest 3, at the time of retention, not at the time of the claim.

units.la: 11 Dos quæ semel fundta est h, amplius fungi non potest, nisi aliud matrimonium fit ".
units.tr: (11) A dowry which has once ceased to be a dowry cannot be made a dowry again, unless there is another marriage.

units.la: 12 Morum nomine, grauiorum quidem sex- ta i retinentur: leuiorum item octaua k. Graviores mores l sunt, adulteria m tantum : leuiores, om- nes reliqui.
units.tr: (12) On account of conduct, a sixth is retained for more serious faults, and likewise an eighth for lesser ones. The more serious faults are adultery alone; the lesser are all the others.

units.la: 13 Mariti mores puniuntur, in ea quidè dote q ndie
units.tr: (13) The husband's conduct is punished, in that dowry ...

units.la: {a} d.§.5. verf. sileat ob liberos retentio. {b} d.§.5. verf. quid enim opus est inducere ob mores retentionem. {c} d.§.5. verf. sed nec ob impensas. {d} d.§.5. verf. vel ex qua causa ob rem donatam: adde l.1.§.3.ff.de dote re- legata. {e} d.§.5. verf. sed nec retentio ob res amotas. † hodie no fit d.§.5.verf.sileat ob liberos retentio. † nota de sextæ retentione. Retentionis quintæ fit mentio §. quarto supra eodem. vtraque retentiones abrogatæ sunt d.verf.sileat ob liberos. {f} id est, non plus dimidia. nam sex sextæ faciunt integrum. {g} An compensationes dotis causa, sint sublatæ, dicam alibi. {h} i. quæ semel dos esse desinit. " i nisi matrimonii fit redintegratio. Redintegratur ... [illegible, ~20 letters]
units.tr: {a} Said §5, "let retention on account of children be silent". {b} Said §5, "for what need is there to introduce a retention for conduct". {c} Said §5, "nor is retention made on account of expenses". {d} Said §5, "or for a gift made from any cause": add Digest 1 §3, on the dowry bequeathed. {e} Said §5, "nor is retention made on account of goods removed". † Today this is not done, by said §5, "let retention on account of children be silent". † Note on the retention of a sixth. Mention is made of the retention of a fifth in §4 above under the same title; both retentions have been abrogated, said "let it be silent on account of children". {f} That is, not more than half, for six sixths make a whole. {g} Whether compensations on account of the dowry have been abolished I will discuss elsewhere. {h} That is, a dowry which has ceased once to be a dowry. "Unless the marriage is restored. It is restored ..." [illegible, about twenty letters]

units.la: Taciè, inquam, quia fem per hoc agi intelligitur nisi aliud conuenerit l.30.ff.de iure dot. id est, nisi dos fit receptitia l.42.in f. ff.soluto. Porrò, non dicitur redintegrari matrimonium, fi post le- ue iurgium vxor rediit. Est enim aliud leue fribusculum, aliud di- uortium l.31.ff.de iure dot: l.31.§.11.§.12.ff.de donat.inter vir. Si di- uortium non fuit, redintegrari non potuit. Vix est enim vt id red- integratum dicamus, quod dissolutum non fuit. ⁱ sextæ Cuiac. ᵏ octauæ Cuiacius. ˡ adde l.39.l.47.ff.soluto. ᵐ An pars a- qua bonorum adulterae, eius marito hodie cedat, dixi ad Nouell. 117.c.p.13. ad Nouell.134.cap.10. ⁿ quæ annua bima trima die &c. Cuiac.hic. Idem tamen 7.obs.20.legit, annua: & hac vnica voce tuiscon sultum affectatiè compendium orationis, vt in l.30.§.1.ff. de legatis ibi, annua die dabuntur l.1.§.2.ff.de dote prælegata, ibi, an- nua die dos præstaretur. Suetonius in Augusto sub finem, quibus solreddi debet. Ita propter maiores mores praesentem{b} dotem reddit: propter minores{c} senum mensum die. In ea autem quae praesens reddi solet, tantum ex fructibus iubetur reddere, quantum in illa dote quadriennio redditur: quod repraesentatio{d} facit.
units.tr: Silently, I say, because it is understood that this is done in such a way unless otherwise agreed, Digest 30 on the dowry law; that is, unless the dowry is receptitia, Digest 42 at the end, on the dissolved marriage. Moreover, a marriage is not said to be restored if the wife returns after a slight quarrel. For a slight squabble is one thing, divorce another, Digest 31 on the dowry law; Digest 31 §§11–12 on gifts between husband and wife. If there was no divorce, the marriage could not be restored. For it is hardly right to say that something is restored which was never dissolved. {i} sixths, Cuiacius. {k} eighths, Cuiacius. {l} add Digest 39 and 47 on the dissolved marriage. {m} Whether the adulteress's share of goods now passes to her husband I have discussed on Novel 117, c. p. 13, and on Novel 134, c. 10. {n} The words "annual, biannual, triennial day, &c." are from Cuiacius here. He also reads "annual" in Observations 7.20, and by this single word gathers a deliberate abbreviation of expression, as in Digest 30 §1 on legacies, "they shall be given on an annual day", Digest 1 §2 on the dowry given as a legacy, "the dowry should be furnished on an annual day". Suetonius, in Augustus near the end, on the times at which it ought to be returned. So, on account of greater misconduct, the husband returns the dowry at once; for lesser misconduct, after six months. But in the case of a dowry usually returned at once, he is ordered to return only so much of the income as the dowry yields in four years; this is what the repraesentatio effects.

units.la: 14 Impensarum species sunt tres{e}: aut enim necessariae{f} dicuntur, aut utiles{g}, aut voluptuosae{h}.
units.tr: 14 There are three kinds of expenses: some are called necessary, some useful, and some voluptuous.

units.la: 15 Necessariae sunt impensae, quibus non factis{i} deterior{k} futura est: veluti si quis ruinosas{l} aedes refecerit.
units.tr: 15 Necessary expenses are those without which the dowry would become worse: for example, if someone rebuilt a ruinous house.

units.la: 16 Utiles sunt, quibus non factis quidem deterior dos non fuerit: factis autem fructuosior{m} dos effecta est: veluti si vineta & oliveta fecerit.
units.tr: 16 Useful expenses are those without which the dowry would not indeed be worse, but with which the dowry has become more productive: for example, if someone planted vineyards and olive groves.

units.la: 17 Voluptuosae{n} sunt, quibus neque omissis deterior dos fieret: neque factis, fructuosior effecta est: quod evenit in viridariis, {o}& pictoris{p}, similibus que{q} rebus.
units.tr: 17 Voluptuous expenses are those without which the dowry would not become worse, and with which it has not become more productive; this happens with pleasure gardens, paintings and similar things.

units.la: DE IURE DONATIONUM INTER VIRUM & UXOREM. TIT. VII.
units.tr: ON THE LAW OF GIFTS BETWEEN HUSBAND AND WIFE. TITLE VII.

units.la: INTER virum & uxorem donatio non valet, nisi certis ex causis: mortis causa, di-
units.tr: Between husband and wife a gift is not valid, except for certain causes: in view of death, for divorce-

units.tr: {l} A collapsing building; see d.l.1 §3, l.4 ff. de impensis.

units.tr: {m} Better; see d.l.79 §1, l.5 inf. ff. de impensis.

units.tr: {n} So called in l.14 at the end, ff. de impensis: voluptuary expenses, l.7 §§9, 10, 11 ff. de impensis.

units.tr: Pleasure gardens, green plots, pleasure gardens, [illegible]. Eclog. c.79.
