units.la: q Cessio in iure,seu prætore ita fit. Is cui res cedítur,Rem tenens ita vindicat, Hunc ego hominē ex iure Quiritum meum esse aio.
units.tr: q Cession in law, or before the praetor, is done thus. The one to whom the thing is ceded, holding the thing, claims it thus: "I declare this man to be mine by the law of the Quirites."

units.la: 10 In iure cedit dominv: vindicat is, cui cediʈur, addicit ᵃ Prætor.
units.tr: 10 In cession in law the ownership v passes: the one to whom it is ceded claims it, and the praetor a adjudges it.

units.la: 11 In iure cedi res etiam incorporales possunt, velut vsufructus ᵇ,& hereditas ᶜ, & tutela ᵈ legitima,& libertas ᵉ.
units.tr: 11 Incorporeal things too can be ceded in law, such as usufruct b, inheritance c, legitimate guardianship d, and liberty e.

units.la: 12 Hereditas in iure ceditur, vel antequam ᶠ adeatur, vel posteaquam adita fuerit.
units.tr: 12 An inheritance is ceded in law either before f it is entered upon or after it has been entered upon.

units.la: 13 Antequam adeatur, in iure cedi potest legitimo ab hærede: posteaquam adita est, tam à legitimo, quàm ab eo qui testamento heres scriptus est.
units.tr: 13 Before it is entered upon, it can be ceded in law by the legitimate heir; after it has been entered upon, it can be ceded both by the legitimate heir and by the one named heir in the will.

units.la: 14 Si antequam adeatur hereditas, in iure cessa fit, perinde heres fit cui cessa est, ac si ipse heres legitimus esset. Quod si posteaquam adita fuerit, in iure cessa fit: is g cui cessa est, permanet heres, & ob id creditoribus defuncti ʰ manet obligatus: debitores defuncti liberantur. Vero pereunt, i. debitores defuncti liberantur.
units.tr: 14 If the inheritance is ceded in law before it is entered upon, the one to whom it is ceded becomes heir just as if he were himself the legitimate heir. But if it is ceded in law after it has been entered upon, the one to whom it is ceded g remains heir, and for that reason remains bound to the creditors of the deceased h; the debtors of the deceased are released. But the debts truly perish, that is, the debtors of the deceased are released.

units.la: 15 Res autem ⁱ corporales, quoties singulæ in iure cessæ sunt, transeunt ad eum cui cessa ᵏ est heredi tas.
units.tr: 15 But corporeal things, whenever they are ceded in law one by one i, pass to him to whom the inheritance k has been ceded.

units.la: Quando negauit, hunc ego hominem præsenti & vindicanti addico. Potuit etiam ita concipi Q,N, A,N,N,H,E H,P,E,V,A, i. Quando neque au, neque negas, hunc ego hominem petenti & vindicanti addico. Hinc constat in rei vindicatione, non satis fuisse posse negare intentionem actoris sed præterea eum debuisse contra vindicare, argum. § 2. Infit. de actionib. ibi, Possessor autem dominum esse dicat adde Cont. t. disput. 12. a Tribus verbis omnes officium prætoris continebatur, Do, Dico, Addico: Dabat iudices, Ius dicebat, Addicebat hic. b Vsufructus cessione finitur l. 66. ff. de iure dotium. c v. § 12. § eod. d tit. 11. 7. 5. eod. e quæ & Cessicia. Fit autem vindicta: cedit libertatem dominus, seruus vindicat: Prætor addicit. Verba domini si requiras, ea fuerunt: Hunc hominem liberum esse volo, Fcllu in voce Manumitti: Verba Prætoris, [illegible, ~24 letters]. Fragmentum indicis Latinogræci in Bibliotheca regia. Interdum etiam fiebat manumissio, sed & absente Prætore, præsente solo eius lictore lege 23. ff. de manumiss. vindicta. f vide §. 13. §. 14. 1. eodem: §. 15. 1. eodem. g is a quo Cuiacius hic. h Qui debitoris hæreditatem adit, contrahit cum defuncti creditoribus l. 3. in f. l. 4. quibus ex cauf. in poss. i Superius dixit de hæreditate, hic de rebus corporalibus. vt hinc colligas, Hæreditatem inter res corporales non adnumerari. Hæreditas, iuris nomen l. 119. l. 178. §. 1. ff. de verbor. signif: incorporalis §. 2. Infit. de rebus corporalibus. k cui cessa sunt. Cuiacius ita legit, pro, cessa est, hæreditas.
units.tr: "When he has denied it, I adjudge this man to the one present and claiming." The formula could also have been framed thus: Q.N. A.N.N.H.E. H.P.E.V.A., that is, "When you neither affirm nor deny, I adjudge this man to the one seeking and claiming." Hence it is established that in an action for vindication it was not enough for the defendant to deny the plaintiff's claim, but he was also obliged to counter-claim; compare §2 Inst. de actionibus, where it says "the possessor, however, says that he is owner"; add Contius, disput. 12. a The whole office of the praetor was contained in three words: Do, Dico, Addico: he gave judges, declared the law, and adjudged here. b Usufruct is ended by cession, l. 66 ff. de iure dotium. c see §12 of the same title. d tit. 11, §5 of the same. e which is also called cessicia. It is done by vindicta: the master cedes liberty, the slave claims, the praetor adjudges. As for the words of the master, if you ask, they were: "I wish this man to be free," Festus in the word Manumitti. The words of the praetor: [illegible]. Fragment of an index Latino-Graecus in the royal library. Sometimes manumission was also made in the absence of the praetor, with only his lictor present, lex 23 ff. de manumissionibus vindicta. f see §13 and §14 of the same; §15 of the same. g the one from whom, Cuiacius here. h One who enters upon the inheritance of a debtor contracts with the creditors of the deceased, l. 3 in fine, l. 4 quibus ex causis in possessionem. i Above he spoke of the inheritance; here of corporeal things, so that you may gather that the inheritance is not counted among corporeal things. "Inheritance" is a term of law, l. 119, l. 178 §1 ff. de verborum significatione; it is incorporeal, §2 Inst. de rerum divisione. k "to whom it has been ceded." Cuiacius reads it thus, instead of "the inheritance has been ceded."

units.la: 16 Adiudicatione{a} dominia nanc ifcimur,per formulam{b} Familiæ erciscundæ{c}, quæ locum habet inter coheredes: & per formulam Communi diuidundo{d}, cui locus est inter socios: & per formulam Finium regundorum{e}, quæ est inter vicinos. Nam si iudex vni ex heredibus aut socijs, aut vicinis rem aliquam adiudicauerit, statim illi adquiritur, siue mancipi, siue mec mancipi sit.
units.tr: 16 We acquire ownership by adjudication: through the formula for dividing an inheritance (familiae erciscundae), which applies between co-heirs; through the formula for dividing common property (communi dividundo), which applies between partners; and through the formula for fixing boundaries (finium regundorum), which applies between neighbours. For if the judge adjudges some thing to one of the heirs, partners or neighbours, it is acquired by that person at once, whether it is a thing held by mancipation or not.

units.la: 17 Lege nobis adquiritur,velut caducum{f} vel{g} ereptitium{h} ex lege Papia Popea{i}: item legatum{k} ex lege XII Tabularum, siue mancipi res sint, siue necmancipi.
units.tr: 17 We acquire by law, for example a caducous or ereptitious share under the Papian-Poppaean law, and likewise a legacy under the Law of the Twelve Tables, whether the things are held by mancipation or not.

units.la: 18 Adquiritur autem nobis etiam per{l} eas personas, quas in potestate, manu,mancipiove habemus. Itaque si quidem (mancipio puta)acceperint, aut traditum{m} eis sit,vel stipulati fuerint{n}, ad nos pertinet.
units.tr: 18 We also acquire through those persons whom we have in our power, in our hand, or in mancipium. So if they have accepted something by mancipation, for instance, or it has been handed over to them, or they have made a stipulation, it accrues to us.

units.la: 19 Item si heredes instituti{o} sint,legatumve{p} eis sit: & hereditatem iussu{q} nostro adeuntes nobis adquirunt,& legatum ad nos pertinet.
units.tr: 19 Likewise, if they have been instituted heirs, or a legacy has been left to them, and they enter upon the inheritance at our command, they acquire it for us, and the legacy accrues to us.

units.la: 20 Si seruus alterius in bonis{r}, alterius ex iure Quiritium sit, ex omnibus caussis adquiret ei, cuius in bonis est.
units.tr: 20 If a slave is in another's bonitary ownership and in someone else's quiritary ownership, he acquires for the person whose bonitary property he is, on every ground.
{g} Hotomanus, Observ. 3.32, deletes this clause.

units.la: {h} Ereptitium, quod quasi indigno aufertur, vt in lege penultima, ff.de iure fisci: quadrans eripiatur,& in lege 25.ff.de scarijs: hæreditas eripietur Cuiacius 6. obseruat.37. & sic statim ipso iure vindicatur l.9.l.18.l.vltima ff.de his quæ vt indignis. Et recte Vlpianus eripiendi verbo potius vsus est,quàm auferendi,vt indicaret, quasi de manibus auferri,quod iam esset adquisitum lege 4. ff. ne quis eum: vide Contium 1.disputat.12. Sed tamen Hotomanus 3. obseruat.32. legit receptitium. Quod quid sit, vide eundem dicto loco.
units.tr: {h} Ereptitium is what is taken away as from one who is unworthy, as in the penultimate law Dig. de iure fisci, where a quadrant is seized (eripiatur), and in law 25 Dig. de scariis, where the inheritance will be seized. Cuiacius, Observ. 6.37, notes this, and so it is claimed at once by law itself: laws 9 and 18 and the last law Dig. de his quae ut indignis. Ulpian rightly used the verb eripiendi rather than auferendi, to show that what was already acquired is, as it were, snatched from the hands, law 4 Dig. ne quis eum. See Contius, 1 disput. 12. Hotomanus, Observ. 3.32, however, reads receptitium. For what that means, see the same author in the place cited.

units.la: {i} Ea lata est de caducis hereditatibus & legatis, vt Falcidia de modo legatorum. l.47.in fine ff. de peculio: l.120.ff.de verborum significationibus.
units.tr: {i} This was introduced concerning caducous inheritances and legacies, just as the Falcidian law was concerning the amount of legacies. Law 47 in fine Dig. de peculio; law 120 Dig. de verborum significationibus.

units.la: {l} vide Infiit. per quas personas cuique adquirerum. {m} §.3.Infiit per quas personas cuique: lege 10. §.primo ff. de adquir. rerum. {n} vide Infiit.&ff.de stipulatione seruorum. {o} §.3.Infiit.de hereditibus instituendis. {p} dicto §.3: lege 39.§.primo in fine: lege 89.§.secundo ff. de legatis 1. {q} In hæreditate, nihil mutatum: in legato mutatum, cum inuito seruus adquirat dicto §.tertio. {r} id est, Boultarius. Theophilus Infiit. de libertis, §.καὶ [illegible, ~40 letters] in bonis: [illegible, ~30 letters] iure Quiritium, ex iure Quiritium. Hæc ille, adde titul.§.16. §.eodem.
units.tr: {l} See Inst. per quas personas cuique adquiritur. {m} Inst. §3 per quas personas cuique; law 10 §1 Dig. de adquirendo rerum dominio. {n} See Inst. and Dig. de stipulatione servorum. {o} Inst. §3 de hereditatibus instituendis. {p} The same §3; law 39 §1 in fine; law 89 §2 Dig. de legatis 1. {q} In an inheritance nothing is changed; in a legacy it is changed, since a slave acquires even against the will of the person concerned. {r} That is, Boulharius. Theophilus, Inst. de libertis, §. [illegible passage] in bonis, [illegible passage] iure Quiritium, from quiritary right. Thus far he; add tit. §16, §eodem.

units.la: 2ī[?] Is quem bona fide possidemus, siue liber, siue alienus seruus sit, nobis adquirit ex duabus caussis tantùm, id est, quod ex re nostra, & quod ex operi-bus{a} suis adquirit: extra{b} has autem caussas, aut sibi adquirit, si liber sit: aut domino, si alienus seruus sit. Eadem sunt & in eo seruo, in quo tantùm vsumfructum habemus.
units.tr: 21 A slave whom we hold in good faith, whether free or another's slave, acquires for us on two grounds only: namely, what he acquires from our property, and what he acquires by his own labour. Apart from these grounds, he acquires for himself if he is free, or for his owner if he is another's slave. The same holds for a slave in whom we have only the usufruct.
ON WILLS
TITLE XX.

units.la: Estamentū est mentis nostrae iusta con-testatio{d}, in id soleniter factum, vt post mortem nostram valeat.
units.tr: A will is a solemn attestation of our mind, made formally so that it may stand after our death.

units.la: 2 Testamentorum genera fuerūt triae: vnum, quod calatis{f} Comitiis, alterum quod in procinctu{g}, tertium quod per{h} ꝰxs{i} & libram appellatum est. Illis duobus testamentis abolitis, hodie solum in vsu est, per xs & libram fit: id est, per mancipationem{k} imaginariam{l}: in quo testamento librīpens adhibetur, & familiae emptor, & non minus quàm quinque{m} testes, cum{n} quibus testamenti factio est.
units.tr: There were three kinds of wills: one made in the calata comitia, another in procinctu, and a third called per aes et libram. The first two are abolished, and today only the third is in use. It is made per aes et libram, that is, by an imaginary mancipation, in which a scale-holder (libripens) is present, a purchaser of the family (familiae emptor), and not fewer than five witnesses, with whom the testator has testamentary capacity.

units.la: 3 Qui in{o} potestate testatoris est, aut familiae sacrorum, aut flaminum: inaugurandorum causa. Eorum alia Curiatis (quae per lictorem Curiatim calari, i. conuocari moris erat) Cēuriata per cornicine. Calatis etiā sacrorū detestatio & testamenta fieri solebat. Gellius 15.27. calata comitia bis in anno fieri solita scribit, pacis tempore: calata dicì, ꝙ populꝰ ad ea vocetur. Est enim calari [illegible, ~2 letters] καλεῖν, Theoph.d.loco. Is autè ꝙ nō vniuersum populū, sed partem aliquam adesse iubet, non comitia, sed concilium edere iubet. Centuriata in campo Martio habebantur, non intra pomerium. Illud addendum est ex Lelio Fœlice, Curiata comitia fuisse, cum ex generibus omnium suffragium ferretur: Centuriata, cùm ex censu & aetate. Tributa, cùm ex regionibus & locis, 15.Gell.27.in f. Videtur tamen Festus in Centuriata, Centuriata & Curiata confundere. ꝙ cū in praelio exituri essent Instit.eo.§.1: cū viri ad praelia faciendum in acie vocabātur 15.Gell.27. h per familiae emancipationē, cui ēs & libra adhibebatur 15 Gell.27.
units.tr: Those who are in the power of the testator, whether of the family of sacred rites or of the flamines, cannot serve as witnesses, for the purpose of inauguration. Of these assemblies, one was the Curiata, which by the lictor was called Curiatim calari, that is, convened, as was the custom; another was the Centuriata, summoned through the horn-blower. Wills and the detestation of sacred rites were also customarily made in the calata. Gellius (15.27) writes that the calata comitia were customarily held twice a year in time of peace; they are called calata because the people are summoned to them. For calari is καλεῖν, as Theophilus says in the same place. But he who orders that not the whole people but some part be present orders a concilium to be held, not comitia. The Centuriata were held in the Campus Martius, not within the pomerium. This must be added from Lelius Felix: the Curiata comitia were held when the vote was given by the kinds of persons; the Centuriata when by census and age; the Tributa when by regions and places (Gellius 15.27, at the end). Yet Festus seems to confuse the Centuriata and the Curiata. When men were about to go out to battle, Inst. same title §1: when men were summoned to form the line for battle (Gellius 15.27). Through the emancipation of the family, at which the scale was also used (Gellius 15.27).

units.la: g cū in praelio exituri essent Instit.eo.§.1: cū viri ad praelia faciendum in acie vocabātur 15.Gell.27.
units.tr: g When men were about to go out to battle, Inst. same title §1: when men were summoned to form the line for battle (Gellius 15.27).

units.la: h per familiae emancipationē, cui ēs & libra adhibebatur 15 Gell.27.
units.tr: h Through the emancipation of the family, at which the scale was also used (Gellius 15.27).
i §1 Inst. same title. k emancipation, Gellius 15.27 §1, Inst. same title.
l See the last law, C. de adoptionibus.

units.la: m tit.19.§.3. S.eo. Hodie septe adhibēdi §.3.Inst.co.
units.tr: m Title 19 §3, same title. Today seven are to be employed: Inst. same title §3.
n §6 Inst. same title.

units.la: o §.9.Inst.e. emptoris, testis ad librx pensx adhiberi non potest. quoniam familiæ mancipatio inter {h}testatorem & familiæ emptorem fit: & ob id domestici {c}testes adhibendi non sunt.
units.tr: o §9 Inst. same title. A witness cannot be employed for the scale of the purchaser, since the mancipation of the family takes place between the testator and the purchaser of the family; for this reason household witnesses are not to be employed.

units.la: 4 Filio familiæ emente, pater {d}eius testis esse non potest.
units.tr: 4 If a son under power buys, his father cannot be a witness.

units.la: 5 Ex duobus fratribus {e}qui in eadem patris potestate sunt, alter familiæ emptor, alter testis esse non potest: quoniam quod unus ex his mancipium accipit, adquirit patri, cui filius suus testis esse non debet: pariter {f}& qui in potestate eius est constitutus.
units.tr: 5 Of two brothers who are in the same father's power, one cannot be the purchaser of the family and the other a witness: because what one of them receives by mancipation is acquired for the father, and the father's son ought not to be a witness; likewise one who is placed under his power.

units.la: 6 Duo fratres, qui in eiusdé patris potestate sunt, testes utrique, vel alter testis, alter libripes fieri possunt, alio {g}familiâ emente: quoniâ nihil {h}nocet ex vna domo plures testes alieno negotio adhiberi.
units.tr: 6 Two brothers in the same father's power may both be witnesses, or one a witness and the other scale-holder, if another buys the family; for it does no harm that several witnesses from one household be called to another's business.

units.la: 7 Mutus {i}, surdus {k}, furiosus {l}, pupillus {m}, fœmina {n}, neque familiæ emptor {o}, neque testis,libripens fieri potest.
units.tr: 7 A mute, a deaf person, a madman, a ward, or a woman cannot be purchaser of the family, witness, or scale-holder.

units.la: 8 Latinus Iunianus {p}, & familiæ emptor, & testis, & libripens fieri potest: quoniam cum eo testamenti factio est {q}.
units.tr: 8 A Latin Junian may be purchaser of the family, witness, and scale-holder, since testamentary capacity exists with him.

units.la: 9 In testamento, quod per æs & libram fit, duę {r}res aguntur, familiæ mancipatio, & nuncupatio testamenti. Nuncupatur {s}testamentum in hunc modum: Tabulas testamenti testator tenens ita dicit, Hæc uti hic tabulæ cerisve scripta sunt, ita do, ita legō, ita utitor, itaque vos, Quirites testimonium præbeatote. Quæ nuncupatio & testatio vocatur.
units.tr: 9 In a will made per aes et libram two things are done: the mancipation of the family and the nuncupation of the will. The will is nuncupated in this manner: the testator, holding the tablets of the will, says: As these tablets or waxes have been written, so I give, so I bequeath, so may you use, and therefore, Quirites, bear witness. This is called the nuncupation and attestation.

units.la: 10 Filius familiæ {u}testamentum facere non potest: quoniam nihil suum habet, vt testari de eo possit. Sed Diuus Augustus Marcus {x}constituit, vt filius familiæ miles {y}de eo peculio quod in castris adquisiit testamentum facere possit.
units.tr: 10 A son under power cannot make a will, since he has nothing of his own about which he could make a testament. But the divine Augustus and Marcus ordained that a soldier who is a son under power may make a will concerning the peculium he acquired in camp.

units.la: 11 Qui de {z}statu suo incertus est (facito quod patre peregrè mortuo, ignorat se sui iuris esse) testamentum facere non {a}potest.
units.tr: 11 One who is uncertain of his own status (for example, when his father has died abroad and he does not know that he is sui iuris) cannot make a will.

units.la: 12 Impubes {b}, licet sui iuris sit, testamentum {c}commercium habet {d}. §.4. {r}Quæ-nam agantur in testamento, per æs & libram. {s}Formula nuncupationis testamentariæ, {t}, cui adde l.58. ff. de hæredib. instit. {t}perhibetote. Apuleius 2: Vos in hanc rem, boni Quirites, testimonium perhibetote. {u}l.6.l.16.l.29.ff.qui testam. {x}superest Marcus Instit.quib.non est permiss.facere. {y}l.6.in f ff.de iniusto.l.22.ff.de testamento militis. {z}l.14. in f.l.15.ff.qui testamenta. {a}v.Nouell.Leonis 4. {b}§.1. Instit. quib. non est permiss: l.5.ff. qui testamenta.
units.tr: 12 A minor, although sui iuris, cannot make a will, since he does not yet have full judgment of mind. Concerning what is done in a will per aes et libram, the formula of the testamentary nuncupation, to which add l.58 ff. de hæredib. instit. Let them bear witness: Apuleius, book 2: "Bear witness to this matter, good Quirites." Marcus remains: Instit. quib. non est permiss. facere. Inst. quib. non est permiss: l.5 ff. qui testamenta.

units.la: p de quo ditum est tit.1. §.5. 5. eod: & tit.9. §.4. 5. eod.: tit.19. §.4. 5. eod. q & commercium habet d. §.4. r Quænam agantur in testamento, per æs & libram. s Formula nuncupationis testamentariæ, cui adde l.58. ff. de hæredib. instit. t perhibetote. Apuleius 2: Vos in hanc rem, boni Quirites, testimonium perhibetote. u l.6.l.16.l.29.ff.qui testam. x superest Marcus Instit.quib.non est permiss.facere. y l.6.in f ff.de iniusto.l.22.ff.de testamento militis. z l.14. in f.l.15.ff.qui testamenta. a v.Nouell.Leonis 4. b §.1. Instit. quib. non est permiss: l.5.ff. qui testamenta. facere non potest: quoniam nondum plenum iudicium animi habet.
units.tr: p Of whom it was said in title 1, §5, same title; and title 9, §4, same title; title 19, §4, same title. q and has commercium, d. §4. r What is done in a will per aes et libram. s The formula of testamentary nuncupation; add l.58 ff. de hæredib. instit. t Let them bear witness. Apuleius, book 2: "Bear witness to this matter, good Quirites." u l.6, l.16, l.29 ff. qui testamenta. x Marcus remains: Instit. quib. non est permiss. facere. y l.6 in f. ff. de iniusto; l.22 ff. de testamento militis. z l.14 in f.; l.15 ff. qui testamenta. a See Nov. Leonis 4. b §1 Instit. quib. non est permiss.; l.5 ff. qui testamenta. He cannot make a will, since he does not yet have full judgment of mind.

units.la: 13 Mutus , surdus , furiosus , itemque prodigus cui lege bonis interdictum est, testamentum facere non possunt: mutus, quoniam sverba loqui non potest: surdus, quoniam verba familiæ emptoris exaudire non potest: furiosus, quoniam mentem non habet, vt testari de eâ re possit: prodigus, quoniam commercium illi interdictū est, & ob id familiam mancipare non potest.
units.tr: 13 A mute, a deaf person, a madman, and likewise a prodigal who has been interdicted from his goods by law, cannot make a will: the mute, because he cannot speak the words; the deaf, because he cannot hear the words of the purchaser of the family; the madman, because he has no mind with which to make a will about the matter; the prodigal, because commercium is forbidden to him, and so he cannot mancipate the family.

units.la: 14 Latinus Iunianus, item is qui Deditiorum numero est testamentum facere non potest. Latinus quidem, quoniam nominatim lege Iunia prohibitus est, is autem qui Deditiorum numero est, quoniam ciuis Romanus testari potest, cum sit peregrinus : nec quasi peregrinus, quoniam nullius certæ ciuitatis, sciens vt aduersus pleges ciu tatis suæ testetur.
units.tr: 14 A Latin Junian, and likewise one who is among the Dediticii, cannot make a will. The Latin Junian, because he is expressly prohibited by the lex Iunia; the one among the Dediticii, because a Roman citizen can make a will although he is a foreigner, yet not as a foreigner, since he belongs to no certain state, so that he may make a will against the laws of his own state.

units.la: 15 Fœminæ post duodecimum annum ætatis testamenta facere possunt tutore auctore, donec in tutela sint.
units.tr: 15 Women after the twelfth year of age may make wills with a tutor's authority, for as long as they are under guardianship.

units.la: 16 Seruus publicus prætorisve, parte dimidia testamenti faciendi habet ius.
units.tr: 16 A public slave, or a slave of the praetor, has the right to make half of a will.

units.la: QVEMADMODVM HERES INSTITVI DEBEAT. Tit. XXI.
units.tr: HOW AN HEIR OUGHT TO BE INSTITUTED. Title XXI.

units.la: HERES institui redè potest his verbis , Titius heres esto, Titius heres sit, Titium heredem esse iubeo. Illa autem institutio, Latinus Iunianus testari non potest.
units.tr: An heir can validly be instituted in these words: "Titius heres esto," "Titius heres sit," "I order Titius to be heir." But a Latinus Junianus cannot make a will by that form of institution.

units.la: {v} Iunianus Latinus, post Iuniam legem, ex Latinis fit ciuis: vide tit.22.§.2. Heredem institut, Heredem facio, plerisque impro-bata est.
units.tr: A Junian Latin, after the Junian law, becomes a citizen out of the Latins: see title 22, §2. The phrases "Heredem instituo" and "Heredem facio" have been disapproved by most authorities.

units.la: QVI HEREDES INSTITVI POSSVNT. Tit. XXII.
units.tr: Who May Be Instituted Heirs. Title XXII.

units.la: HEREDES institui possunt, qui testa-menti factionem cum testatore habent.
units.tr: Heirs may be instituted if they have testamentary capacity with the testator.

units.la: 2 Deditiorum numero heres insti-tui non potest, quia peregrinus est, cum quo testamenti factio non est.
units.tr: 2 Someone among the dediticii cannot be instituted heir, because he is a foreigner, and there is no testamentary capacity with him.

units.la: 3 [Latinus Iunianus] si quidem mortis testa-toris tempore, vel intra diem cretionis ciuis Romanus sit, heres esse potest: quod si Latinus manserit, lege Iunia capere hereditatem prohibetur. Idē iuris est in persona cœlibis propter legem Iuliam.
units.tr: 3 [The Junian Latin]: if he is a Roman citizen at the time of the testator's death, or within the day of cretio, he can be heir; but if he remains a Latin, the Lex Junia forbids him to take the inheritance. The same law applies to a celibate person, because of the Lex Julia.

units.la: 4 Incerta persona heres institui non potest, veluti hoc modo: Quisquis primus ad funus meum venerit, heres esto: quoniam certum consilium debet esse testantis.
units.tr: 4 An uncertain person cannot be instituted heir, for example in this way: Whoever first comes to my funeral, let him be heir, since the testator's intention must be certain.

units.la: 5 Nec municipia, nec municipes heredes institui possunt: quoniam incertum corpus est, vt neque cernere vniuersi, neque pro libito de herede cernere possunt vt heredes fiant. Senatusconsulto tamen concessum est, vt a libertis suis heredes institui possint. Sed fideicommissa hereditas municipibus restitui potest: idque hoc senatusconsulto prospectum est.
units.tr: 5 Neither municipalities nor the citizens of municipalities can be instituted heirs, since the body is uncertain: they cannot all accept the inheritance together, nor can one of them accept on behalf of the others so as to become heir. By senatus consultum, however, it was allowed that they may be instituted heirs by their freedmen. But an inheritance held in trust may be restored to a municipality, and this was provided for by the same senatus consultum.

units.la: 6 Deos heredes instituere non possumus praeter eos, quos senatusconsulto, constitutionibus Principum instituere concessum est: sicuti Iouem heredem institui, nec praecipere rempublicam posse constat Cuiac. hic.
units.tr: 6 We cannot institute gods as heirs, except those whom it was allowed to institute by senatus consultum or by imperial constitutions. Thus it is established that Jupiter cannot be instituted heir, nor can the state take a legacy. Cuiac. hic.

units.la: Tarpeium a, Apollinem Didymæum b, sicuti Mar-tem in Gallia c, Mineruam Melienfem d, Herculem Gaditanum, e Dianam Ephesiam f, matrem deorum Cybelem g, eam quæ Smyrnæ colitur, & Cœle-ftum h Salinenfem Carthaginis. a ita dictus a Tarpeio mô-te. Tarpeius autem appel-latus fuit a Tarpeia vir-gine Vestali ab Sabineis necata, ibique sepulta. antea Saturnius mons, & in eo oppidum Saturnium, unde Saturnia terra. Postremo mons Capitolinus dictus quod cum fundamenta foderentur ædis Iouis, caput humanum inuentum fuit Varro 4. de lingua. b Appol-linis templum & oraculum quod Didymis fuit antiquum. Paufanias 7. in Achaicis eiusdem facit mentionem in 2, seu Corinthiacis, adde Strabone 9. & 11. c Galli quondam Mercurio coluere maxime, post hunc, Appolline & Marte & Iouem & Mineruam. Martem bella regere. Marti, cum præelio dimicare cœpifent, ea quæ bello cœpissent plerumque deuouebant; quæ supererant animalia capta immolabant, reliquas res in vnum locum conferebant v. Cæsar. 6. de bello Gallico. De diis veteris Gallorum v. P. Pitheum c. 1. aduerf. 3. d à Melio vrbe, non procul ab Euphrate: nisi malis hic legere Melitenfem. e de Gadibus & Hercule v. Strabonem 3. in f. fuit & alius cognomento Gallus & Ogmius: de quo v. Lucianum in Hercule. f v. act. 19. verf. 26. 27. de templo Dianæ Eufeb. 3 6. Plin. 14. g de qua dixi libro superiore. h Tertullianus 23. Apologet. Vnicuique, inquit, ctiam prouinciæ & ciuitati suus Deus est, vt Syriæ Aftartis, vt Arabiæ Diafares: vt Norico Tibilenus, vt Africæ Cœleftus, vt Mauritaniæ reguli fui & post, Cruftuminienfium Deluentinus, Narnienfiu Viridianus, Afculanorum Ancaria, Volfinienfiu Nurfia, Otriculanorum Valentia, Sutrinorum Nortia, Faliscorum Iuno Curilis & pater Curis. Sed nos foli arcemur à religionis proprietate. Hæc ille. Cui loco visum illud Arnobii 8. adiungere, Inde adeo per vniuersa imperia, prouincias, oppida videmus singulos sacrorum ritus gentiles habere, & deos colere municipes, & Eleufinos Cereres, Phrygas Magnam matrem, Epidaurios Æfculapium, Caldæos Belum, Aftarte Syros, Dianam Tauros, Gallos Mercurii, vniuersa Romanos. Porro quis fuerit Cœleftus an deus, an dea ambigitur. Petrus Pithæus 1. aduerf. 4. deam fuisse ait. Ammianus lib. 22. Aclepiades Philosophus cum visendi gratia Iuliani ad id suburbanum venisset, dex Cœlestis argenteum breue figmentum quocumque ibat secum solitum efferre, ante pedes statuit fimulachri sublimes, accensisque cereis ex vsu, fecit. Philaftrius Brixienfis in Catalogo hæref. Alia, inquit, hæreses in Iudæis quæ Reginam, quâ & Fortunam cœli nuncupant, quam & Cœlestem vocant in Africa. Tertullianus in Apologet. 23. Ita ipsa virgo Cœlestis, pluuiarum pollicitatrix. Saluianus, de gubernatione, Cœlestis illa. Idem 8. de prouidentia. Apul. 4. Floridor. Carthago, Africæ Musa Cœlestis. vt nō iniusta ratione possis dicere legendum esse apud Tertullianū in libro de virginibus, Cœlestis Africæ, non Ceres. Ambrof. 1. epistol. ad Valent.
units.tr: Tarpeius a; Apollo of Didyma b; Mars as worshipped in Gaul c; Minerva of Melite d; Hercules of Gades; e Diana of Ephesus f; the mother of the gods, Cybele g; the goddess who is worshipped at Smyrna; and Caelestis h of Salinae at Carthage. a He was so called from the Tarpeian rock. Tarpeius, moreover, was named from the Vestal virgin Tarpeia, who was killed by the Sabines and buried there; before that it was the Saturnian hill, and on it the town of Saturnium, whence the land of Saturnia. Finally, the Capitoline hill was so named because, when the foundations of the temple of Jupiter were being dug, a human head was found. Varro, De lingua Latina, book 4. b The temple and oracle of Apollo at Didyma, which was ancient. Pausanias, Achaica, book 7, or Corinthiaca, makes mention of it in book 2; add Strabo, books 9 and 11. c The Gauls once worshipped Mercury above all, and after him Apollo, Mars, Jupiter and Minerva. They held that Mars governed wars; to Mars, when they began to fight in battle, they generally devoted the things they were to win in war; the animals that remained after capture they sacrificed, and the rest of the goods they gathered into one place. Caesar, De bello Gallico, book 6. On the gods of the ancient Gauls, see Petrus Pithoeus, Adversaria 3, ch. 1. d From the city of Melos, not far from the Euphrates, unless you prefer to read here Melitensis. e On Gades and Hercules, see Strabo, book 3, at the end. There was also another, surnamed Gallus and Ogmius, about whom see Lucian, On Hercules. f See Acts 19:26–27; on the temple of Diana, Eusebius, book 3, ch. 6; Pliny, book 14. g Of whom I spoke in the previous book. h Tertullian, Apologeticus 23: "Each province and city, he says, has its own god: Astarte for Syria, Diasares for Arabia, Tibilenus for Noricum, Caelestis for Africa, and the petty kings of Mauretania have their own. And afterwards: Deluentinus of the people of Cruptumine, Viridianus of the Narnians, Ancaria of the Asculani, Nursia of the Volsinians, Valentia of the Otriculani, Nortia of the Sutrini, Juno Curilis and Father Quiris of the Falisci. But we alone are excluded from the peculiarity of religion." So he. To this passage it seemed good to add that of Arnobius, book 8: "From this we see that throughout all empires, provinces and towns the individual nations have their own rites and worship the gods of their localities: the Eleusinians Ceres, the Phrygians the Great Mother, the Epidaurians Aesculapius, the Chaldeans Belus, the Syrians Astarte, the Taurians Diana, the Gauls Mercury, and the Romans everything." Moreover, it is uncertain whether Caelestis was a god or a goddess. Petrus Pithoeus, Adversaria 1, ch. 4, says she was a goddess. Ammianus, book 22: when the philosopher Asclepiades had come to that suburban place to see Julian, he set up before the feet of the lofty statue of Caelestis a small silver ornament, which he always carried with him wherever he went, and lit candles in the customary way. Philastrius of Brescia, in his Catalogue of Heresies: "Another heresy among the Jews, who call the Queen of Heaven, also called Fortune of heaven, and in Africa call her Caelestis." Tertullian, Apologeticus 23: "Thus the virgin Caelestis herself, promiser of rains." Salvian, De gubernatione: "that Caelestis." The same, book 8, De providentia. Apuleius, Florida, book 4: "Carthage, the Muse Caelestis of Africa." So that you may not unjustly say that in Tertullian's book De virginibus one should read "Caelestis of Africa" and not "Ceres". Ambrose, Epistles, book 1, to Valentinian.

units.la: 7 Seruos heredes instituere possumus nostros cum † libertate: alienos, sine libertate: communes, cum libertate, vel sine libertate {a}.
units.tr: 7 We can institute our own slaves as heirs with freedom; other people's slaves without freedom; common slaves with or without freedom. {a}

units.la: 8 Eum seruum qui tantùm in bonis noster est, nec cum libertate heredem instituere possumus, quia Latinitatem consequitur: quod non proficit ad hereditatem capiendam {b}.
units.tr: 8 We cannot institute as heir a slave who is ours only in goods, not even with freedom, because he attains Latin status, which does not help him to take an inheritance. {b}

units.la: 9 Alienos seruos heredes instituere possumus: eos tamen, quorum cum dominis testamenti factio nem habemus.
units.tr: 9 We can institute other people's slaves as heirs, but only those with whose masters we have testamentary capacity.

units.la: 10 Communis seruus cum libertate rectè quidem heres instituitur, quasi proprius, pro parte nostra: sine libertate autem, quasi alienus, propter socij partem.
units.tr: 10 A common slave instituted heir with freedom is rightly instituted, as though he were our own, for our share; without freedom, however, he is instituted as though he were another's, on account of the partner's share.

units.la: 11 Proprius seruus cum libertate heres institutus, si c quidem in eadem causa permanserit, ex testamento liber & heres fit, id est necessarius.
units.tr: 11 A slave of our own instituted heir with freedom, if he remains in the same condition, becomes free and heir by the will; that is, a necessary heir.

units.la: 12 Quòd si ab ipso testatore viuente manumissus, vel alienatus fit: suo arbitrio, vel iussu emptoris hereditatem adire potest. Sed si sine libertate fit institutus, omnino non confiat institutio.
units.tr: 12 But if he is manumitted or alienated by the testator while the testator is still living, he may take up the inheritance at his own discretion or at the command of the buyer. But if he is instituted without freedom, the institution is not valid at all.

units.la: 13 Alienuse seruus heres institutus, si quidem in ea causa permanserit iussu domini debet heredi tatem adire. Quòd si viuo testatore manumissus, aut alienatus à domino fuerit: aut suo arbitrio, aut iussu emptoris poterit adire hereditatem.
units.tr: 13 A slave of another person instituted heir, if he remains in that condition, must take up the inheritance at the command of his master. But if he is manumitted, or alienated by his master, while the testator is alive, he may take up the inheritance either at his own discretion or at the command of the buyer.

units.la: 14 Sui heredes instituendi sunt, vel exheredan di. Sui autem heredes sunt liberi quos in potestate habemus, tam naturales, quàm adoptiui: item vxor quæ in {g} manu est, & nurus quæ in manu est filij, quem in potestate habemus.
units.tr: 14 Heirs-in-the-family must be instituted or disinherited. Heirs-in-the-family are the children whom we have in our power, both natural and adopted; likewise the wife who is in manus, and the daughter-in-law who is in the manus of a son whom we have in our power.

units.la: 15 Posthumi {h} quoque liberi, id est, qui in vte ro sunt, si tales sunt, vt nati in potestate nostra su turi sint, suorum heredum numero sunt.
units.tr: 15 Posthumous children also, that is, those in the womb, if they are such that when born they would be in our power, belong to the number of heirs-in-the-family.

units.la: 16 Ex suis heredibus filius quidem neque he res institutus, neque nominatim exheredatus, non Vxor, inquit, quæ in manu eius est, Is sua hæres est: quia filiæ loco est. Item nurus quæ in filij manu est, nam & hæc neptis loco est. Sed ita demum erit sua hæres, si filius cuius in manu erit, dum pater moritur, in potestate eius non fit. Idemque dicimus & de ea quæ in nepotis manu matrimonij causa fit, quia proneptis loco est. {h} Posthumi quoque, qui si viuo parente nati essent in potestate eius futuri forent, sui heredes sunt Caius d. loco patitur
units.tr: 16 Of the heirs-in-the-family, a son who is neither instituted nor expressly disinherited, and the wife, he says, who is in his manus, is his heir, because she takes the place of a daughter. Likewise the daughter-in-law who is in the manus of a son, for she too takes the place of a granddaughter. But she will be an heir-in-the-family only if the son in whose manus she is does not pass out of his father's power while the father dies. And we say the same of her who is in the manus of a grandson for the sake of marriage, because she takes the place of a great-granddaughter. Posthumous children also, who, if born while the parent was alive, would have been in his power, are heirs-in-the-family. Gaius, d, takes the place of ... [continued at the foot of the page].

units.la: {h} Caius d. loco. [Continuation of the sentence at the foot of the page.] patitur valere testamentú. Reliquæ vero personæ li-berorum,velut filia, nepos, neptis, si prætereritæ sint, valet testamentum.
units.tr: Gaius, d, takes the place of: [continuation of the sentence at the foot of the page] allows the will to stand. But the other persons of children, such as a daughter, grandson or granddaughter, if they have been passed over, the will stands valid.

units.la: 17 Scriptis a heredibus adcrescunt, suis quidem heredibus in partem virilem, extraneis autem in partem dimidiam.
units.tr: 17 Written heirs accrue to heirs-in-the-family: to our own heirs in a male share, and to strangers in a half share.

units.la: 18 Posthumi, quoque liberi cuiuscumque b sexus omissi, quod valuit testamentú, agnatione rumpitur c.
units.tr: 18 Posthumous children of either sex who have been omitted break the will that was valid, by agnation.

units.la: 19 Eos qui in utero{d} sunt, si nati sui heredes nobis futuri sunt, possumus instituere heredes: si{e} quidem post mortem nostram nascantur, ex iure civilij{f}: si vero viventibus nobis, ex lege Iulia{g}.
units.tr: 19 Those in the womb, if when born they will be our heirs-in-the-family, we can institute as heirs: if they are born after our death, under the civil law; but if while we are still living, under the Lex Julia.

units.la: 20 Filius qui in potestate est, si nō instituatur he-res,nominatim exheredari debet: reliqui sui heredes utriusque sexus aut nominatim, aut inter{h} caeteros.
units.tr: 20 A son who is in his father's power, if he is not instituted heir, must be disinherited by name. Other sui heredes of either sex must be disinherited either by name or among the rest.

units.la: 21 Posthumus filius nominatim exheredandus est: filia posthuma, cæteræque posthumæ fœminæ vel nominatim, vel inter cæteros {k}: dummodo inter cæteros exheredatis aliquid legetur.
units.tr: 21 A posthumous son must be disinherited by name. A posthumous daughter and other posthumous females may be disinherited either by name or among the rest, provided that something is bequeathed to those disinherited among the rest.

units.la: 22 Nepotes & pronepotes, cæterique masculi posthumi præter filium, vel nominatim, vel inter cæteros cum adiectione legati sunt exheredandi: sed tutius{l} est tamen nominatim eos exheredari: & id obseruatur magis.
units.tr: 22 Grandsons and great-grandsons, and other posthumous males besides a son, must be disinherited either by name, or among the rest with the addition of a legacy. It is safer, however, to disinherit them by name, and this is the practice more commonly observed.

units.la: 23 Mancipatos{m} liberos cum iure civili neque heredes instituere, neque exheredare necesse sit, tamē [illegible, ~4 letters] iubet: si non instituantur heredes, exheredari masculos omnes nominatim, fœminas vel inter
units.tr: 23 It is not necessary, under civil law, either to institute emancipated children as heirs or to disinherit them. Yet [illegible] directs that if they are not instituted heirs, all the males are to be disinherited by name, and the females either by name or among the rest.

units.la: a legendum est, sed scriptis eo sensu. Iure antiquo, filiarum nepotes, præ-teriri potuis-se, sed nec testamentum ex causa præteritionis infirmasse[?], cùm illis consultú ita foret. Nam scriptis concurrebat: suis quidem, in virilem: extraneis, in dimidiam. & hoc est quod ȝ[?] Triboniano obscure scriptum est, Ius adcrescendi eis ad centa por-tionem præ-stium Instit. de exhæredat.
units.tr: a This should be read as written, but in that sense. Under the ancient law, the grandchildren through daughters could be passed over, but the will was not invalidated on account of the omission, since provision had been made for them in that way. For in the writings it worked thus: for the sui heredes in equal shares per head, for strangers in half. This is what Tribonian wrote obscurely, that the right of accrual to them extends to the full portion. Inst. de exheredat.

units.la: b ut in eo par fit masculorum & fœminarum conditio §.1. Instit. de exhæredat. liber.
units.tr: b So that in this respect the position of males and females is equal. §1 Inst. de exheredat. liber.
c They break (the will).

units.la: d Posthumi, hæredes instituí possunt l.4. l.5. l.14. l.27. l.29. ff. de liber. & posthum.
units.tr: d Posthumous children can be instituted heirs: laws 4, 5, 14, 27 and 29 ff. de liber. et posthum.

units.la: e Dux posthumorum species. alij n. post mortem testatoris nascuntur: alij post testamentum vivo testatore l.3. §.2. ff. de iniusto.
units.tr: e There are two kinds of posthumous children. For some are born after the testator's death, others after the will is made while the testator is still alive. l.3 §2 ff. de iniusto.

units.la: f idest legibus x 11. tabularum, quod ius antiquum à Scæuola dicitur in lege 29. §.7. ff. de liberis & posthumis: habita ratione ad legem Velleam.
units.tr: f That is, by the laws of the Twelve Tables, which ancient law Scaevola calls in law 29 §7 ff. de liberis et posthumis, with regard had to the Velleian senatusconsult.

units.la: g Vellea sc. §.2. Instit. de exhæred. liberor: l.29. ff. de liberis.
units.tr: g The Velleian, namely §2 Inst. de exheredat. liberorum; l.29 ff. de liberis.

units.la: h Instit. de exhæredat. liber. verf. sed non ita in f: Inter cæteros exhæredare, est ἀοριστῶς[?] siue indefinite exhæredare. fuit autem hæc formula, Cæteri exhæredes sunto. Theophil. Inst. de exhæredat. liber: l.23. ff. de liberis. & opponitur inter cæteros exhæredatio, ei quæ nominatim fit §.21. l.eo. Nominatim exhæredatio longè diversa ab indefinita, & generali exhæredatione, de qua v. l.2. l.3. ff. de liberis.
units.tr: h Inst. de exheredat. liber., at "sed non ita" in f. To disinherit among the rest is to disinherit indefinitely [ἀοριστῶς], that is, without naming. The formula was: "Let the others be disinherited." Theophilus, Inst. de exheredat. liber.; l.23 ff. de liberis. Disinheritance among the rest is set against disinheritance made by name, §21 of the same title. Disinheritance by name is very different from indefinite and general disinheritance, on which see l.2 and l.3 ff. de liberis.

units.la: i §.1. in f. Instit. de exhæredat. liber.
units.tr: i §1 in f. Inst. de exheredat. liber.

units.la: k Ix hoc quid essent dixi ad §.20. §. eod.[?]
units.tr: k On what these were, I spoke at §20 of this title.

units.la: l §.1. in f. Instit. de exhæredat. liberor.
units.tr: l §1 in f. Inst. de exheredat. liberorum.

units.la: m ȝ, emancipationis §.3. Instit. de exhæredat. liberor. exteros: alioqui contra tabulas bonorum possessionem eis pollicetur.
units.tr: m Emancipation: §3 Inst. de exheredat. liberorum. Otherwise he grants them possession of goods against the tablets.

units.la: 24 Inter necessarios heredes, id est, seruos cum libertate heredes scriptos, & suos scilicet necessarios, id est, liberos qui in potestate sunt, iure ciuili nihil interest (nam utrique etiam inuiti heredes fiunt), sed iure praetorio suis & necessariis heredibus abstinere se a parentis hereditate permittitur: necessarius autem tantum heredibus abstinendi potestas non datur.
units.tr: 24 Between necessary heirs, that is, slaves instituted heirs with their freedom, and their own necessary heirs, that is, the children who are in power, there is no difference under civil law, for both become heirs even against their will. Under praetorian law, however, sui and necessary heirs are permitted to abstain from their parent's inheritance. The necessary heir, however, is not given the mere power of abstaining.

units.la: 25 Extraneus heres, si quidem cum cretione fit heres institutus, cernendo fit heres: si vero sine cretione, pro herede gerendo.
units.tr: 25 An external heir, if he is instituted with cretion, becomes heir by cernere (accepting). If without cretion, he becomes heir by acting as heir.

units.la: 26 Pro herede gerit, qui rebus hereditariis tanquam dominus utitur: velut qui actionem rum hereditariarum facit: aut seruis hereditariis ciuitatem [?] baria mandat.
units.tr: 26 One acts as heir who uses the hereditary goods as if he were owner: for example, one who brings the hereditary actions, or who gives orders to the hereditary slaves.

units.la: 27 Cretio est certorum dierum spacium, quod datur instituto heredi ad deliberandum: utrum expediat ei ad rehereditatem, necne, velut Titius heres esto cernito quin in diebus centum proximis, quibus scieris potcrit [?] sque: ita creuerit exheres esto.
units.tr: 27 Cretion is a space of certain days given to the instituted heir for deliberation, whether it is advantageous for him to take up the inheritance or not. For example: "Let Titius be heir and accept within the next hundred days, on which you know and are able. If he does not accept in this way, let him be disinherited."

units.la: 28 Cernere est verba cretionis dicere, ad hunc modum: Cum me Maeuius heredem instituerit, eam hereditatem adeo cernoque.
units.tr: 28 To cernere is to speak the words of cretion, in this manner: "Since Maevius has instituted me heir, I accept that inheritance and so I accept it."

units.la: 29 Sine cretione heres institutus, si conscituerit se heredem esse, statim excluditur ab hereditate, amplius eam adire non potest.
units.tr: 29 An heir instituted without cretion, if he declares that he is heir, is at once excluded from the inheritance and can no longer enter it.

units.la: 30 Cum cretione vero heres institutus, sicut cernendo fit heres, ita non aliter excluditur, quam si pro emptore.
units.tr: 30 An heir instituted with cretion, just as he becomes heir by accepting, is excluded in no other way than by acting as a buyer would.

units.la: † Cretiones hodie sublatae sunt l.17.C.de iure deliberandi.
units.tr: † Cretions have been abolished today. l.17 C. de iure deliberandi.

units.la: h Formula instituendi cum cretione. i id est, facito vt videat te heredem Varro 5.de lingua. k Cicero 1.de Orator. vt in cretionibus scribi solet, quibus sciam potestque.
units.tr: h The formula for instituting with cretion. i.e. "See to it that he sees you as heir," Varro 5 de lingua. k Cicero 1 de Orat.: "as is customary to write in cretions: on which you know and are able."

units.la: l Cernere, est quasi decernere se heredem esse velle l.13 §.penult.ff.de adquir.haered: cuius rei facultas non est in pupillo l.9.ff.de adquir.haered.
units.tr: l To cernere is, as it were, to decide to be heir. l.13 §penult. ff. de adquir. haered. The power of doing this does not belong to a pupil. l.9 ff. de adquir. haered.

units.la: m Formula cernendi. Huius loci vetustia sunt apud Varronem 5. de lingua. In cretione adhiberi iubet testes & lib. 6. Heres cum constituit se heredem esse, dicitur cernere: & cum id fecerit, creuisse. Varroni respondet Cicero 13.ad Atticum, Cretionem fieri testibus praesentibus. Fiebat etiam verbis solennibus vt hic: & l.51. in sin.ff.de adquir.haered.pure fit. est enim actus legitimus l.77. ff. de regul.iur: & semel l.80.in f. ff.de adquir. haered: non per alium l.90. ff. de adquir.haered.
units.tr: m The formula of cernere. The oldest examples of this place are in Varro, 5 de lingua. He orders witnesses to be used in cretion, and in book 6: "When someone decides that he is heir, he is said to cernere, and when he has done so, to have accepted." Cicero, 13 ad Atticum, answers Varro: cretion is made with witnesses present. It was also done with solemn words, as here. And l.51 in fin. ff. de adquir. haered.: it is done purely, for it is a legitimate act, l.77 ff. de regul. iur.; and once only, l.80 in f. ff. de adquir. haered.; not through another, l.90 ff. de adquir. haered.

units.la: Eius symbolum, digitorum percussio dixi ad epigraphen tituli de verb. oblig. † dixi superius, sublatam cretionis scrupulositatem l.17.C.de iure deliberandi. intra diem cretionis non creuererit: ideoque etiam si constituerit nolle fe heredem esse, tamen fi super-sint dies cretionis, pœnitentia actus, cernendo heres fieri potest.
units.tr: Its sign is the striking of the fingers. I spoke of this at the epigraph of the title de verb. oblig. † I said above that the scrupulosity of cretion was abolished, l.17 C. de iure deliberandi. If he has not accepted within the day of cretion, then even if he has decided that he is unwilling to be heir, yet, if days of cretion remain, by repentance of the act he can become heir by accepting.

units.la: 31 Cretio autem vulgaris dicitur, aut continua. Vulgaris {a}in qua adiiciuntur hæc verba, Quibus scie ru,poterisque. Continua{b}, in qua non adiiciuntur.
units.tr: 31 Cretion is called either common or continuous. Common cretion is that in which these words are added: "on which you know and are able." Continuous cretion is that in which they are not added.

units.la: 32 Ei qui vulgarem cretionem habet, dies illi dati computantur quibus scit se heredem institutum esse,& potuit cernere. Ei vero qui continuam habet cretionem, etiam illi dies computantur quibus{c} i-gnorauit se heredem institutum, aut sciuit,sed non potuit cernere.
units.tr: 32 For one who has common cretion, the days given to him are counted from the day on which he knows that he has been instituted heir and was able to accept. For one who has continuous cretion, the days are counted also from the time when he was ignorant that he had been instituted, or knew it but was not able to accept.

units.la: 33 Heredes aut{d} instituti dicuntur, aut substituti: instituti,qui primo gradu scripti sunt: substituti,qui fecundo gradu,vel sequentibus.
units.tr: 33 Heirs are called either instituted or substituted. Instituted heirs are those written in the first degree; substituted heirs are those written in the second degree or in the following ones.

units.la: 34 Heredes scripti sunt, veluti{e}: Titius heres esto, cernitoque in diebus proximis centum quibus scieris, poterisque. Nisi ita creueris, exheres esto: tunc Mœuius heres esto, cernitoque in diebus, & reliqua. Similiter & deinceps substitui poterit.
units.tr: 34 Heirs are written thus: "Let Titius be heir, and let him accept within the next hundred days, on which you know and are able. If he does not accept in this way, let him be disinherited; then let Maevius be heir and accept within the days," and so on. Likewise one may be substituted further down the line.

units.la: 35 Si sub imperfectam{f} cretionem heres institutus fit, id est, non adiectis his verbis{g}, Si non creueris, exheres esto: sed si ita{h}, si non creueris, tunc Mœuius heres esto: cernendo quidem, superior inferiorem excludit: non cernendo autem{i}, sed pro herede gerendo, in partem admittit substitutum. Sed posteā Di-uus Marcus constituit, vt & pro herede gerendo, ex{k} asse fiat heres. Quòd si neque creuerit, neque pro he-rede gesserit, ipse excluditur,& substitutus ex asse fit heres.
units.tr: 35 If someone is instituted heir under an imperfect cretion, that is, without these words, "if you do not accept, let him be disinherited," but with these: "if he does not accept, then let Maevius be heir," then by accepting, the first heir excludes the second; but by not accepting, yet acting as heir, he admits the substitute to a share. Afterwards, however, the divine Marcus decided that even by acting as heir the substitute becomes heir to the whole as. If he neither accepts nor acts as heir, he himself is excluded and the substitute becomes heir to the whole as.
In what ways wills are broken. Title 23.

units.la: {g} Formula perfectæ cretionis. {h} Formula imperfectæ cretionis.
units.tr: {g} Form of perfect cretion. {h} Form of imperfect cretion.

units.la: {i} Nota veterem differentiam cernendi & pro hærede gerendi. Qui cernebat, excludebat inferiorem: qui pro hærede gerebat, in partem admittebat substitutum.
units.tr: {i} Note the old difference between cernere (to enter on the inheritance) and acting as heir (pro herede gerere). He who made cretion excluded the inferior heir; he who acted as heir admitted the substitute to a share.
{k} 28 ff. j: §1 Instit. quib. mod. test. sam. [?]

units.la: TESTAMENTVM[?] iure factum infirmatur duobus modis, si ruptum{a} aut irritum{b} factum fit.
units.tr: A will made lawfully is invalidated in two ways: if it is broken (ruptum) or made void (irritum).

units.la: 2 Rumpitur testamentum mutatio-ne, id est, si postea aliud{c} testamentum iure factum sit: item agnatione{d}, id est, si suus he-res agnascatur, qui neque heres institutus, neque ut oportet, exheredatus sit.
units.tr: A will is broken (1) by change, that is, if another will is afterwards made lawfully; and (2) by agnation, that is, if a suus heres is born after the making, who was neither instituted heir nor properly disinherited.

units.la: 3 Adnascitur suus heres, aut{e} agnascendo, aut adoptando, aut in manum conveniendo, aut in{f} lo-cum sui heredis succedendo: velut nepos mortuo fi-lio, vel emancipato: aut manumissione id est, si filius ex prima secundave mancipatione manumissus, re-uersus sit in patris potestatem.
units.tr: A suus heres is added (1) by agnation, (2) by adoption, (3) by coming into the hand (manus), or (4) by succeeding into the place of a suus heres: as a grandson does when his son has died or been emancipated; or (5) by manumission, that is, if a son, manumitted after the first or second mancipation, returns into his father's power.

units.la: 4 Irritum{g} sit testamentum, si testator capite di-minutus{h} fuerit aut si iure facto testamento nemo extiterit heres.
units.tr: A will is void (irritum) if the testator has suffered loss of civil status (capitis deminutio), or if, when a will has been lawfully made, no one comes forward as heir.

units.la: 5 Si is qui testamentum fecit, ab{i} hostibus captus sit, testamentum eius valet: si quidem{k} reuer-sus fuerit, iure postliminij, si non{l} ibi decesserit, ex lege Corneliana, quae perinde successionem eius con-firmat, atque si in civitate decessisset.
units.tr: If the one who made the will is taken captive by enemies, his will is valid: if indeed he returns, by the right of postliminy; if he dies there, under the lex Cornelia, which confirms his succession just as if he had died in the state.

units.la: 6 Si{m} septem signis testium signatum{n} testamentum, licet iure civili ruptum vel irritum factum sit, Praetor scriptis heredibus iuxta tabulas bonorum possessionem dat, si testator & civis Romanus, & suae potestatis cum moreretur fuit, quae bonorum possessio cum re, id est, cum effectu habetur, si nemo alius iure heres sit.
units.tr: If a will has been sealed with the seals of seven witnesses, then although it has been broken or made void by civil law, the praetor gives the instituted heirs possession of the goods according to the tablets, provided the testator was both a Roman citizen and under his own power when he died. This possession of goods is held to be effective (cum re), that is, with effect, if no one else is heir by law.

units.la: 7 Liberis{o} impuberibus in potestate manentibus tam natis quam posthumis, heredes substituere parentes possunt duplici modo: id est, aut eo quo extraneis, ut si heredes non extiterint liberi, substitutus heres fiat: aut proprio iure, id est, si post mortem parentis heredes facti intra pubertatem decesserint, substitutus heres fiat.
units.tr: While children who are still under age remain in power, both those born and posthumous, parents can substitute heirs in two ways: either in the way they can for strangers, so that if the children do not become heirs, the substitute becomes heir; or by their own right, that is, if the children who became heirs after the parent's death die before puberty, the substitute becomes heir.

units.la: 8 Etiam exheredatis{p} filiis substituere parenti-bus licet.
units.tr: Parents may also substitute heirs for sons who have been disinherited.

units.la: 9 Non aliter impuberi filio substituere quis heredem potest, quàm{q} si sibi quis heredem instituerit, vel ipsum filium, vel quemlibet alium.
units.tr: One cannot substitute an heir for an impubescent son except on condition that one has instituted as heir either the son himself or some other person.
{t} But if: the reading seems to be this.
{m} §6 Instit. quib. mod. testam.
{n} l.12 ff. de iniusto:
{o} v. Instit. de pupillari substit.
{p} l.1 §2 ff. de vulgari: §4 Instit. de pupillari.

units.la: {q} d.l.1. §.vlt. §.5. Instit.de pupil. {ro}Milites quomodocunque {a}fecerint testamen-ta, valent, id est, etiam sine legitima obseruatione. Nam principalibus {b}constitutionibus permissum est illis, quomodocunque vellent, quomodocunque possent, testari. Idque testamentum quod mi-les contra iuris regulam fecit, ita demum valet, si vel in {c}castris mortuus sit, vel post missionem in-tra {d}annum.
units.tr: {q} d.l.1 §ult. §5 Instit. de pupil. {ro} Soldiers, however they have made their wills, are valid, that is, even without the legal formalities. For by imperial constitutions it was permitted to them to make a will however they wished and however they could. And that will which a soldier made contrary to the rule of law is valid only if he died in camp or within a year after his discharge.
ON LEGACIES. TITLE 24.

units.la: {e}LEGATVM est quod legis modo, id est, imperatiuè, testamento relinqui-tur. Nam ea quæ precatione modo relin-quuntur,fideicommissa vocantur.
units.tr: A legacy is that which is left in a will in the form of a command, that is, imperatively. Those things which are left by way of request are called fideicommissa.

units.la: 2 Legamus autem quatuor {g}modis, per vindicationem {h}, per damnationem {i}, sinendi modo {k},per præceptionem {l}.
units.tr: 2 There are four ways of bequeathing: by vindication, by damnation, by the mode of permitting, and by preception.

units.la: 3 Per vindicationē {m}his verbis legamus, Do, le-go,capito,sumito,siue habeto.
units.tr: 3 A bequest by vindication is made in these words: "I give, I bequeath, let him take, let him have."

units.la: 4 Per damnationem {n}his verbis:Heres meus da-mnas esto dare,dato,facito, heredem meum dare iubeo.
units.tr: 4 A bequest by damnation is made in these words: "Let my heir be bound to give, to hand over, or to do; I order my heir to give a man."

units.la: 5 Sinendi {o}modo ita,Heres meus damnas esto si-nere Lucium Titium sumere illam rem,sibique habere.
units.tr: 5 By the mode of permitting, it is done thus: "Let my heir be bound to allow Lucius Titius to take that thing and to have it for himself."

units.la: 6 Per præceptionem {p}sic,Lucius Titius illam rem præcipito.
units.tr: 6 By preception, thus: "Let Lucius Titius take that thing beforehand."

units.la: 7 Per vindicationem legari possunt res quæ utroque {q}tempore ex iure Quiritium testatoris fue-runt {r},mortis,& quando testamentum faciebat:præ-terquam si pondere,mensura,numero contineantur: in his enim satis est, si vel mortis duntaxat tempore fuerint ex iure Quiritium.
units.tr: 7 Things which belonged to the testator under Quiritary law at both times, that is, at his death and when he made the will, can be bequeathed by vindication, except those which are contained by weight, measure, or number; for in these it is enough that they belonged to him under Quiritary law at the time of death alone.
Passages cited: Paul. 4 Sent. 1 §6. g §1 Inst. de legat. 2. Gaius 5 §1.
h §3 l. eod. i §4 l. eod. k §5 l. eod. l §6 l. eod.
m 2 Gaius 5 §2; §2 Inst. de legatis; Paul. 3 Sent. 6 §§3 and 7.
n 2 Gaius 5 §§3, 4, 5, 6; §2 Inst. de legat.; Paul. 3 Sent. 6 §§3 and 10.

units.la: {o} 2.Caius 2.§.7:§.2.Instit.de legat:Paul. 3.sent.6. §.11. {p} 2.Caius 5: §.8.& 2.Instit.de legat.Paul. 3.sent. §.6. hoc & præ legatum dicitur & præcipuum,Sidonius 6.epistol.Illud autem deberi tibi quo dam,vt Iurisconsulti dicunt, præcipui titulo. {q} §. 11. 1.eod.
units.tr: o 2 Gaius 2 §7; §2 Inst. de legat.; Paul. 3 Sent. 6 §11. p 2 Gaius 5; §8 and 2 Inst. de legat.; Paul. 3 Sent. §6. This is called both a prelegacy and a preciput, as in Sidonius, Epist. 6: "But that is owed to you under the title of preciput, as the jurists say." q §11 l. 1 eod.

units.la: {r} & ita per vindicationē res aliena relinqui nō potest 2.Caius 5.§.3.
units.tr: r And thus a thing belonging to another cannot be bequeathed by vindication: 2 Gaius 5 §3.

units.la: 8 Per damnationem omnes res legari possunt, & iam quæ non sunt testatoris, dummodo tales sint, quæ dari possint.
units.tr: 8 All things can be bequeathed by damnation, even those which are not the testator's, provided they are such as can be given.

units.la: 9 Liber homo,aut res populi,aut sacra, aut religiosa,nec per damnationem legari potest:quoniam & non potest.
units.tr: 9 A free man, or public property, or sacred or religious things, cannot be bequeathed by damnation, since they cannot be given either.

units.la: 10 Sinendi modo legari possunt res proprię testatoris & heredis eius.
units.tr: 10 Things which are the testator's own and his heir's own can be bequeathed by the mode of permitting.

units.la: 11 Per præceptionem legari possunt res quæ ctiam per vindicationem. Si ea res quæ non fuit vtro- que tempore testatoris ex iure Quiritium,per vindicationem legata fit,licet iure ciuili non valeat legatum, tamen senatusconsulto Neroniano firmatur: quo cautum est, vt quod minus pa&is e verbis legatum est.perinde fit , ac si optimo iure legatum effet. Optimum f autem ius legati per damnationem est.
units.tr: 11 Things which can be bequeathed by vindication can be bequeathed by preception. If a thing which did not belong to the testator under Quiritary law at both times is bequeathed by vindication, the legacy, though invalid under civil law, is confirmed by the Senatus consultum Neronianum, which provides that a legacy made in words less than full is treated as if it had been made by the best law. The best law for a legacy, however, is that of damnation.

units.la: 12 Si duobus eadem res per vindicationem legatur: si fit:si quidem disiunctim, singulis in solidum & dei- bentur:si vero coniunctim,velut Titio & Seio,homi- nem Stichum do,lego, iure ciuili concursu partes fie- bant. non concurrente altero pars eius alteri adcre- scebat.Sed post legem Papiam Popeam,non capietis pars caduca fit.
units.tr: 12 If the same thing is bequeathed to two persons by vindication: if it is done disjunctively, the whole is owed to each of them; but if conjunctively, as "to Titius and Seius, I give and bequeath the slave Stichus," then under civil law the shares were merged by concurrence, and if one of them did not take, his share accrued to the other. But since the Lex Papia Poppaea, the share of one who cannot take becomes caducous.

units.la: 13 Si per damnationem eadem res duobus legata fit,siquidem coniunctim, singulis partes debentur, & non capientis pars iure ciuili in hereditatem re- manebat,nunc autem caduca fit:quod fi disiunctim, singulis in solidum debetur.
units.tr: 13 If the same thing is bequeathed to two persons by damnation: if conjunctively, each is owed a share, and the share of one who cannot take remained in the inheritance under civil law, but now it becomes caducous; but if disjunctively, the whole is owed to each.

units.la: 14 Oprione autem legati, per vindicationem da- ta,legatarij electio est , veluti , Hominem optato,eli- gito.Idem que est, & si tacite legauerim. Titium mo- hominem aut decem heres meus dato:hominem da- re heredis electio est.
units.tr: 14 Moreover, when a thing is given by vindication with an option, the choice belongs to the legatee, as in "Choose a man," or "Let my heir give you a man or ten." The same holds if I have bequeathed tacitly. But if I have said, "Let my heir give a man," the choice belongs to the heir.

units.la: Sic optimum ius vsurarum l.1. Cod. de vsu: optimum ius possessionis l. 26. §.1.ff. de pignorib. l id est non data optione. n homine. At si ita heres meus damnas esto hominem dare, heredis electio est Cuiac.hic. Similiter in legatis disiunctiuis electio est legatarij,si per vindicationem,l.94.§.1.ff.de legat.1: l.23. ff.de legat.2,heredi,si per damnationem l.43 in f.ff.de legat.2.
units.tr: Thus the best law of usufructs: l. 1 Cod. de usu; the best law of possession: l. 26 §1 ff. de pignoribus; that is, when no option is given regarding a man. But if it is said, "Let my heir be bound to give a man," the choice belongs to the heir: Cuiacius here. Similarly, in disjunctive legacies the choice belongs to the legatee if by vindication: l. 94 §1 ff. de legat. 1; l. 23 ff. de legat. 2; to the heir if by damnation: l. 43 in fine ff. de legat. 2.

units.la: 15 Ante heredis institutionem legari non {†} potest: quoniam & potestas testamenti ab heredis institutione incipit.
units.tr: 15 A legacy cannot be made before the institution of the heir, since the power of a will begins with the institution of the heir.

units.la: 16 Post mortem heredis legari non potest {†}, ne ab heredi herede legari videatur: quod iuris civilis ratio non patitur. In mortis autem heredis tempus legari potest: velut cum heres moriatur.
units.tr: 16 A legacy cannot be made after the death of the heir, lest it appear to be left by the heir's heir, which the reason of civil law does not allow. But a legacy may be made for the time of the heir's death, as in "when the heir dies."

units.la: 17 Pœnæ caussa legari non potest. {†} Pœnæ autem caussa legatur: quod coercendi heredis caussa relinquitur, vt faciat quidem aut non faciat, non vt legatum perrineat: vt puta hoc modo, Si filiam tuam in matrimonio Titio conlocaueris, decem millia Scio dato.
units.tr: 17 A legacy cannot be made for the sake of a penalty. A legacy is made for the sake of a penalty when it is left to compel the heir to do or not to do something, not so that the legacy should take effect; for example, in this form: "If you marry your daughter to Titius, give ten thousand to Seius."

units.la: 18 Incertæ personæ legari {b} non {†} potest:vel-uti, Quicunque filio meo filiam suam in matrimonio conlocauerit, ei hominí tot millia dato. Sub certa tamen demonstratione incertæ legari potest, vel-ut, Ex cognatis meis qui nunc sunt, qui primo ad funus meum venerit, ei hers meus illud dato.
units.tr: 18 A legacy cannot be made to an uncertain person, as in: "Whoever marries his daughter to my son, give that man so many thousand." Yet a legacy can be made to an uncertain person under a certain designation, as in: "To whichever of my kinsmen who now exist comes first to my funeral, let my heir give that."

units.la: 19 Neque ex {f} falsa demonstratione, neque ex falsa caussa {e} legatum infirmatur. Falsa demonstratio est, velut, Titio fundum, quem à Titio emi, do, lego, cum fundus à Titio emptus non sit. Falsa caussa est: velut, Titio, quoniam negotia mea curauit, fundum do, lego, vt negotia eius nunquam Titius curasset.
units.tr: 19 A legacy is not invalidated by a false designation, nor by a false cause. A false designation is, for example: "I give and bequeath to Titius the farm which I bought from Titius," when the farm was not bought from Titius. A false cause is, for example: "To Titius, since he has looked after my affairs, I give and bequeath the farm," when Titius never looked after his affairs.
20 A legacy cannot be made to the legatee himself.

units.la: 21 Legatum ei tantum dari potest, qui extraneus est. Ideoque filio familiæ heredi instituto, vel seruo, neque à patre, neque à domino legari potest.
units.tr: 21 A legacy can be given only to one who is a stranger. Therefore it cannot be left, either by the father or by the master, to a son under power who has been instituted heir, or to a slave.

units.la: 22[?] Heredi à semetipso legari non potest.
units.tr: 22[?] A legacy cannot be made by an heir to himself.

Therefore, etc.: Cuiacius here. x l. 18; l. 34 §11; l. 116 §1 ff. de legat. 1; l. 34 §1 inf. ff. de legat. 2. 23 A legacy can be made, under a condition, to one who is in the power, hand, or mancipium of the instituted heir; but it is required that at the time when the legacy's day falls due, he is not in the heir's power.

units.la: 24 Ei cuius in potestate, manu, mancipiove est heres scriptus, legari non potest.
units.tr: 24 A legacy cannot be made to one in whose power, hand, or mancipium the instituted heir is.

units.la: 25 Sicut singulæ res legari possunt, ita valuerunt quoque summa legari potest: vtputa, Maniuo heres meus cum Titio hereditatem meam partito dividito: quo casu dimidia pars bonorum legata videtur. Potest autem & alia pars, velut tertia vel quarta legari: quæ species Partitio
units.tr: 25 Just as single things can be bequeathed, so too a sum can be bequeathed: for example, "Let my heir divide my inheritance with Titius and Maevius." In that case half of the goods is considered bequeathed. Another part may also be bequeathed, such as a third or a quarter; this kind is called partition.

units.la: 26 Vsusfructus legari potest earum rerum, quarum salua substantia vtendi fruendi potest esse facultas, & tam singularum rerum, quam plurium, id est, pluribus.
units.tr: 26 A usufruct can be bequeathed of those things whose substance being preserved allows the power of using and enjoying them, both of single things and of several, that is, to several persons.

units.la: 27 Senatusconsulto cautum est, vt etiamsi ea rerum, quæ in abusu continentur, vt puta vini, olei, tritici, vsu fructus legatus sit, legatario res tradantur cautionibus interpositis, de restituendis eis, cum vsufructus ad legatarium pertinere desie-rit.
units.tr: 27 By senatus consultum it is provided that, even when the usufruct is of things which are consumed by use, such as wine, oil, or wheat, the things may be handed over to the legatee, with securities given for their restitution when the usufruct ceases to belong to the legatee.

units.la: 28 Ciuitatibus omnibus, quæ sub imperio Prætoriani sunt, legari potest, idque a Diuo Nerua introductum, postea a Senatu, autore Adriano Pio dixi ad l. 164. §.1. ff. de verborum signif.
units.tr: 28 A legacy can be made to all cities which are under the rule of the Praetorians; this was introduced by the deified Nerva, and afterwards confirmed by the Senate on the authority of Hadrian Pius. Said on l. 164 §1 ff. de verborum significatione.

units.la: 29 Legatum quod datum est, adimi potest, vel eodem testamento, vel co[dicillis] testamento confirmatis: dum tamen eodem modo adimatur, quo modo datum est.
units.tr: 29 A legacy which has been given can be revoked, either in the same will or in codicils confirmed by the will, provided it is revoked in the same way in which it was given.

units.la: 30 Ad heredem legatarij legata non aliter transeunt, nisi si iam dies legatorum ceciderit, legatarius decesserit.
units.tr: 30 Legacies do not pass to the heir of a legatee unless the day of the legacies has already fallen due and the legatee has died.
